sections.heading: Starting with an ESS private tutor or home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Have three things ready before you message. The student's year, school and examination session. A photograph of the most recent marked ESS work, comments included. And one or two sentences saying which conversation you are having: catching up, rethinking the subject, or going further than the classroom goes. That last sentence changes the shortlist more than anything else, so it is worth the thirty seconds it takes to write honestly rather than diplomatically.

If a subject change is on the table, make the coordinator appointment before the tutoring call, not after. A tutor can help you work out whether the student is in the wrong subject; only the school can tell you what is actually possible and by when. Going into a tutoring conversation already knowing the deadline turns a vague worry into a decision with a date on it, and families who do this in that order get noticeably better outcomes than families who do it in reverse.

The first session is deliberately unexciting. The tutor reads the marked work with the student rather than at them. They ask the student what they expected the subject to be and what it turned out to be, which is usually the most revealing ten minutes of the whole engagement. They give the student one piece of real course work to attempt, at the level the course actually asks for, so that everyone is looking at evidence rather than at impressions. They set reading. Then they tell you plainly what they think, including if what they think is that the subject fits fine and the student needs to work harder.

After that, the schedule is yours. Most families run one weekly session, in your home or online, and add a second only through the pressure months. Tell us if the slot stops working, if the commute stops holding, or if the fit is wrong, and we change it without making it difficult. faqs.question: My child chose ESS because it sounded like the easy science. What happens now?
faqs.answer: Usually a difficult first set of written answers, followed by a decision. The content load does feel approachable early, and then the course asks for accurate data reading, applied systems diagrams and extended writing judged on how evidence is weighed. That combination catches out students who picked it to protect time for other subjects. The first useful step is four weeks of one-to-one work to find out whether this is a wrong-subject problem or an unprepared-student problem, because they look identical from outside. The second is a conversation with the Diploma Programme coordinator about what the school permits and by when.

faqs.question: Is ESS a better fit for a student who prefers geography to biology?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and this assumption causes real disappointment. The overlap with geography is genuine in that both deal with human and physical systems interacting, but ESS is framed around systems thinking and scientific method rather than around place and process, and it asks for more data handling than many geography-minded students expect. A student who liked geography because of the human stories may find ESS drier; one who liked it because of the systems and the data will probably enjoy ESS more. Ask a tutor who has taught the course to walk your child through both working styles.

faqs.question: Will taking ESS affect university applications for an environmental degree?
faqs.answer: It can, and the only reliable answer comes from the institutions themselves. Entry requirements vary by institution, by country and by individual course, they change between admissions cycles, and some science-facing degrees specify particular subjects at particular levels. We will not tell you what any named university requires, and nobody on a tutoring platform should. Check the published requirements for the specific course in the cycle your child will apply in, and use the school's university counsellor, who sees these decisions every year. Do that before you treat the environmentally named subject as the obvious route into an environmental degree.

faqs.question: Can we still change subject partway through DP1?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the school decides. There is normally a window early in Diploma Programme Year 1, with its length, paperwork and timetable consequences set by the school within the IB's rules and registration deadlines. Ask your coordinator for the latest date in writing today rather than next month, because the options narrow every week. Assume that any coursework already started does not transfer, since work is designed against one subject's requirements and supervision. A late change costs the work already done and compresses the new subject into less time, which is manageable early in DP1 and much less so afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a private tutor come to our home in Kharghar for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the right match is a tutor already living in one of the nearby Navi Mumbai nodes. Kharghar connects easily to Belapur, Nerul, Vashi and Panvel along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, so node-to-node matching holds for a full year. What rarely holds is pulling a tutor across the creek from the island city twice a week for a 7pm slot, even with the Atal Setu; that arrangement usually ends with a request to move the time. Tell us the exact slot you need before we shortlist, and we will tell you honestly whether it is realistic.

faqs.question: Is society or gate approval needed before a private tutor visits in Thane?
faqs.answer: In most gated complexes yes, and it takes one conversation to solve. Societies along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road generally want the resident to pre-approve a visitor through the society application or a standing instruction at the gate. Ask for a recurring weekly entry rather than approving each visit, because a tutor held at the gate loses part of a lesson you are paying for. Some complexes prefer tuition in a common study room rather than a flat, which is workable if it is quiet. Sort this out in the first week, not the fifth.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a private ESS tutor?
faqs.answer: We publish no rates, because one figure would be wrong for most families reading this. IB tuition fees in Mumbai move with the board and level, how scarce the subject is, the tutor's teaching and examining background, session length and frequency, whether lessons are at your home or online, and the travel distance involved. Environmental Systems and Societies is at the scarce end in this city, which affects availability more than price. Ask each shortlisted tutor directly, compare on a per-hour basis, and check whether written feedback between sessions is included or charged separately.

faqs.question: How is a private tutor different from a group class for this subject?
faqs.answer: The difference matters more in ESS than in most subjects. A group class teaches to an average confusion; this course produces very specific confusions, and the student who cannot read a figure needs something different from the student who writes fluent unevaluated prose. One-to-one also allows the tutor to look across the student's whole timetable and see where the real pressure is, and to have a frank subject-fit conversation that would be impossible in front of other students. It costs more per hour. For a scarce, writing-heavy, judgement-based subject it is usually worth the difference.

faqs.question: Who decides how Environmental Systems and Societies counts in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The school, within the International Baccalaureate's rules, and you should get the answer from the Diploma Programme coordinator in writing. How the subject is placed within a particular student's six subjects, and which levels a campus offers, are determinations made there rather than things a tutoring platform can tell you, and the rules are revised on the IB's own cycle. Ask before making any decision that depends on it, including a subject change. A tutor can help your child do well in the course once the school has confirmed how it sits in their programme.

faqs.question: My child writes well but is weak with numbers. Is ESS a reasonable choice?
faqs.answer: It can be, with eyes open. The arithmetic in this course is not advanced, but it is present: percentage change, rates, efficiencies and straightforward calculations around flows. A strong writer who avoids numbers tends to leave those questions blank, which is the most expensive single habit in the subject because those marks are among the most reliably earned. Four weeks of targeted practice usually breaks the habit. If the student is willing to attempt the numbers rather than route around them, their writing strength becomes a real advantage in the extended questions.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help us choose between ESS and Biology before DP1 begins?
faqs.answer: A tutor can describe honestly what each course demands and how different working styles fare in them, which is genuinely useful. What a tutor cannot do is tell you how either subject would count in your child's Diploma, whether your campus offers the levels you want, or what a university will require, and a tutor who offers opinions on those should be treated with caution. Combine the tutor's view of the working style with the coordinator's view of the structure and the university counsellor's view of the destination. Those three together give you a decision; any one alone does not.

faqs.question: What can a private tutor realistically change about a subject-choice mistake?
faqs.answer: A good deal, and not everything. One-to-one work can usually fix the gap between what the student expected and what the course asks: data reading, applied systems work, writing that weighs evidence, and the belief that the subject needs no effort. It cannot manufacture interest in a subject a student has genuinely decided against, it cannot recover a term of missed content in a fortnight, and we do not guarantee grades. Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade or predicts an outcome before meeting your child, particularly in a conversation about whether to stay with a subject.

sections.heading: What happens when you ask for an IB DP Environmental Systems and Societies tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Requests for this subject arrive late in the year more often than requests for anything else. Almost nobody books in June of DP1. They book after a first mock paper comes back lower than the student expected, or after a teacher's comment on an investigation draft that nobody in the family knows how to act on. The sentence we hear most is some version of: she is perfectly fine in Biology, she is losing marks here, and nobody can tell us exactly why. That is a solvable problem, but it is not solved by more content revision, which is what most families try first and what wastes the most time.

So the sequence is built to find the actual fault before anybody books a term. 1. You send a written intake: year group, level, school, and the last three pieces of feedback the student received in the subject. 2. You send one piece of marked work, ideally a data question and an extended answer rather than a test score, because a score tells us nothing about which skill broke. 3. We match on two separate axes, scientific fluency and written argument, which are the two halves of this course and are rarely strong in the same student. 4. You get a shortlist in writing with each tutor's disciplinary background, level experience, availability and realistic travel radius. 5. One diagnostic session happens before any standing weekly slot is agreed.

That third step is worth explaining because it is where an IB DP Environmental Systems and Societies tutor in Mumbai is genuinely different from a Physics or Economics match. Teachers come into this subject from two directions. A Biology-trained or Environmental Science-trained tutor is usually excellent on the ecology, the productivity concepts and the numerical work, and can be thinner on the extended writing where a student has to set out competing value positions. A Geography-trained tutor is often the reverse: confident with the human and social half, less quick with the calculation and the diagram conventions. Neither background is better. The useful question is which half your child is losing marks in, and then matching to that gap rather than to a label.

What does not happen: no block of sessions sold before a tutor and student have met, no promise about a grade, and no match made purely on who lives closest. A tutor thirty-five minutes away who has run this course through two full cohorts is worth more than a general science tutor in the next building, up to the point where travel starts cancelling sessions. That crossover point is different on JVLR than it is on Palm Beach Road, which is why travel radius is written down rather than assumed.

sections.heading: How does Environmental Systems and Societies count towards a Mumbai student's Diploma?
paragraphs: Environmental Systems and Societies (ESS) is a two-year Diploma Programme (DP) course, deliberately interdisciplinary, built on both scientific method and social analysis. It can satisfy more than one subject group in a Diploma. Exactly how it counts for your child is the school's and the International Baccalaureate's determination, so confirm it with the Diploma Programme coordinator.

That hedge is not us being careful for the sake of it. Parents are routinely told by other parents that ESS does double duty, and then build an entire six-subject plan on a second-hand sentence. Whether a particular arrangement is available to a particular student depends on the rest of the six, the Higher Level and Standard Level mix, the school's option blocks, its staffing, and the IB's own rules as they currently stand. A combination approved for one student in one school is not a precedent for another. If any part of your child's subject plan depends on ESS counting a specific way, that is the first thing to get in writing from the coordinator, before the choice form is submitted rather than after.

Level availability is the other thing to establish early. ESS is offered at Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) where a school runs both, and a number of Mumbai schools run one level only because the cohort does not justify two. There is also the ordinary problem of option blocks: the subject may sit opposite something else your child wants, and no amount of enthusiasm moves a timetable. Ask what level is available, which block it sits in, and what it is opposite. Entry requirements for universities vary by institution and by course and change over time, so check those at each university's own current published source rather than relying on any summary, this page included.

The course connects outward in ways that matter for planning. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) sits naturally alongside it, because the question of when a model is reliable enough to act on is a TOK question wearing a scientific coat. An Extended Essay (EE) in the subject depends on the school having a willing supervisor. Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) often picks up environmental volunteering, which is good for the student and is not assessment, and confusing the two is a common way for a DP1 student to feel busy while the actual coursework slides.

sections.heading: Papers 1 and 2, the systems-and-models approach, and the individual investigation
paragraphs: The written examinations test two different things. Paper 1 works from provided resource material about a situation the student has never seen, and the skill is reading unfamiliar data and text quickly, then applying course concepts to it rather than reciting them. Paper 2 mixes shorter data-based and structured questions with extended writing. The exact format, the order of the papers and how long each one runs are set by the current subject guide, which the IB revises on its own cycle, so take those details from the guide and your teacher and treat any website quoting them, this one included, as out of date by default.

The systems-and-models approach is the spine of the course and the thing most often taught too lightly. A system is described by its storages and its flows, with transfers moving material or energy without changing its form and transformations changing it. Students must be able to draw a system, not describe one in prose: storages as labelled boxes, flows as labelled arrows, arrow width indicating relative size, and a system boundary actually drawn on the page. Feedback is a graded concept, and the direction of it trips people constantly, because negative feedback stabilises and positive feedback amplifies, which is the opposite of how the words sound in ordinary English. Take a pond a student already knows, map its inputs, its outputs, what is stored in it and what moves between the stores, and the abstraction stops being abstract. Models are then taught with their limits attached: every model leaves something out, and naming what a model omits is a mark-scoring move, not a criticism of the model.

The quantitative work is where the easy-science belief dies. Students are asked to calculate percentage change and rates, convert between units without being reminded to, read a graph with an awkward axis, work with means and ranges, handle a diversity index, and reason about productivity. None of it is Higher Level Maths. All of it is unforgiving if the student has spent two years rounding at the wrong point or dropping units. The harder skill sits one step beyond the arithmetic: given two sets of field measurements that differ, saying whether the difference means anything at all, given how variable the measurements were in the first place. A student who reports a difference without discussing variability has answered half the question.

Command terms decide the shape of an answer before any content goes in. Identify and outline want much less than explain, and explain wants much less than evaluate or discuss. The individual investigation, which is the internal assessment, is developed by the student during the course with their teacher's supervision, and any fieldwork is arranged and supervised by the school. No tutor arranges a site visit, and no student should be collecting data at a site nobody is supervising. A tutor may teach the method, work through other people's examples, and comment on the student's own draft. A tutor may never write, redraft or supply any part of it.

sections.heading: Mumbai coverage for ESS tutors, zone by zone
paragraphs: IB Gram covers all six zones of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and demand for this subject is heaviest in the Central Suburbs, so that is where to start. The Central Suburbs run along the Central Line from Kurla through Ghatkopar and Kanjurmarg to Mulund West, with the Eastern Express Highway carrying the road traffic and Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in the middle with no station of their own. A tutor reaching Hiranandani Gardens arrives by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and Metro Line 1 from Ghatkopar to Andheri has made that crossing predictable in a way it was not before. The Santacruz Chembur Link Road is the single piece of infrastructure that makes a Chembur to Santacruz booking survive a term. Powai also has the convenient accident of a large lake inside walking distance of several schools, which gives a student in this subject a system they have looked at since they were six.

The Eastern Suburbs are the other concentration. Chembur, Govandi, Mankhurd, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Wadala sit on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Express Highway inland and the Eastern Freeway making the run into South Mumbai from Chembur and Wadala considerably faster than the map implies. The Monorail links Chembur to Wadala for students travelling to a session themselves. Students in Vikhroli and Bhandup live within sight of the Thane creek wetlands, which is the kind of nearby, familiar system that makes the storages-and-flows vocabulary land properly instead of staying on a worksheet. An IB home tutor in Mumbai working this corridor generally keeps to it rather than crossing the city, and the honest reason is traffic, not preference.

South Mumbai is short on distance and long on time. Colaba, Churchgate, Grant Road, Mumbai Central, Worli, Peddar Road, Walkeshwar and Parel are all minutes apart on paper and forty minutes apart at seven in the evening once the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals set in. Metro Line 3 between Cuffe Parade and BKC and the Coastal Road have both changed what is bookable here, and the Harbour Line still carries the CSMT to Dockyard and Sewri stretch. The Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing substantially, and we still match node to node for weekday evenings because an occasional fast crossing is not a schedule. sections.heading: The Mumbai school year that sets ESS deadlines
paragraphs: One date matters more than all the others on this course, and most families do not ask for it until it is too late to be useful: the week of the school's field trip. Any fieldwork for this subject is arranged, risk-assessed and supervised by the school, and Mumbai schools schedule it to avoid the monsoon, which in practice pushes it into the drier months between late in the calendar year and February. Everything downstream is dated from that trip. If the trip lands in January and the school's internal submission deadline is in March, the whole investigation lives inside an eight-week window that already contains mock examinations. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator in DP1 when the trip is likely to fall, and plan the tutoring around it rather than reacting to it.

The rest of the Mumbai IB calendar follows the familiar shape: an academic year opening around June, with the monsoon at the front, and the May examination session closing the second year. DP1 is quieter than it feels. DP2 is a traffic jam, because internal assessments across six subjects tend to bunch between August and October, mocks arrive in January and February, and the Theory of Knowledge essay has its own deadline sitting in the middle of all of it. A DP2 student in Chembur can have an ESS investigation draft due in the same fortnight as a TOK essay and a Chemistry internal assessment. Nothing fixes that except knowing about it in July. Your own school's dates differ from the next school's, so get them in writing at the start of DP2 instead of assuming a common calendar.

Podar International School has Santacruz and Powai campuses, JBCN International School runs Chembur, Parel, Borivali and Oshiwara, and Witty International School has Malad and Chembur. In BKC there are Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Ascend International School and the American School of Bombay. South Mumbai has Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Activity High School on Peddar Road and Gopi Birla Memorial School at Walkeshwar. Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School is in Thane and D.Y. sections.heading: Is home tuition or online tutoring better for ESS in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition wins for the diagram and calculation work, because both happen with a pen on paper and a tutor needs to watch the student's hand hesitate. Online wins on access to a genuine subject specialist and on late slots. Most Mumbai families run both: one in-person session weekly, one short online review midweek.

IB home tuition in Mumbai is the lead service here, and the reason is specific to this course rather than general. Systems diagrams are drawn, redrawn and corrected, and a tutor sitting beside the student sees the pause before the arrow goes in, which is the moment the misunderstanding is visible. Data work is the same: spread three years of figures across a table, give the student a calculator, and watch where the units get dropped. On a screen share you see the finished answer and have to reverse-engineer the error from it. A home tutor also sees the working conditions, and will tell you plainly when the study table facing a television is a bigger problem than anything in the syllabus. For DP1 students, in-person is the faster route to habits that hold.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai answers the problem in-person cannot, which is that this is a small-cohort subject and the person who has actually taught it twice may live on the other side of the creek from you. Online removes travel from the equation and makes a nine o'clock slot possible after a CAS commitment or a late bus back from school. The trade-offs are real and worth naming. Annotation of data tables and diagrams needs a shared document or tablet set up properly before the session rather than during it. A student who drifts drifts faster on a screen. A weak connection in a monsoon week costs you minutes you have paid for. For a self-directed DP2 student working on timing and essay structure, none of that outweighs having the right teacher.

The hybrid is what holds across two years. Weekly Environmental Systems and Societies home classes Mumbai parents can realistically keep, usually weekend mornings or an early evening slot before the corridor fills, plus a twenty-minute online check midweek on one diagram or one paragraph. It keeps the in-person diagnosis and takes four evening commutes a month out of the tutor's week, which is what stops the arrangement quietly dying in November. If you want a home tutor for Environmental Systems and Societies Mumbai families can hold on to through DP2, ask for this shape by name in the first conversation.

sections.heading: Verifying an ESS tutor: the background question that matters most
paragraphs: Checks on IB Gram are unglamorous and that is the point. Government photo identity, documentary proof of the qualification claimed, and a teaching history we can contact. Where a tutor says they have taught this course inside a Diploma Programme school, we ask which school, which years and which levels, and we ask them to describe how they teach a systems diagram, because somebody who has taught it cannot improvise that for three minutes and somebody who has not cannot fake it. Where a tutor claims examining or moderating experience with a board, we record what the role was and for how long, and we tell you clearly when a claim is the tutor's own statement that we have not been able to confirm independently.

Then ask the question that actually predicts fit on this subject: which discipline did you come from, and how do you teach the half you did not train in? A Biology or Environmental Science background usually means strong ecology and strong numerical work. A Geography background usually means strong social analysis and strong extended writing. Both are fine. What you want to hear is a specific answer about the weaker half, not a claim that there is no weaker half. Follow it with two practical tests: ask the tutor to mark one of your child's data questions and explain the marks against the criteria, and ask them to mark one extended answer. A tutor strong at both will show you two different kinds of correction, and an IB private tutor Mumbai parents keep for two years will welcome being asked.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, or who discusses results before reading a single piece of work. Be wary of anyone offering to write, redraft or tidy up part of the individual investigation, which is academic misconduct and puts the student's diploma at risk rather than the tutor's. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor promises a specific grade, because the examination is sat by the student and is not in anybody else's control. A tutor worth keeping will tell you where the student currently is, what is causing the loss of marks, and what a realistic range looks like with consistent work between sessions.

There is one more check specific to this course. Ask the tutor how they handle a topic the student already feels strongly about. The right answer is that they teach the student to set out the evidence and then lay out how people holding different environmental value positions read that same evidence, so the student can do it under examination conditions. The wrong answer is a tutor who hands the student their own view on a disputed question. That is not tutoring and it damages marks, because an examiner is assessing the handling of evidence and competing positions, not the student's conclusions. IB Gram takes no position on contested environmental questions, and a tutor on the platform should not be pushing one either.

sections.heading: Why is Environmental Systems and Societies not the easy science option?
paragraphs: Because it is not one subject with the hard parts removed. It is two methods held together: the scientific one, which demands systems thinking, measurement and calculation, and the social one, which demands that a student weigh evidence alongside competing environmental value positions without substituting an opinion for either. Students expecting a lighter science meet both at once.

The misconception has an understandable source. The subject has no laboratory-heavy reputation, the content sounds like general knowledge, and the title contains the word societies, which reads as soft to a sixteen-year-old choosing in a hurry. Then the course starts. Week by week it asks for storages and flows drawn to convention, feedback loops identified by direction, percentage change computed correctly and interpreted against variability, productivity reasoned about rather than recalled, models evaluated by what they leave out, and written answers that hold scientific evidence and human value positions in the same paragraph without collapsing into either. Nothing there is beyond a capable student. All of it is beyond a student who selected the subject on the assumption that it would not ask for work.

The single biggest mark-loser is the student who writes about the environment well and scores averagely. Their answers are fluent, committed and full of conviction, and they score in the middle because conviction is not what is being assessed. The course teaches environmental value systems as an analytical tool: broadly, positions that place intrinsic value on nature, positions that evaluate the environment through human need, and positions that trust technological solution. The examiner wants to see a student apply that framework to evidence. A weak answer on a disputed question says what the student believes should happen. A strong answer states what the evidence shows and what its limitations are, then explains how a reader starting from each of those value positions would interpret it differently, and why those readers can disagree while looking at the same data. The student's own view is neither required nor penalised. It is simply not the question. This is why a tutor who argues their own position with your child is doing harm, however well-informed they are, and why nothing on this page takes a side on any contested environmental question, names any company, government or campaign as a case, or tells you what the right policy is.

What a tutor diagnoses first, in order, and it is almost always the same order. One, the numerical work, because it is the fastest thing to fix and the easiest to measure: units, rounding, percentage change, reading an awkward axis. Two, the diagrams, because conventions can be taught in a fortnight and are worth marks immediately. Three, command term discipline, because an evaluate answer written as a description loses marks the student already earned the knowledge for. Four, the value-systems writing, which is the slowest to build and takes most of a term. Alongside all of that, one planning conversation: how this subject counts within your child's Diploma is a matter for the school and the IB, so have the coordinator confirm it in writing rather than carrying a second-hand version of it into DP2.

sections.heading: What should change after four sessions with a Mumbai ESS tutor?
paragraphs: The numerical work and the diagrams should be visibly better, and the extended writing should not be yet. Four sessions is enough to fix units, rounding, percentage change and diagram conventions. Rebuilding how a student constructs an argument about competing value positions takes most of a term, and anybody promising otherwise is selling.

Measure it on paper rather than on mood. Put a data question from week one next to one from week four: units present, working shown, the answer interpreted rather than just stated. Put a systems diagram from week one next to week four: labelled storages, labelled flows, a boundary drawn, feedback identified with the correct direction. Those are binary and you can see them without understanding the subject. By one term, the student should be planning an extended answer without the tutor in the room and should be naming the limitations of a model unprompted. By one full mock cycle you learn the thing that actually matters, which is whether any of it survives a clock, because writing well with ninety minutes and writing well with an examiner's time limit are different skills.

The honest limits. A tutor cannot sit the paper, cannot move a school deadline, and cannot make a student read a resource booklet carefully who has decided to skim it. An IB DP Environmental Systems and Societies tutor in Mumbai starting with a DP2 student six weeks before finals is triaging: picking the two changes that move the most marks, probably the calculation discipline and the command terms, and deliberately abandoning the rest. That is a reasonable thing to buy and a bad thing to plan for. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and the difference between a student who does the work between sessions and one who does not is larger than the difference between any two tutors on the platform.

If it is going wrong, say so in week three. The three common failures are a tutor teaching content when the fault is in the writing, a disciplinary mismatch where the tutor's weaker half is your child's weaker half, and a slot neither side can keep because the corridor was optimistic. All three are fixable and none of them require an awkward conversation with the tutor. Tell us what specifically is not working, and a different tutor is put in front of you without you restarting the search or explaining yourself to anyone. Replacing a tutor in week four costs a week. Replacing one in week fourteen costs a term.

sections.heading: Your first home classes: a diagnostic built around marked work
paragraphs: Bring four things to the first of the home classes and the session pays for itself. The last marked data question with the teacher's annotations on it. The last extended written answer, marked. The school's internal deadline calendar for the term, including the field trip week if it is known. And one sentence from the student about what they find hardest, in their own words. A student who says 'I can do the maths but I never know what to write in the long answers' has given the tutor a diagnosis that no report card contains.

Expect the first session to be mostly reading and questions. The tutor should work through the marked data question with the student talking, draw one systems diagram together from a situation the student already knows rather than a textbook one, test a single command term in practice, and look at where the individual investigation stands if DP2 has begun. At the end they should say out loud, with the student present, what the two priorities for the next month are and what you should be able to see by week five. If they cannot name two priorities after ninety minutes, that is information too.

Fix the practical things in the same conversation so nobody renegotiates them in November. Choose a weekly slot the corridor can actually support rather than the one that suits the calendar. Register the tutor with the building office so entry stops being a weekly discussion at the gate. Pick the spot in the flat where sessions happen and keep it clear of phones. Agree what happens when travel fails, which in this city it will. Then review at four weeks against what was said at session one, on paper, not from memory.

faqs.question: What does an ESS tutor in Mumbai charge, and what changes the rate?
faqs.answer: Rates are set by the individual tutor, not by IB Gram, and we deliberately publish no price list because one figure would mislead most readers. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board and level, how scarce the subject specialism is, the distance and time of day the tutor travels, the session length, and whether you book one subject or several. This subject has a small pool of genuine specialists, so a tutor who has run the course through two cohorts typically quotes above a general science tutor. Get the per-session rate and the travel expectation in writing before the first standing slot.

faqs.question: Will an evening home tutor slot work if we live on Ghodbunder Road?
faqs.answer: It works if the tutor is already on the Thane side, and it rarely works otherwise. Ghodbunder Road takes about twenty minutes from Thane station to Kasarvadavali off-peak and close to an hour at the evening peak, so a 7pm slot is comfortable for a home tutor living in Majiwada or near Pokhran Road and unreliable for one coming from Mulund or Powai. We ask tutors for the radius they will actually honour in traffic rather than the one they would like. If no specialist sits inside it, we say so and propose online rather than booking something that fails in week four.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get a gate pass for weekly sessions in our Powai building?
faqs.answer: Yes, and setting it up once at the start of term is the whole trick. Most Powai and Chandivali towers want the tutor's name and number on a standing visitor list, photo identity shown at the gate, and a resident's approval for repeat entry, with some running app-based or QR approval for every single visit. Do that in week one and the gate stops costing ten minutes a session. If your building restricts recurring visitors altogether, ask whether the clubhouse study room can be booked, and tell us, because that changes which tutors we can realistically offer you.

faqs.question: Is ESS really easier than Biology or Geography?
faqs.answer: No, it is different, and treating it as easier is the most expensive assumption a student can make in this subject. It carries less laboratory work than Biology, which is where the reputation comes from, and replaces that with systems thinking, quantitative handling of messy field data, and extended writing that has to hold scientific evidence and competing environmental value positions in the same answer. A student who is strong in Biology but writes weak essays will find this harder than Biology. A strong essay writer who drops units will find it harder than Geography. Choose it for interest, not for workload.

faqs.question: My child writes passionately about the environment but gets average marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the examination assesses how evidence and competing positions are handled, not what the student concludes. Fluent, committed writing scores in the middle when it argues a view instead of analysing one. The fix is mechanical and teachable: state what the evidence shows, state its limitations, then explain how readers holding different environmental value positions would interpret that same evidence differently and why they can reasonably disagree. The student's own opinion is neither required nor penalised. Most students who make this switch see the difference inside a month, because the knowledge was already there.

faqs.question: How do we know whether ESS will count the way we were told in our child's Diploma?
faqs.answer: Only by asking the Diploma Programme coordinator at your child's school and getting the answer in writing. The subject is interdisciplinary and can satisfy more than one subject group, but whether a specific arrangement is open to a specific student is determined by the school and by the International Baccalaureate, taking account of the other five subjects, the level mix and the timetable. Another family's experience is not a precedent, and neither is anything on a website. If your subject plan depends on it counting a particular way, verify that before the choice form goes in.

faqs.question: Does a tutor arrange the fieldwork trip or site visit?
faqs.answer: No. Fieldwork for this subject is arranged, risk-assessed and supervised by the school, and that is not a formality we are passing on politely. A tutor never organises a site visit, never accompanies a student to one, and should never suggest a student go and collect measurements somewhere nobody is supervising. What a tutor can properly do is prepare the student beforehand, so that they arrive knowing what they are measuring and why, and work with whatever data the supervised trip produced afterwards. If a tutor proposes an independent outing, tell us.

faqs.question: How much maths does Environmental Systems and Societies need?
faqs.answer: Less than Physics and more than most students expect when they choose it. The arithmetic itself is ordinary: percentage change, rates, unit conversion, means and ranges, reading graphs with uncooperative axes, a diversity index, reasoning about productivity. What catches students is that none of it is flagged in the question, so a student who has quietly been rounding at the wrong point or dropping units for two years loses marks steadily without knowing why. This is the quickest part of the course to repair with a tutor, usually inside three or four sessions, which is why it is diagnosed first.

faqs.question: Our tutor keeps telling our child what to think about environmental issues. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is not acceptable and it costs marks. A tutor's job on contested questions is to teach the student to lay out evidence and then show how people holding different environmental value positions read that evidence differently. Handing a student a conclusion removes exactly the skill the examiner is looking for, and it leaves the student unable to write the other side of an argument under timed conditions. Raise it with us. IB Gram takes no position on disputed environmental questions, and a tutor on the platform should not be advancing one in a student's session.

faqs.question: Does travel across the Eastern Express Highway make a weekday session unrealistic?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the direction and the hour. North to south along the Eastern Express Highway between Mulund, Bhandup, Vikhroli and Chembur is manageable at most times, and a 7pm booking in that corridor usually holds. Crossing west to east, Andheri or Santacruz to Chembur, is a different proposition, and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road is what makes it possible at all. The Eastern Freeway makes Chembur to South Mumbai far quicker than the map suggests. We match along the corridor rather than across it, and say so before you commit.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is strong on the science but weak on the essays?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week three, because it is the most common mismatch on this subject and it has a straightforward fix. Teachers arrive at this course from Biology, Environmental Science or Geography, and almost nobody is equally fluent in the numerical half and the extended-writing half. If your child's gap is the writing and the tutor's strength is the data, you have two people working on the wrong problem politely. We will put a different tutor in front of you without restarting the search, and some families run two tutors briefly, one per half, until the weaker side catches up.

faqs.question: Do you work with students at Hiranandani Foundation School or NES International School?
faqs.answer: Families from both book tutors through IB Gram, as do families from Oberoi International School, JBCN International School, Dhirubhai Ambani International School and many others. sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an Extended Essay (EE) tutor in Mumbai to the writing phase
paragraphs: A request for IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai produces a shortlist of two or three tutors from the subject group the essay is registered in, not a general writing coach. We ask four things before we shortlist anybody: the registered subject, the research question in the words the student is currently using, the last comment the supervisor made, and the school's internal draft deadline. Those four answers decide the match more than anything else a parent can tell us.

The registered subject matters far more than most parents expect. An Extended Essay in History is read for the handling of sources and the weighing of competing interpretations. One in Biology is read for method, data handling and the honesty of the evaluation. One in English is read for the quality of the reading of the text itself. A tutor who is confident about essay structure in general but has never worked through an Economics Extended Essay will give advice that sounds entirely sensible and scores nothing, because the criteria reward subject-specific reasoning rather than tidy paragraphs. We filter on the subject group first and treat writing craft as the second filter, never the first.

Most parents reach us having already typed "best IB tutor in Mumbai" or "IB tutors near me Mumbai" into Google, which is a sensible place to start and a poor place to finish, because neither phrase tells a search engine which subject group the essay is registered in. The second question is where the student actually stands. "Has a question and cannot start" is a different brief from "has eleven pages of notes and no argument", which is different again from "has an overlong draft and three weeks left". Each of those needs a different first session, and a tutor who is good at the third is not automatically good at the first. The third question is domestic: which suburb, which evenings are genuinely free once school and sport are accounted for, whether the study table is shared with a younger sibling, and whether your building wants a visitor pass arranged ahead of a standing weekly slot.

There is one kind of request we turn down at this stage. If the message is "can someone write the conclusion" or "can someone sort the draft out before Friday", we say no on the call and explain why. A tutor may teach a skill, press on a draft with questions, and mark that draft against the published criteria. A tutor may never write, redraft, research for, supply data for, or produce any part of an Extended Essay or an Internal Assessment. The student signs the work as their own, so the work has to be theirs.

sections.heading: Where the Extended Essay sits in the IB Diploma Programme (DP) in Mumbai
paragraphs: The Extended Essay (EE) is the independent research essay every candidate in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) writes, and it sits in the DP core alongside Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity and service requirement. We deliberately do not quote how the core converts into points, how long the essay may run, or how many supervisor meetings are required, because the IB revises its guides on its own cycle and the only rules that matter are the ones in the guide your child is registered under. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator has that document and will give you the current version in a two-minute conversation.

What we can describe is the shape of the two years as Mumbai families actually experience it. The subject is chosen and the question drafted in DP1, usually after the school runs an introductory session on what research at this level means. The research and the first full draft land across the long gap between DP1 ending and DP2 beginning. The redrafting, the reflections and the final submission fall in DP2, in the same months as the heaviest Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines. A student who leaves the essay until DP2 has not left themselves a hard job; they have left themselves three hard jobs stacked on one calendar.

The supervisor is appointed by the school, and so is the subject teacher. That is not a formality we are being polite about. The supervisor is the only person whose comments count inside the school's process, the only person who signs off on the authenticity of the work, and the only person who can tell a student what their own school expects at each internal checkpoint. A tutor working alongside that relationship never replaces it, never overrides it and never contacts the school. If a tutor's advice and the supervisor's advice disagree, the supervisor wins and the tutor's job is to help the student understand why.

The essay may be registered in a subject the student takes at Higher Level (HL) or at Standard Level (SL), and it may be registered in a subject with constraints a student has not noticed. That is a question for the coordinator rather than for us, and it is worth asking early, because changing the registered subject late is the single most expensive change a candidate can make.
bullets: The Extended Essay sits in the DP core with Theory of Knowledge (TOK)
Subject and question in DP1; redrafting and reflections land in DP2
The school appoints the supervisor and signs off authenticity, not a tutor
Ask the DP coordinator for the current guide instead of trusting any website
Changing the registered subject late is the costliest possible change

sections.heading: Subject choice, the research question and what the criteria actually reward
paragraphs: Three decisions set the ceiling on an Extended Essay before a single paragraph is written: which subject it is registered in, how narrow the question is, and whether the student can get at the material the question demands. A question about a famous equity market crash sounds exciting until the student discovers the data series they need sits behind a subscription. A question about a local Mumbai manufacturer sounds modest until it turns out the student can obtain real figures and ask real questions, at which point it outperforms the exciting one comfortably.

The criteria are published, they are named in the current guide, and they are the only standard that matters. Broadly they reward a focused question with a method suited to it, genuine subject knowledge used rather than displayed, critical thinking applied to the student's own evidence, presentation that lets a reader follow the argument, and honest engagement with how the work actually went. We teach students to read those criteria as instructions rather than as a rubric to be shown at the end, because almost every weak draft we see is a draft written to a topic rather than to a criterion.

The reflections on planning and progress are part of the assessment, not paperwork attached to it. They are written by the student, in the student's voice, about what they actually tried, abandoned and changed. A reflection that says "I learned a lot about time management" is wasted space. One that says "the first two sources agreed so completely that I went looking for a third that did not, and the third changed the structure of section two" does real work, because it shows a mind in motion. A tutor who drafts those sentences has manufactured an authenticity problem rather than solved one.

Marking a student's own draft is the most useful thing a session can do, and it is also where the boundary is clearest. The student brings the draft. The tutor asks what criterion each section is trying to satisfy, points at the paragraph where the argument stops advancing, and explains which band the draft currently sits in and why. The tutor does not rewrite the paragraph, supply the missing analysis, or hand over a corrected version. The student goes away and writes the next draft, which is the only version anybody is interested in.
bullets: Narrow questions with reachable material beat ambitious questions with none
Read the published criteria as instructions before drafting, not after
Reflections are assessed: the student's own voice, actual changes, no ghosting
A tutor names the band and the reason; the student writes the next draft
Subject knowledge has to be used in the argument, not displayed beside it

paragraphs: We match tutors for IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai across all six zones of the city, and we match within a zone wherever we can, because a tutor who can reach you in twenty minutes keeps a weekly slot for a full term and a tutor crossing the city does not. In the Western Suburbs, which carry the largest share of DP candidates in Mumbai, Maharashtra, we place tutors along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway rather than across them: Bandra to Khar West to Santacruz works, Juhu to Andheri works, Malad to Kandivali to Borivali works, and Dahisar sits comfortably on Metro Lines 2A and 7. Goregaon East off the JVLR is its own pocket, reached by road rather than by rail.

South Mumbai is short-distance and slow. A tutor moving from Worli to Colaba covers a handful of kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening, so we match inside the island rather than pulling somebody down from the suburbs. Cuffe Parade, Fort, Walkeshwar, Babulnath and Tardeo are all served by island-based tutors; the Coastal Road has changed the Worli and Nariman Point run noticeably, and Metro Line 3 has changed the Cuffe Parade to Bandra Kurla Complex trip more than the map suggests.

In the Central Suburbs we cover Powai, Chandivali, Kurla, Kanjurmarg and Ghatkopar, with Powai as the awkward case: it is physically central and has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Ghatkopar or Kanjurmarg over the JVLR, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road matters to anybody crossing from the Western side. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup up to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway, and the Eastern Freeway makes Wadala and Chembur far closer to the island than they look.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so we match node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short run from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and the Atal Setu has shortened the island crossing without making a weekday evening commute from South Mumbai realistic for a full term. In Thane, the Ghodbunder Road stretch sets the schedule: a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so we place Thane tutors in Thane, across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Hiranandani Estate, with Mulund tutors crossing over only when the slot is late enough to clear the worst of it.

sections.heading: How do Mumbai school EE deadlines land across DP1 and DP2?
paragraphs: Mumbai schools set their own internal Extended Essay checkpoints well ahead of the external submission, which is why two students in the same building can be under completely different pressure in the same week. Most schools here want a question signed off before the long break at the end of DP1, a full first draft early in DP2, and a final version weeks before anything is actually sent anywhere. The internal deadline is the one that governs your household calendar, and it is the one parents most often do not know.

Families we work with attend schools including Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in Bandra Kurla Complex, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off the JVLR in Goregaon East, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, B.D. Somani International School at Cuffe Parade, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, the JBCN International School campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. Naming a school here is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, nor with the International Baccalaureate organisation.

The collision that catches DP2 families is not the Extended Essay on its own. It is the fortnight where an Extended Essay redraft, two Internal Assessment deadlines and a mock paper land together, often in the same month as a TOK exhibition or essay. A student in Chembur with a Physics IA draft due the same week as her Extended Essay redraft does not have a motivation problem; she has a sequencing problem, and the fix is deciding which one gets the good hours and which one gets the leftovers.

That is the argument for starting during DP1 rather than in the panic window. The students who finish calmly are almost always the ones whose question was settled and whose reading was done before DP2 began, which leaves DP2 for the work that actually earns marks: redrafting, cutting and sharpening. Ask your school for its internal checkpoint dates in writing and put them on the same calendar as the IA deadlines, because seeing the stack is what changes behaviour.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for the Extended Essay writing phase?
paragraphs: Home tuition is what most Mumbai families book for this work and it is what we lead with. The Extended Essay (EE) home classes Mumbai parents ask for are almost always a single protected weekly sitting at the student's own desk rather than a course of lessons. IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai means a tutor at your dining table with the student's draft printed out, pens on the page, and the criteria open beside it. For the writing phase specifically this is the strongest format, because the session is built on reading the student's own sentences slowly and asking what each one is doing. That is hard to do well over a screen share, and it is much harder to fake: a parent in the next room hears whether a session is teaching or dictating.

Online suits a narrow set of situations genuinely well. An IB online tutor in Mumbai is the better answer when the registered subject is unusual enough that the right specialist lives in a different zone, when the student is at a boarding school or travelling, or when the slot that actually works is early on a Sunday. Screen-shared drafts with tracked comments are fine for structural feedback, and recorded sessions help a student who needs to hear the same point twice. The honest trade-off is attention: a seventeen-year-old with a phone beside the laptop at nine in the evening is not fully in the room.

Hybrid is what most of our Extended Essay placements settle into by DP2. One home session a week for the hard, slow work of reading and marking a draft, plus a short online check-in mid-week to confirm the student actually wrote the thing they said they would write. Hybrid also absorbs the Mumbai problem that no scheduling cleverness fixes: monsoon weeks, exam weeks, and the evenings when Ghodbunder Road or the Western Express Highway simply does not move. The session happens online instead of not happening.

Whichever mode you choose, the boundary does not move with it. Online or at your table, a tutor teaches technique, questions a draft and marks it against the published criteria. A tutor does not write sentences into the document, does not research the topic on the student's behalf, does not supply data, and does not produce any part of the submission. If a tutor offers to "just tidy it up" in a shared document, that is the point to stop the engagement and tell us.
bullets: Home tuition suits the writing phase: printed draft, criteria open, slow reading
Online fits scarce subjects, travel, boarding school and early weekend slots
Hybrid is common in DP2: one home session plus a mid-week online check
Online sessions lose attention more than they lose content

sections.heading: How are IB home tutors in Mumbai checked before they reach your door?
paragraphs: Before a tutor appears on a shortlist for IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai we confirm identity with government photo identification, we confirm the subject claim with degree documents or examiner or teaching evidence in that subject, and we take references we can actually call rather than a line in a profile. For Extended Essay work we also ask something more specific: which subjects they have supervised or marked research writing in, and what they tell a student who asks them to fix a draft. The second answer is more informative than the first.

What we check is not everything a parent should check. Ask the tutor directly, in the first session and in front of your child, what they will not do. The answer you want is plain: they will not write, redraft, research for or supply data for the essay, and they will not touch the document. A tutor who hesitates, or who answers with something about "guiding the writing", has told you what you need to know. A tutor who says it cleanly has just made your child's authenticity declaration easier to sign honestly.

Those two questions are the whole difference between an IB home tutor in Mumbai who is useful and one who is a risk, and they cost nothing to ask. The other checks are practical. Ask how the tutor will record what happened in each session, because a short written note after each sitting is the record that protects everybody if the school ever asks how the essay was produced. Ask whether they are willing for you to keep every dated draft in one folder. Ask whether they expect to contact the school, and expect the answer to be no, because the supervisor relationship belongs to the school and a tutor inserting themselves into it causes problems rather than solving them.

Be wary of anybody who promises a specific grade, offers a sample essay "to work from", or quotes a package price for an outcome rather than for sessions. Those three signals travel together. An honest Extended Essay tutor will tell you plainly that the result depends on what the student does between sessions, and will be comfortable with you sitting in on a session to see how it runs.
bullets: Identity, subject-specific qualification evidence and callable references verified
Ask the tutor in session one, out loud, what they will refuse to do
Keep every dated draft in one folder and a short note per session

sections.heading: Writing at length: one argument instead of ten separate sections
paragraphs: The hardest part of the Extended Essay is not producing enough words. It is making one argument hold across the whole length of the piece. Most first drafts that reach us are sequences of competent sections, each answering a slightly different question, so the essay reads as a set of short essays sharing a title page. The reader is looking for a line of reasoning that starts in the opening paragraph and is still being pushed forward on the last page. Stamina produces length. Structure produces marks, and the two are not the same problem.

The test we teach is applied one paragraph at a time, out loud. What does this paragraph do for the argument that the previous paragraph did not already do? If the only honest answer is "it says more about the topic", the paragraph is description, and description is where marks quietly disappear. A student in Khar West writing on wartime propaganda can describe twelve posters and score below a student who analyses three, because the third one complicates the pattern the first two suggested, and showing that complication is the thinking the criteria reward.

We teach the introduction written last. It is the one section that has to promise precisely what the essay delivers, and nobody knows what the essay delivers until it exists. Signposting earns marks only when it is honest and specific: "this section tests the first explanation against the second data set" is a signpost, while "now we will look at some other factors" is filler that costs space. The conclusion has to answer the question actually printed on the title page, including answering it partially, or with a qualification, if that is where the evidence landed. A conclusion that quietly answers an easier question is the most common way a strong draft loses marks late.

Editing down an overlong draft is a real skill and it belongs to the student. A tutor can show how to spot the paragraph that repeats an earlier one in new clothes, how to compress three sentences of setup into a single clause, and where a long block quotation should become a short quotation plus a sentence of analysis. The tutor demonstrates the move on a different passage, and the student makes the cuts in their own document. That division is not a technicality. It is the difference between a student who can explain every decision in the essay when asked and a student who cannot, and being able to explain every decision is the best protection a candidate has.
bullets: Read each paragraph aloud and name what it adds that the last one did not
Write the introduction last, once the essay's real claim has settled
Signpost with the specific test the next section runs, never with filler
Cut repetition and setup before cutting evidence when a draft runs long
The tutor demonstrates a cut elsewhere; the student cuts their own document

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and submission
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a better draft. You should expect a sharper question, a plan the student can say out loud without reading it, and a visible change in how they talk about their own work. The clearest early signal is the student using the language of the criteria unprompted, saying "this bit is description" about their own paragraph. If after four weeks the student still cannot explain what their essay argues in two sentences, something is wrong with the match and we would rather hear from you then than in month three.

At one term the draft should be doing structural work: an argument that runs end to end, sections that each advance it, evidence used rather than listed, and a student who knows which parts are weak. Expect the draft to be too long at this stage, because a draft that is already the right length after one term is usually a draft that has not explored enough. By the end of a term the reflections should be accumulating as the student goes, written at the time, rather than being reconstructed from memory the week before submission.

By submission the honest measure is simple: can the student explain every decision in the essay, in their own words, without the tutor in the room? If yes, the work is theirs and the process was sound, whatever the eventual mark. We do not guarantee grades and nobody honestly can, because the result depends on the student's reading, their writing between sessions and an external process none of us controls. What a good tutor changes is the quality of the thinking the student brings to the page, and that is worth paying for on its own terms.

When a match is not working, tell us early and tell us specifically: the student has stopped preparing, the sessions have become the tutor talking, or the feedback is vague. We re-shortlist from the same subject group and hand over the session notes so the new tutor does not start from zero. The one thing we will not do is keep a placement alive because the calendar is tight. If a tutor has begun drifting towards writing or correcting the draft directly, that placement ends immediately, whatever month it is.
bullets: Four weeks: a sharper question and criteria language used unprompted
One term: an argument running end to end, and a deliberately overlong draft
Reflections written as the work happens, not reconstructed at the end
We do not guarantee grades; the student's work between sessions decides most of it
Vague feedback or a tutor touching the draft ends the placement at once

sections.heading: Starting IB DP Extended Essay home tuition in Mumbai this term
paragraphs: To get a shortlist that is actually useful, send four things: the registered subject, the research question as it currently reads, the school's next internal deadline, and your suburb with the evenings that are genuinely free. If the student has a draft, send its length and nothing else about it; we do not want the document and a tutor will read it with the student rather than before them. If there is no draft, say what exists instead, whether that is a reading list, a page of notes or an empty file. Say also whether you want an IB private tutor Mumbai side of the creek or across it, because a home tutor for Extended Essay (EE) Mumbai families book in Vashi is a different shortlist from one in Worli.

The first session is diagnostic and it is deliberately uncomfortable. The student explains the question in their own words, says what they think the essay will argue, and reads one paragraph of whatever they have written aloud. The tutor maps that against the published criteria and names, concretely, the two things that would improve the draft most. The student leaves with a task for the week that they will do alone, because a session that ends with the tutor taking work away has already gone wrong.

What we will not take on, stated once more because these requests arrive weekly: we do not write Extended Essays or Internal Assessments, we do not redraft them, we do not research them, we do not supply data for them, and we do not accept work framed as finishing or fixing a submission. If artificial intelligence tools have been used at any point, that use is declared under the school's own rules, and a tutor will tell a student to go and declare it rather than help them around it. Those limits are the service, not a restriction on it.

Practically, a standing weekly slot works better than a block of sessions booked in a panic. Pick a day and time your household can protect for a term, tell us about the building's visitor protocol before the first visit, and let the tutor and student settle into a rhythm. The essays that land well are almost never the ones rescued late; they are the ones worked on steadily by a student who understood, early, that this is their piece of writing and nobody else's.
bullets: Send subject, question, next internal deadline, suburb and free evenings
First session: the student explains the question and reads a paragraph aloud
Every session ends with work for the student, never work for the tutor
Declare any AI use under the school's rules; a tutor will insist on it

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Khar West for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Khar West it is usually straightforward because we match along the Western Line rather than across the city. A tutor based between Bandra and Santacruz reaches most Khar West buildings in fifteen to twenty minutes outside the worst of the evening peak, so a 7pm or 7.30pm start on a fixed weekday holds for a full term. What breaks these slots is not distance but crossing the Western Express Highway at the wrong hour. Tell us your two preferred evenings and we will shortlist tutors who live on your side of the line.

faqs.question: Our society in Powai requires a gate pass for every visitor. How does that work?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once with your society office as a recurring weekly visitor and the problem disappears. In Powai and the larger Hiranandani Gardens complexes this is routine, and most managements will issue a standing entry for a named tutor on a fixed day once a resident sponsors it. Give us the building's requirement before the first visit so the tutor carries photo identification that matches the name on the pass. Where a society insists on a fresh pass each time, we ask the tutor to arrive ten minutes early rather than losing session time at the gate.

faqs.question: Can you help finish my daughter's Extended Essay? It is due in ten days.
faqs.answer: We cannot finish it, and no honest service can. What a tutor can do in ten days is sit with your daughter, read what exists against the published criteria, tell her which two changes would improve it most, and teach her how to make those changes herself in the time left. What a tutor will not do is write a section, rewrite her paragraphs, add research, or hand back a corrected document. She signs the essay as her own work, and a submission she did not write puts her entire diploma at risk, not just one essay. If the request is really "produce a finished essay", we will decline the work.

faqs.question: Will a tutor polish the draft or correct the English in it?
faqs.answer: No. Polishing somebody else's academic submission is producing part of it, whatever it is called. A tutor will tell your son that paragraph four repeats paragraph two, that a sentence is doing three jobs and should do one, and that a tense slips in his methods section, and will show him how to fix that kind of problem on a different passage. He then makes the corrections in his own document. The reason is not pedantry: a student who made every edit himself can explain every sentence if the school asks, and a student handed a cleaned-up file cannot.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Rates for IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on five things rather than a published price list: the board and level, how scarce the subject specialism is, how far the tutor travels and at what hour, the session length, and whether you book home sessions, online or a hybrid pattern. Extended Essay work in a common subject group costs less to staff than a scarce one, and a South Mumbai evening slot that needs a tutor to cross Peddar Road in peak hour prices differently from a slot ten minutes away. We quote per tutor once we know those details, and we do not quote an outcome.

faqs.question: My son already has a supervisor at school. Why would he also need a tutor?
faqs.answer: The supervisor is appointed by the school, owns the process and signs off the work, and nothing a tutor does replaces that. The gap a tutor fills is time and repetition. A supervisor has a limited number of meetings with a limited number of minutes each, spread across several candidates, while the writing problem your son has is one he needs to work on weekly with somebody reading his sentences slowly. A tutor also never contacts the school. If supervisor advice and tutor advice conflict, the supervisor is right and the tutor's job is to help him understand the reasoning.

faqs.question: The research question feels far too broad. Can a tutor narrow it for him?
faqs.answer: A tutor can press on it until he narrows it himself, which is a different and more useful thing. The session looks like interrogation: what exactly are you comparing, over what period, using what evidence, and what would a surprising answer look like? Most broad questions collapse into something workable in forty minutes of that. The tutor does not hand over a replacement question, partly because a question the student did not choose produces an essay he cannot sustain for the full length, and partly because the question is part of the work he is submitting as his own.

faqs.question: How many sessions does the writing phase usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the student starts, and we will not invent a number for your case. A student with a settled question, a full set of notes and a clear argument may need a handful of sessions on structure and cutting. A student who has drifted for a term needs weekly sessions across months, because the problem is not the draft but the habit of working on it. The useful way to plan is a standing weekly slot through to the school's internal deadline, reviewed after four weeks when there is actual evidence of how fast this particular student moves.

faqs.question: Does online work for Extended Essay sessions, or is home tuition better?
faqs.answer: For the writing phase, home tuition is better and we say so plainly. Reading a draft slowly, pen on paper, with the criteria open beside it, is a physical activity that loses something over a screen share. Online is the right answer when the registered subject is scarce enough that the right specialist is in another zone, when the student is travelling, or when the only workable slot is an early Sunday. Most families end up hybrid by DP2: one home session for the hard reading and a short online check mid-week to confirm the writing actually happened.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What happens then?
faqs.answer: Tell us, with specifics, and we re-shortlist from the same subject group. The useful specifics are these: has the student stopped preparing between sessions, have the sessions become the tutor talking while the student listens, or is the feedback too vague to act on? Each points to a different fix, and only the third is always the tutor's fault. We hand the session notes to the next tutor so nothing restarts from zero. We will not keep a placement running because a deadline is close, and we end it immediately if a tutor has started editing the draft directly.

faqs.question: Is artificial intelligence allowed? My daughter used it to summarise some articles.
faqs.answer: That use must be declared under your school's own rules, and the school's policy is the one that governs, not ours. Schools in Mumbai differ on what is permitted and on how it is recorded, so the first step is reading your school's academic honesty policy and then telling the supervisor exactly what was used and for what. A tutor will tell her to declare it rather than help her work around it, and will not use these tools to produce or improve any part of her essay. An undeclared use discovered later is treated as misconduct against the candidate.

faqs.question: Should the tutor speak to the supervisor or email the school about the essay?
faqs.answer: No, and we instruct tutors not to. The supervisor and the subject teacher are appointed by the school, the relationship belongs to the school, and a private tutor inserting themselves into it creates confusion about who is advising the candidate. If something needs raising with the school, you or your child raise it. The tutor's contribution is to make sure your child walks into the next supervisor meeting able to say clearly what the essay argues, what changed since last time, and what they want feedback on.
