sections.heading: Deciding about Film in Mumbai: one home tuition session of questions
paragraphs: If you are here to decide rather than to start weekly tuition, book a single session and say that is what it is for. Bring three things: the student's current subject list with levels marked, anything they have already made or written for Film, and an honest account of what their weekends already contain. That last item sounds irrelevant and is the one that most often changes the advice.

Expect the session to be uncomfortable in a productive way. A tutor doing this properly will show the student a short extract and ask them to write about it for ten minutes, then read what they wrote in front of them. They will ask what the student imagines the course is, and then describe what it is. They will ask about finishing: what was the last thing you started and did not complete, and why. By the end, you should have a direct answer about fit, and a sentence about what would have to be true for this to work.

If you are starting ongoing tuition instead, the same first session doubles as a diagnostic and ends with a six-week plan and a named first weakness. Weekly one-to-one home classes then do the unglamorous work: scope control, the writing cycle, the production calendar, and somebody asking every week what has actually moved. The tutor teaches craft and critiques the work. The student makes every part of the submission themselves, and locations, equipment, safety, other people and copyright all go through the school.

Settle logistics in week one either way. The evening and length, the room, whether your society needs a standing visitor entry arranged in advance, and what happens when a session is missed for rain or an examination. Film home classes Mumbai families sustain for two years are the ones where the slot was realistic from the start, and where somebody was willing to say in week one that a 6pm Tuesday across the city was never going to happen.
bullets: Book one session explicitly for the decision, and say so when you write
Bring the subject list with levels, any existing work, and the weekend picture
Expect ten minutes of writing and a direct reading of it
Leave with an answer on fit and what would have to be true
Ongoing tuition starts with a named weakness and a six-week plan
Agree the slot, the room, gate entry and the missed-session rule immediately

faqs.question: Can a private tutor tell us whether our child should take Film at all?
faqs.answer: A good one can give you a clear, evidenced opinion in a single session, and that is a legitimate reason to book. Tell us upfront that the hour is for a decision, because we shortlist differently for it: you want someone who has watched several cohorts succeed and fail at this subject, not someone who will be encouraging. The session should involve the student attempting a short piece of the actual written work rather than discussing films, because how they handle that is the evidence. Ask the tutor directly whether they have ever advised a family against the subject.

faqs.question: My child wants to direct. Will Film give them that?
faqs.answer: Partly, and less than they are picturing. Diploma Programme Film includes the student's own production work, so they will direct something, but a large share of the assessed output is written: close analysis, comparative work, documentation of their own decisions, and at Higher Level an account of their individual role. A student expecting two years of directing is usually disappointed by the end of the first term, which is structural rather than anyone's fault. Showing them what the written components look like before the subject choice is fixed is the cheapest way to avoid that, and it takes about an hour.

faqs.question: What does Film cost in equipment, and what do we need at home?
faqs.answer: No camera purchase is necessary, and buying one is rarely the best use of the money. A recent phone, an inexpensive tripod, a basic external microphone and free editing software are enough to produce work that reads well against the criteria, because what is assessed is the thinking and the control rather than the hardware. The costs that do bite are a machine that can play back and cut footage without stalling, somewhere quiet enough to record dialogue, and other people's time. If your household is short on quiet space, that matters more than any kit decision.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Chembur or Mulund for an evening session?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the Eastern Suburbs are better served than families there expect. Chembur, Govandi, Wadala, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund sit on the Central and Harbour lines with the Eastern Express Highway running through, and the Eastern Freeway makes the island city unusually close, so a tutor based here can hold slots in two directions in one week. Mulund also connects to Thane on the Eastern Express Highway, which widens the pool further. Tell us your building, the free evenings and the latest start time you would accept, and we will say what that realistically opens up.

faqs.question: How much weekend time does Film take, and will it affect other subjects?
faqs.answer: More than the Diploma trains you to expect, and in blocks rather than hours. A single sequence can take a Saturday morning to set up and shoot plus two evenings to cut, and at Higher Level the collaborative work means coordinating several families' weekends. The collision to watch for is October to December of DP2, when Film deadlines, science internal assessments and the Extended Essay all want the same weeks, and the one that slips is always the one needing other people. Map every deadline across all six subjects on one page at the start of DP1.

faqs.question: Does taking Film help with film school applications?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the institution, and that is the only honest answer anyone can give you. Requirements differ from one place to another and change over time, so check each institution's own admissions information directly and recently rather than relying on a second-hand account. What the Diploma Programme Film course reliably develops is precise analysis, planning under constraint and the ability to finish a project, and those are useful whatever the student goes on to study. Make the subject decision from what each place actually publishes, written down, rather than from a conversation at a family dinner.

faqs.question: Should my child take Film at Higher Level or Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Decide it as a workload question rather than a seriousness question. Higher Level adds a collaborative project made with other Film students, which means classmates' availability becomes part of your child's deadline, on top of the extra depth. The decisive input is what else is at Higher Level: Film plus two heavy science subjects is a scheduling problem regardless of how much your child enjoys the course. A tutor who knows the Diploma will ask for the full timetable before offering a view, and should be willing to recommend Standard Level if the rest of the week is already full.

faqs.question: Can we still change out of Film, and what happens to the work already done?
faqs.answer: The window is set by your school within the registration timetable, so ask the DP coordinator directly and early. What matters practically is that production work already begun does not transfer anywhere, those hours are not recoverable, and the student joins a new subject with its continuous assessment already underway. The cost of changing rises steeply week by week, which is why a wavering student is better served by one honest assessment in the first months of DP1 than by waiting for certainty. Certainty tends to arrive after the window has closed.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a private Film tutor?
faqs.answer: IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on level, subject scarcity, session length, travel distance and the tutor's specialisation, and Film pushes several of those upward. A tutor who has actually taught or examined the Diploma Programme course is scarce, and one crossing a zone for a weekly evening slot either prices the travel in or declines the booking. A one-off decision session is usually arranged differently from ongoing weekly work. We publish no figures because an honest range would be too wide to be useful, so ask each shortlisted tutor directly what their rate assumes.

faqs.question: Is one-to-one home tuition better than a group class for this subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, more clearly than in most subjects, because every Film student is making something different. A group session has to stay general while the student's real problems are entirely specific: this scope, this location, this paragraph, this cut. One-to-one home classes also let the tutor work on the student's own drafts against the criteria rather than on shared examples. The exception is viewing: watching and discussing unfamiliar films works perfectly well in a group, and some schools run that anyway. For the assessed work, individual attention is what moves it.

faqs.question: Our child is disorganised. Can a weekly tutor actually fix that?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot change a temperament, and weekly home tuition can build a structure that works around one, which in this subject matters more than usual. Film punishes non-finishers harder than other Diploma subjects, since a half-finished production cannot be usefully submitted and no weekend of revision rescues it. What a weekly one-to-one arrangement provides is a fixed point: somebody asking every seven days what moved, a dated plan working backwards from the deadline, and a scope small enough to be finishable. Parents should expect the tutor to reduce ambition deliberately in the first month, and should back that rather than resist it.

faqs.question: What if we book a tutor and the fit is wrong?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, with no argument. For decision-focused bookings the usual mismatch is tone: the family wanted a straight assessment and got encouragement. For ongoing work it is usually specialism, where the tutor is strong on analysis and weak on practical planning or the reverse. One specific example of what is not landing lets us pick a different profile deliberately rather than at random. Everything produced so far, including marked drafts and the production plan, belongs to the student, so a replacement starts from where the work actually is.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB DP film tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Film is the smallest tutor pool on this platform and the one where the obvious candidate is most often the wrong one. Mumbai has more working film professionals than any other city in the country, and a camera operator or an assistant editor with ten years on sets knows a great deal that a sixteen-year-old would benefit from hearing. Knowing how a scene gets made is not the same as knowing how the Diploma assesses a student's account of it, and a professional who has never read the assessment criteria will teach craft brilliantly and leave the written components exactly where they were. We screen for both, and when somebody has only one half we say which half.

The diagnosis before matching has three parts, and families are often surprised by which one is weak. First, can the student analyse a sequence she has not seen before, in film language rather than in plot summary? Second, can she produce work to a brief, meaning a set of constraints she did not choose, rather than the project she already wanted to make? Third, can she document her own reasoning so that somebody who was not there understands why each decision was taken? Most students who arrive here are strong on enthusiasm, adequate on production and genuinely weak on the first and third.

We then ask for two things rather than a conversation: one piece of her written analysis with the teacher's comments still on it, and one thing she has shot, however short and however rough. The pair together tells a tutor more in fifteen minutes than an hour of discussion, because the gap between the two is usually the whole problem. A student whose three-minute film shows real instinct and whose written paragraph is a plot summary needs a very specific kind of help, and it is not more equipment.

Matching for an IB DP film tutor in Mumbai then has to respect the map, because Film tutors are concentrated in a few places and most families are not in them. We match inside one travel shed wherever we can and recommend online honestly where we cannot, rather than booking a weekly cross-city commitment that nobody keeps past the monsoon.
bullets: 1. Send the year, the level and the components the school has flagged.
2. Attach one marked written analysis and one short thing she shot.
3. We separate the analysis problem from the production problem.
4. Two or three tutors return with an eight-week plan each.
5. Paid trial at home or online, then a standing weekly slot.

sections.heading: Where Film sits in the IB Diploma Programme
paragraphs: Film is an arts subject within the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), taken across the two years Mumbai schools call DP1 and DP2, and in most schools a student may take it or replace it with a second choice from another group. Fewer schools in the city offer it than offer Visual Arts, so families sometimes choose between Film at one school and no Film at all, which raises the stakes on getting the fit right. A Film IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai parents hire is most often brought in during DP1, once the first written task has come back with a mark nobody expected.

The course is built from textual analysis, comparative study, the film portfolio and, at Higher Level (HL), the collaborative film project. Read those names carefully and the shape of the subject becomes clear: two strands that reach an examiner as sustained written and spoken argument, one that reaches an examiner as created work with reasoning attached, and at Higher Level a further piece made with other people under real constraints. Confirm the exact structure and any weightings with your school's DP coordinator and the current subject guide, because the IB revises guides on its own cycle and nothing on this page should be treated as the specification.

The Higher Level and Standard Level (SL) choice matters more in Film than families expect, because the extra work at Higher Level is collaborative and therefore dependent on other people's calendars. A group project in DP2 means coordinating four students across a city where a Saturday shoot can involve three train lines. That is a genuine logistical commitment, and it falls in the same months as the Extended Essay (EE) deadline and the mock examinations. Students who like working with other people thrive on it. Students who prefer to control everything find it the hardest part of their Diploma.

Two neighbouring pieces of the Diploma connect usefully. A student may write an Extended Essay in Film, which rewards somebody with a real analytical question and punishes somebody who simply wants to write about films she likes. Theory of Knowledge (TOK) discussions about representation, evidence and perspective sit naturally beside this subject. Neither should drive the subject choice on its own.
bullets: Arts group subject, offered by fewer Mumbai schools than Visual Arts
Strands: textual analysis, comparative study, film portfolio, collaborative project

sections.heading: Textual analysis, comparative study and the film portfolio
paragraphs: Textual analysis asks a student to take a short extract and account for how it works, which means film language rather than story. Shot scale and duration, camera movement and height, the logic of the cuts, what the sound is doing and whether it belongs to the world on screen, lighting and colour, performance and blocking, and the relationship between all of them and the effect produced. The discipline is evidence: every claim should point at something a second viewer could find in the extract. Students who have watched thousands of films and never been taught this write confident paragraphs about tension and brilliant acting and are marked down for saying nothing checkable.

Comparative study asks for something harder, which is an argument across films from different contexts, supported by research and delivered in a sustained form. Context is the operative word. It means production circumstances, period, technology, industry structure, audience and the cultural conditions a film came out of, used to explain why the film is made the way it is rather than decorating the analysis with background. A student who can say that a particular editing rhythm belongs to a period's working practices, and show it in the footage, is doing the subject properly.

The film portfolio is the created half, and it is a documented half. Work is produced to a brief, in defined film-making roles, with the student's own account of her intentions, her research, her decisions and her evaluation of the result. The documentation is not a cover sheet. An examiner reading it wants the reasoning: this framing was chosen for this reason, the first attempt failed because of this, the fix was that. A tutor can set exercises, interrogate a plan, screen the rushes and read the written reasoning hard, and a tutor cannot shoot, light, edit, grade, sound-mix, write or direct any part of the submission. Nobody teaching this subject should offer to, and a student who hands in work that is not substantially her own has a problem no mark can fix.

There is one more obligation that is heavier in Film than in any other Diploma subject, and families consistently underestimate it. Everything in a student's work that is not hers has to be credited or cleared under her school's rules: clips used in analysis, music under a sequence, stock footage, a photograph on a wall, somebody else's recording of a street. Schools have clear policies on this and departments will explain them. Sort it out before the edit rather than after, because discovering in February that the track under the final scene cannot be used is a problem with no good solutions left.
bullets: Textual analysis is film language with checkable evidence, not plot summary
Comparative study uses context to explain why a film is made that way

sections.heading: Film tuition across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Thane
paragraphs: The Western Suburbs are where Film tutors actually live, and that is not an accident in a city that is the base of the Hindi film industry. Andheri West, Oshiwara, Juhu, Goregaon East, Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz West, Malad, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar East sit along the Western Line, the Western Express Highway and Link Road, with Metro Line 1 running Versova to Andheri to Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 covering Dahisar to Gundavali. Most people in this city who can teach both halves of the subject are within that corridor. Matching along the line works and matching across it does not, so a Juhu family has a deep pool and a Dahisar East family has a thin one, and we say which you are in before you book anything.

Navi Mumbai deserves a separate paragraph because the production half plays out differently there. The nodes, Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, are laid out with wide roads, newer buildings and open space that is far easier to film in than anything on the island, and Palm Beach Road, the Sion-Panvel Highway, the Harbour Line, the Trans-Harbour Line from Thane to Vashi and the Belapur to Pendhar metro make moving a small crew between nodes genuinely practical. What Navi Mumbai lacks is tutors who have taught this course, so we match node to node where we can and run an IB DP film tutor in Mumbai online for families in Kharghar and Panvel when nobody suitable is inside the shed. The Atal Setu has changed what is reachable from the island, and it has not changed what a tutor will do twice a week at seven in the evening.

The remaining zones each shape the work in their own way. South Mumbai, covering Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Fort, Babulnath, Walkeshwar, Tardeo, Peddar Road and Worli, is served by the Western Line into Churchgate and Mumbai Central, the Harbour Line to Dockyard and Sewri, Metro Line 3 out of Cuffe Parade and the Coastal Road, and gives students the most visually interesting locations in the city and the hardest permissions to obtain. Thane runs from Thane West and Pokhran Road through Majiwada out along Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali, where the evening doubles every journey and weekend shooting is far easier than weekday tutoring.

The Central and Eastern Suburbs complete the map. Powai and Chandivali hang off JVLR with no station of their own, reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and Kurla links west through the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR). Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup, Mulund West and Wadala sit on the Central and Harbour lines with the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway, and the Chembur to Wadala monorail. The Eastern Freeway matters for Film students specifically: a Higher Level group with members in Chembur and Wadala can realistically shoot together on a Saturday, while a group split between Borivali and Panvel cannot, and the group that ignores this loses its collaborative project to logistics rather than to talent. A search for IB tutors near me Mumbai returns hundreds of names and almost none who have taught DP Film, which is the gap this page describes.

sections.heading: Which months decide a Mumbai DP Film student's grade?
paragraphs: The production calendar decides it, and it runs ahead of the academic one. Mumbai schools start in June, which puts the first months of DP1 inside the monsoon, when outdoor shooting is unreliable and often impossible. A student who plans a rain-independent interior piece for August and saves the ambitious exterior for the clear weather after the festivals is working with the city. A student who schedules the opposite loses four weekends and then rushes. The second constraint is that post-production always takes longer than a sixteen-year-old estimates, usually by a factor nobody believes until the second project.

That makes November to January the real deadline zone for DP2, because everything created has to be finished, documented and written up while mock examinations and the Extended Essay final submission are also happening. A student with footage in hand in November is in good shape. A student still trying to get four classmates into the same location in December is not, and no amount of tuition recovers a shoot that did not happen. The useful intervention in that situation is ruthless scope reduction, which is exactly what a good tutor does and a sympathetic one does not.

School calendars across the city differ by weeks. Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School, Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Oberoi International School at JVLR in Goregaon East, Hiranandani Foundation School and Podar International School in Powai, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Activity High School on Peddar Road, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, JBCN International School in Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, NES International School in Mulund West, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Witty International School in Malad and Chembur, Ryan Global School in Kandivali and Worli, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul each set their own internal dates and their own equipment policies. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, or with any film school, studio or production house. We name schools because their calendars are what a shooting plan has to fit around.

Two practical requests to make of the department early. Ask what equipment the school lends, for how long and with what booking system, because a student who assumes a camera will be free on the weekend she needs it is planning on hope. And ask for the written policy on third-party material, music and clips, in writing, before the first edit rather than during the last one.

sections.heading: Home tuition or online for a subject with a production half?
paragraphs: Home tuition leads for the analytical half, and the reason is the same one that applies to any writing-heavy subject: a tutor at the same table watches the student work rather than receiving the finished paragraph. A home tutor can pause a sequence, ask what just happened in the sound, and get the answer before the student has had time to compose a presentable one. For a subject where the gap between watching and analysing is the whole problem, that immediacy is worth paying for. IB home tuition in Mumbai for Film is scarce rather than unavailable, and it is scarcest exactly where families most expect it to be easy.

Online does two jobs better than a room. Screen-sharing a sequence and stepping through it frame by frame, with both people annotating, is a better analysis lesson than two heads over one laptop in a living room. And reviewing a rough cut works well remotely, because the student screens it, the tutor takes timed notes and they talk through them, which is closer to how feedback actually happens in production anyway. An IB online tutor in Mumbai also solves the geography: a Panvel or Kasarvadavali family can work with a specialist in Andheri West every week without anybody crossing the city.

There is one boundary that applies in both formats and matters more here than in any other subject. The tutor does not touch the work. Not the camera, not the timeline, not the colour, not the sound, not the script. A tutor who takes the mouse to show how a cut should go has crossed a line, and in an edit suite the line is easy to cross by accident and hard to defend afterwards. Good tutors describe, demonstrate on something that is not the student's project, and hand the mouse back. Ask any Film tutor in Mumbai how she handles that moment, and listen carefully to the answer.

Most of our Film families end up hybrid. Home classes for the written strands and the planning, online for sequence analysis and rough-cut review, and a clear understanding that the production itself happens between sessions with the student's own hands and her own crew of classmates. A home tutor costs travel inside the rate, and a weekday evening slot in Dahisar East or Kharghar is the first thing to break in July. Online costs you the shared physical screen and the ability to look at a storyboard spread across a table, which matters more in this subject than in most.
bullets: Home tuition: best for written strands, planning and watching a student write
Online: best for frame-by-frame sequence analysis and rough-cut review
The tutor never takes the mouse, the camera or the timeline

sections.heading: How are Film tutors in Mumbai checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Identity, qualifications and references are verified before any Mumbai family meets a tutor, and every applicant is interviewed by somebody who knows the Diploma. For Film the subject screen is built from the job itself. The applicant is shown an extract she has not seen, given a few minutes, and asked to produce the shot-by-shot analysis she would expect from a strong student. Then she is handed a real anonymised portfolio reflection and asked to mark it against published criteria and justify the mark to a parent. A verified IB DP film tutor in Mumbai has passed both parts, not just the first.

We welcome working film professionals and we screen them differently. Somebody with years on sets brings craft knowledge no classroom teacher can match, and the questions we put to them are about assessment rather than about filming: what does documented reasoning look like for an examiner, where do students lose marks in comparative study, how would you handle a student whose film is good and whose written account of it is empty. Professionals who have read the criteria answer these well. Professionals who have not are honest about it, and we place them differently or not at all.

Three checks are yours to make in the trial session. Give the tutor a sequence your child has never discussed in class, because the skill is response to the unfamiliar and any tutor can be impressive about a film she has taught twenty times. Ask what she will not do, and expect shooting, editing, writing and directing any part of a submission to be on that list without prompting. And be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or a guaranteed film-school place. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, no tutor on the platform may suggest otherwise, and a tutor who promises a specific grade in a first conversation is describing the next two years.

One further question is worth asking because of where you live. Ask the tutor how she would widen a student's viewing beyond the films that student already loves. An answer that names a range of traditions, periods and forms, including documentary and animation, and that treats the Hindi film industry as one serious cinema among several rather than as either the default or the thing to grow out of, tells you she will teach breadth without condescension in either direction.
bullets: Applicants analyse an unseen extract under time, shot by shot
Applicants mark a real portfolio reflection and justify the mark
Industry professionals are screened on assessment knowledge, not craft

sections.heading: Why loving films is not analysing a sequence
paragraphs: Put a two-minute extract in front of a student who watches constantly and the response is usually some version of this: the scene is really tense, the acting is excellent, the music builds and you can feel what the character is going through. Every sentence may be true and the paragraph earns very little, because nothing in it points at anything a second viewer could locate in the footage. The same student, taught properly for eight weeks, writes something like this instead: the extract opens on a wide static frame held long enough to become uncomfortable, the cut to a mid-shot happens on the character's movement so the edit is almost invisible, the next three shots shorten in duration while the camera moves closer, the ambient sound of the street drops away under a sustained low tone that belongs to no visible source, and the shift from shallow to deeper focus in the final shot puts the figure back into a space she had been isolated from. Same student. Same film. An education in between.

The method behind that transformation is dull and reliable. Watch the extract with the sound off and describe only what the camera does. Watch it again with the picture off and describe only what you hear, separating what exists in the world of the film from what has been laid over it. Count the shots and note where the durations change. Mark the one cut that does the most work and say why. Only then write a paragraph, and strike out every sentence that does not point at something in the extract. A student who runs that procedure forty times stops needing it, which is the point.

Context is the second half of the subject and the half students skip. A film is made the way it is because of when, where, by whom and for whom it was made: the technology available, the industry's working practices, the economics, the censorship environment, the audience's expectations, the traditions the makers were trained in or reacting against. Used properly, context supplies the because that analysis on its own cannot. Used lazily, it becomes a paragraph of history pasted in front of an unrelated description, which examiners recognise instantly. The discipline is to let context explain something specific you have already observed in the footage.

Breadth is where living in this city cuts both ways. A student here has unusual access to one of the world's major film cultures, and grows up fluent in its grammar, its stars, its song sequences and its narrative conventions. That fluency is a real asset and it is also a default that has to be made visible before it can be examined, because the conventions of any one industry are choices rather than the natural shape of cinema. The course asks for engagement well beyond what a student already watches: early silent cinema, post-war European movements, Japanese and Korean and Iranian and Latin American and West African traditions, documentary in its several forms, animation as a serious mode rather than as children's material, and the many cinemas of India, which are not one thing and should never be described as one. India has distinct film cultures with their own histories, languages, economics and aesthetics. A student who writes about all of them as a single entity has already lost the argument she was about to make.

Which leaves the student who wants to direct and resents the theory, and in a city full of people who work in film there are a lot of them. The honest response is not to defend theory. It is to point out that every production decision in the portfolio has to be explained in writing, that the explanation is assessed, and that the ability to say exactly why a shot is framed the way it is survives long after school in every room where films actually get made. The analysis strand is not a tax on the fun part. It is the vocabulary for the fun part, and the students who come to believe that in DP1 produce visibly better films by DP2. The ones who never believe it make competent work and write apologetic paragraphs about it, and that gap is the single most common reason a Film grade comes in below what a family expected.

sections.heading: What the first term with a Film tutor should change
paragraphs: At four weeks, look at a paragraph rather than a mark. Take the analysis your child wrote in week one and the one she wrote last Tuesday and count only the sentences that point at something locatable in the extract: a shot, a cut, a sound, a movement, a change in focus or colour. In week one that count is usually one or two. By week four it should be five or six, even if the writing is awkward, because precision arrives before elegance in this subject and the elegance follows on its own. The second early signal is that she starts talking about films she is watching for pleasure in these terms, unprompted and slightly annoyingly.

At one term the production side should have changed too, and not in the direction most families expect. Good tuition usually makes a student's projects smaller and better: fewer locations, fewer people, a clearer idea, a finishable scope. If her plans are getting more ambitious every month, something is wrong. Her documentation should also have changed character, from describing what she did to explaining why, which is the single highest-value shift available in this subject and the one that moves marks fastest.

Over a full cycle the limits are worth stating. A tutor can teach analysis, widen viewing, structure a production plan and mark documentation honestly. She cannot be on the shoot, cannot fix a project whose footage was never captured, and cannot manufacture the hours of watching that breadth requires, which is work only the student does. She also cannot make four classmates turn up on a Saturday in Kandivali. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, because the final judgement is an examiner's. What we commit to is a verified tutor who knows this course, a written note after each session and a replacement within days when the fit is wrong.

Families sometimes ask us to find the best IB tutor in Mumbai for Film, and the request is understandable and not answerable. The tutor who rescues a student with strong films and empty writing is not the tutor who helps a careful analytical writer get a camera moving. Tell us which of the two you have and the shortlist becomes genuinely useful, and if neither description fits, say that too.

sections.heading: Booking a home tutor or online Film session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Send three things and the first session becomes a diagnosis. One piece of written analysis with the teacher's comments still on it. One thing she has shot, however short, however rough, and preferably something she is not proud of. And the school's dates and rules: internal deadlines, the equipment booking system, and the written policy on clips, music and third-party footage. Families who send all three get a plan. Families who send none get a conversation, which is pleasant and costs the same.

The session itself is deliberately uncomfortable. The tutor screens an extract your daughter has never seen and asks for a written analysis under a clock, which establishes the baseline honestly. Then they watch what she shot and talk about the decisions behind it rather than the result. Then the tutor writes the plan: whether the analytical half or the production half comes first, what the next eight weeks drill, and what scope her current project should be cut to. You get that note in writing whether or not you book again, and whether you continue with an IB private tutor Mumbai families keep for two years or a short eight-week engagement.

Tell us your node rather than the city. A home tutor for Film Mumbai parents can realistically keep comes from inside one travel shed: Andheri West to Juhu, Chembur to Wadala, Nerul to Belapur, Thane West to Majiwada. Film home classes Mumbai families book as a standing weekly slot hold when the tutor is twenty minutes away and collapse when he is across the city, whatever everyone agreed in June. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on level, how scarce the specialism is, session length and travel distance, and Film is the scarcest specialism we handle, so we quote after the match rather than before it.

faqs.question: My son watches three films a week. Is he not already good at this?
faqs.answer: He has an advantage and a blind spot, and the blind spot is the one that shows up in marks. Watching widely builds instinct, reference and taste, none of which the course assesses directly. What it assesses is the ability to take a sequence apart in film language and support every claim with something a second viewer could find in the frame, and that is a taught skill rather than an absorbed one. Knowledgeable fans often write the most confident and least evidenced paragraphs in a class, because they are describing their reaction rather than the construction. Eight weeks of structured work usually closes it.

faqs.question: How much of DP Film is writing rather than film-making?
faqs.answer: Enough that families who pictured a production course are regularly surprised. The analytical strands reach an examiner as sustained argument, and even the created work is accompanied by the student's own documentation of intentions, research, decisions and evaluation. A student who writes badly will be held back whatever she can do with a camera. For the exact component structure and any weightings, check the current subject guide and your school's DP coordinator rather than any website, because the IB revises its guides on its own cycle. The practical implication does not change: treat this as a writing subject with a production half.

faqs.question: Do we need to buy a camera, or will a phone do?
faqs.answer: A phone is genuinely enough to start, and most schools lend equipment for the work that needs more. What matters far more than the sensor is sound, light and planning, in that order. Usable audio is the single most common technical failure in student films, and an inexpensive external microphone fixes more problems than an expensive camera body. Ask your school what it lends, for how long and how bookings work, because a student who assumes a camera will be free on the one weekend her crew is available is planning on luck. Buy nothing in DP1 until a tutor has seen her work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our home in Andheri West for an evening session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Andheri West is one of the easier places in the city for this subject. Most Film tutors live along the western corridor, so Andheri West, Oshiwara, Juhu and Goregaon East have a real pool rather than a notional one. Early evening slots between five and seven fill first and hold best; a 7.30pm weekday slot becomes a weekly negotiation once the monsoon settles in. Home tuition suits the written strands and the planning especially well. If your preferred hour is unavailable with the right specialist, a weekly online session plus a monthly home tutor visit is the usual compromise.

faqs.question: He wants to direct and finds the theory boring. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Stop defending the theory and connect it to the thing he wants. Every decision in his portfolio work has to be explained in writing and that explanation is assessed, so the analytical vocabulary is not a separate subject but the language for describing his own choices. In practice the fastest route is to analyse his own footage with the same rigour used on anybody else's: shot by shot, with the sound separated out. Students who resent analysis in the abstract usually stop resenting it the moment it is turned on their own work and starts making that work better.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help edit his film if he runs out of time?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the firmest boundary in the subject. A tutor does not touch the camera, the timeline, the grade, the mix or the script. She can watch rushes and give notes, demonstrate a technique on footage that is not his, question a structural choice and push him to cut scope to something finishable, which is usually the real answer when time has run out. Work submitted has to be substantially the student's own, and anything in it that is not his, including music, clips and stock footage, has to be credited or cleared under the school's rules.

faqs.question: What should she be watching beyond the films she already likes?
faqs.answer: Deliberately unfamiliar territory, chosen for range rather than reputation. In practice that means early silent cinema, post-war European movements, Japanese, Korean, Iranian, Latin American and West African traditions, documentary in several forms, and animation treated as a serious mode rather than as children's material. It also means the cinemas of India plural: the industries and traditions of this country differ in language, history, economics and aesthetics, and writing about them as one thing is a mistake examiners notice. A good tutor builds a viewing list around the gaps in what your daughter already knows, then makes her write about each one.

faqs.question: Can a student film be shot inside our society compound?
faqs.answer: Often yes, with permission obtained in advance and in writing from the managing committee. Say who will be present, which areas and what hours, and keep the crew small, because a request for four students and a tripod in the back lobby on a Sunday morning is usually granted and a vague request for filming is usually refused. Avoid residents' faces and private flat interiors unless the people involved have agreed. Public spaces, roads and transport are a different matter with their own rules and permissions, so plan interiors and controlled spaces first and treat street filming as something to research properly.

faqs.question: Does living in Mumbai actually help a DP Film student?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one caveat worth naming. A student here grows up inside a major film culture and often has access to people who work in it, which builds fluency, reference and a sense of how production really runs. The caveat is that fluency in one industry's conventions can look like a universal grammar when it is a set of choices, and the course rewards a student who can see those choices as choices. The strongest students here use their access and then deliberately widen their viewing well past it. We write about this industry respectfully and make no claims about any particular studio, production house, film or professional.

faqs.question: What do IB Film tuition fees depend on?
faqs.answer: Level, scarcity, session length and travel, and Film is the scarcest specialism on this platform. IB tuition fees in Mumbai sit higher for DP work than for MYP or IGCSE support, higher at Higher Level than at Standard Level, and higher again where very few tutors can teach both the analytical and the production halves. A home tutor prices the journey into the rate, so somebody crossing from Andheri West to Kharghar at seven in the evening costs more than somebody walking over within Juhu. Online removes travel entirely. We publish no price list, because a figure quoted without your node and level would be invented.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Navi Mumbai or Thane for a weekly home session?
faqs.answer: Within those areas, yes, and across the creek or the highway, usually not for a weekly slot. Navi Mumbai works node to node across Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel on Palm Beach Road, and Thane works from the station and Pokhran Road out towards Ghodbunder Road, with the caution that the evening roughly doubles every journey. Bringing a Film specialist from Andheri West to Panvel every week is a plan that survives about a month. Where the local pool is empty, we recommend weekly online with a monthly home tutor visit, and we say so before you book rather than after.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after six weeks. What happens?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them within days, with no notice period and no charge for the switch. Be specific about which half has stalled, because it changes who we propose next: the written analysis is not improving, the production notes are vague, the tutor talks about her own work more than the student's, or the viewing list has never materialised. In this subject a mismatch between a craft-strong tutor and an analysis-weak student is the most common failure, and it is entirely fixable by changing the person rather than the plan.

Two or three verified tutors come back within about two working days with an eight-week plan each. Book a paid trial at home or online, expect an unseen extract and a clock, and read the written plan afterwards. If the match is wrong, say so and we replace it. Nobody here promises a specific grade.

sections.heading: How a Mumbai home tuition request for French ab initio turns into a shortlist
paragraphs: Most families who book IB DP French ab initio home tuition in Mumbai are not looking for someone to teach French from scratch. They are looking for someone to explain why a student who follows every lesson, does the vocabulary, and chats happily in class keeps coming back with marks in the middle of the range. That is almost never a knowledge problem. It is a technique problem, and it is specific to each paper, so the first thing the intake asks for is the last two pieces of marked work and the marks on them, not a description of how the student is doing.

From there the shortlist is built around a single question: has this tutor marked beginner work against the published criteria, repeatedly, and can they say which criterion a particular lost mark came from? A tutor who looks at a weak piece of writing and says the grammar needs work is describing the symptom. A tutor who says the student wrote a formal article when the task asked for a message to a friend, and that the register alone cost her across two criteria, is describing the cause. The second kind is who you want, and the difference shows up inside twenty minutes of a trial session.

You then read profiles before anyone discusses a slot. Each states the DP components the tutor has taught, whether they mark to the criteria in session or take work away, which Mumbai zones they travel to, and the evenings they can hold. That last detail is why in-person matching in this city is slower than online matching: a tutor who is right on paper and lives across a creek from you will not hold a 7pm Tuesday slot in March, however enthusiastic everyone is in June. We would rather tell you that at the shortlist stage.

If the first tutor is wrong, say so after one or two sessions. A replacement is proposed without any argument about why, and the handover includes the student's marked work and whatever error record has been built so far, so the second tutor does not restart from zero. Changing a tutor in August costs a fortnight. Changing one in February of DP2 costs considerably more, which is the only reason we push families to judge the fit early rather than politely.

sections.heading: Group 2, ab initio, and why a beginner course is not the light one
paragraphs: French ab initio is one of the language acquisition courses in Group 2 of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP). It is built for students with no meaningful prior study of French, which in Mumbai usually describes a student who came through the Middle Years Programme (MYP) or an IGCSE in Hindi, Marathi or Sanskrit and then picked French at the start of DP1. French B is the parallel course for students who already have real French behind them.

Which course a student takes is settled by the school with the family, and it should stay there. A tutor can report what they observe, which is useful information for that conversation, but a tutoring platform has no business adjudicating a placement decision made by the DP coordinator and the language department who hold the student's record. Schools also differ in which level they offer the course at, so that question goes to your coordinator too, not to a website.

The thing worth saying loudly on a page about home tuition is that beginner does not mean undemanding. The course asks a student who knew no French in June of DP1 to produce written text for a specified audience, to follow unscripted speech, and to hold a recorded conversation about an image, inside two years that are already carrying the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and five other subjects with their own Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines. Families who choose it expecting an easy sixth subject tend to discover their mistake in the second term of DP1, which is late but recoverable, or in DP2, which is harder.

Technique is what makes the difference between a student who knows a certain amount of French and a student who converts that French into marks. Two students with identical vocabulary can finish a paper several marks apart purely on how they read the question, how they allocate their time, and whether they wrote the kind of text they were asked for. That is learnable, it is learnable quickly, and it is the reason a French ab initio IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai parents book in person is usually spending more time on papers than on grammar.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: what each French ab initio component actually rewards
paragraphs: French ab initio is assessed through Paper 1 writing, Paper 2 listening and reading, and the individual oral. Paper 1 rewards producing the right kind of text for the audience and purpose given. Paper 2 rewards accurate retrieval from what is heard and read. The individual oral rewards continuous speech built from a visual stimulus. Confirm the current structure through your school, because the IB revises its subject guides on its own cycle and no tutoring site should be your source for format.

On Paper 1, the single largest avoidable loss is text type. A beginner's grammar is going to be imperfect and the criteria are written in the knowledge that it will be. What the criteria are much less forgiving about is a student who ignores what she was asked to produce. If a task asks for a set of instructions and receives a diary entry, the language criterion might still pick up something, but the message and the conceptual criteria suffer badly, and no amount of correct verb endings repairs it. So the technique is mechanical: identify the text type, write its conventions down in the margin before writing a word of French, then produce them.

On Paper 2, reading and listening fail in different ways. Reading punishes guessing. A beginner who sees a word that resembles an English one and assumes the meaning will walk into the classic traps: une librairie is a bookshop and not a library, actuellement means currently and not actually, and a question about the first will be answered confidently and wrongly by a student working from resemblance. The discipline is to find the answer in the text, locate the words the question is built from, and read the sentence they sit in rather than the paragraph they remind you of.

Listening is where limited replay bites. The recording plays a limited number of times, so a student who spends the first play trying to understand everything has wasted it. The technique is to use the time before the audio starts to read the questions, mark what kind of answer each one wants, and predict the vocabulary that would carry it, then listen for those. The individual oral then draws on the prescribed themes of identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation and sharing the planet, and rewards continuity above accuracy: a minute of imperfect connected speech scores better than four perfect sentences separated by silence.
bullets: Paper 1: identify the text type first and write its conventions in the margin
Paper 1: wrong text type damages the message and conceptual criteria badly
Reading: the answer is in the text, not in what a word resembles
Reading traps: librairie, actuellement, journée, sympathique and their lookalikes
Listening: replay is limited, so read and predict before the audio begins
Oral: continuous imperfect speech beats a few perfect disconnected sentences

sections.heading: Which Mumbai zones can actually staff a weekday home tuition slot?
paragraphs: All six, but not equally, and the difference matters when you are booking a standing weekly hour rather than a one-off. In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clock is the problem: a tutor coming from Byculla or Tardeo to Napean Sea Road or Churchgate covers very little ground and can still lose forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, so tutors here are matched inside the island rather than pulled down from the suburbs. The Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 have improved specific journeys, not the general evening. Families around Fort, Colaba and Walkeshwar usually get the most reliable in-person slots at 4.30pm or at the weekend.

The Western Suburbs reward matching along the line rather than across it. Santacruz West to Vile Parle, Malad West to Kandivali East, Borivali to Dahisar East: these hold for a full term. Bandra West to Dahisar at 6pm does not, whatever anyone says in June, and the Western Express Highway in the evening is the reason. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made some north-south pairings workable that were not, and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link makes a South Mumbai tutor reachable in Bandra in a way it never makes one reachable in Kandivali. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali sit off the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR) with no station of their own, so tutors come by road from Andheri East, Ghatkopar West or Kanjurmarg, while Kurla and Mulund West sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway and are easier to staff.

The Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi through Bhandup to Mulund, are served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway, the Monorail from Chembur to Wadala, and the Eastern Freeway, which puts Wadala and Chembur closer to the island city than the map implies. The Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) is what makes a Chembur tutor viable in the western suburbs and vice versa. Navi Mumbai works node to node along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, so Vashi, Sanpada, Nerul, Seawoods, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are matched locally; the Atal Setu has changed weekend travel across the harbour, but it has not made a weekday 7pm island-to-Kharghar lesson survive a full term, and the Trans-Harbour Line is the realistic route from Thane.

Thane runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Vartak Nagar, Majiwada, Kolshet and out along Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali, and Ghodbunder sets everything: twenty minutes off-peak, close to an hour in the evening. Thane tutors cover Thane, and Mulund tutors cross over sometimes. For families at the far end of Ghodbunder, the realistic shape of French ab initio home classes Mumbai tutors can sustain is one long weekend session in person plus online midweek, and anyone who promises three weekday evening visits out there is agreeing to something they will stop doing in week five.

sections.heading: When do Mumbai schools apply the real pressure to a beginner language?
paragraphs: The IB year in Mumbai, Maharashtra opens in June, and for a technique-focused home tuition arrangement the calendar should be read backwards from the papers rather than forwards from the start of term. The useful window for building technique is June to September of DP1, when nothing is due and a tutor can spend whole sessions on how to read a question. Nobody wants to do that in June, because nothing feels urgent. It is still the only period when it can be done properly, and the families who use it are the ones whose DP2 looks calm.

October and November of DP1 is the first collision: science and humanities IA drafts arrive together, and French, with no deadline of its own, gets quietly dropped. For a beginner language that gap costs more than it would in Economics, because a language decays rather than waits. The second collision runs from November to February of DP2, when the individual oral is prepared and recorded in most schools alongside EE deadlines and mock examinations. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School in the Bandra Kurla Complex, Ecole Mondiale World School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR, Bombay International School at Babulnath, B.D. Somani International School at Cuffe Parade, Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, JBCN International School, Chembur, NES International School in Mulund West and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul will recognise the shape, even though every school sequences its internal dates differently.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, with the IB organisation, or with any body that certifies language proficiency. Schools appear on this page only so you can place your own family's calendar. What a tutor should do with these dates is unexciting: hold French at reduced intensity through the heavy IA weeks instead of pausing it, and put the timed paper practice in the quiet months rather than the busy ones.

One practical consequence for in-person sessions. From January of DP2 the useful home session stops being a lesson and becomes a supervised paper: the student writes under time at her own desk while the tutor sits there and does nothing, then they mark it together against the criteria. That is the single strongest argument for home tuition over online in this subject, because the one thing a tutor cannot do through a screen is watch a student write by hand for the duration of a paper and see exactly where she slows down, crosses out, and runs out of time.

sections.heading: Home tuition first, with online and hybrid as honest alternatives
paragraphs: For exam technique in a beginner language, home tuition is the strongest of the three modes and the reason is physical. The papers are handwritten and timed. An IB home tutor in Mumbai sitting at your table can set a paper, watch the student write it, and see the things that never show up in a finished script: that she spent four minutes rereading the first question, that she crossed out a correct answer, that her accents become ambiguous when she rushes, that she stopped looking at the clock after the second page. Booking IB home tuition in Mumbai buys you that observation, and it is not available any other way. This is the whole case for IB DP French ab initio home tuition in Mumbai over a screen.

A home tutor for French ab initio Mumbai families bring in also gets the student's own workspace, which turns out to matter. Marked papers accumulate in one place instead of in a bag. The criteria can stay printed and open on the table through a marking session. The student writes at the desk she will use for every piece of homework for two years, which is where the habit has to live. And a parent passing the room hears whether a session is a lesson or a conversation, which is a cruder check than reading a report and a more honest one.

Online is the better mode for two specific things, and a tutor who denies it is selling rather than teaching. It is better for frequency, because two short midweek slots are bookable online and genuinely impossible in person across this city. It is better for access, because the right beginner-French specialist may live in Thane while you live in Worli. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can also share a screen for live correction more neatly than a paper notebook allows. What online cannot do is supervise a handwritten paper, which is most of what matters from January of DP2 onwards.

So hybrid is what most families should actually ask for, and the split should follow the calendar rather than a preference. Through DP1, online midweek for frequency and one weekend home session for handwritten work. From the middle of DP2, flip it: the in-person session becomes the main event because it is a supervised paper, and online becomes the top-up. Parents comparing IB tutors near me Mumbai listings against online-only options are usually choosing between frequency and supervision, and the correct answer changes halfway through the course.

sections.heading: What should you check in a French ab initio home tutor yourself?
paragraphs: IB Gram checks identity, the components a tutor claims to have taught, and their teaching history with this age group before a profile goes live. For IB DP French ab initio home tuition in Mumbai we also ask a specific question at vetting: describe a mark a beginner lost last year and name the criterion it came from. Tutors who answer that in one sentence have marked real work. Tutors who talk about motivation and confidence have not, and do not get a profile for this subject however fluent their French is.

Your own checks take one session and no French. Ask the tutor to bring the published criteria to the first session and watch whether they use them. Ask them to mark one piece of the student's existing work in front of you and listen for criterion names rather than adjectives. Ask what proportion of sessions will be timed practice by DP2, and be suspicious of an answer below most of them. Ask what they do with work the school is marking, because a tutor may teach, model and mark practice work without limit, but may not write or supply any part of what the student submits as her own, and the honest ones say so before you ask.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, and more so in a subject the student started this year. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. The checkable version of a promise is a description of what the student will be able to do by a named month, which you can hold someone to, and the best IB tutor in Mumbai for your child is whoever gives you that instead of a number. Equally, treat anybody who states a particular university's language requirement from memory as guessing: entry requirements differ by institution and country and are revised between admission cycles, so read them on the university's own admissions pages.

There is one thing to check that families almost never think of. Ask whether the tutor will teach the student to mark her own work. A tutor who marks everything themselves for two years produces a student who cannot tell a good answer from a weak one in an examination hall, which is precisely where no tutor is present. By the second term the student should be scoring her own practice writing against the criteria first, and the tutor should be marking her marking.

sections.heading: Exam technique for a beginner, built in the order the marks come back
paragraphs: Most of an hour of IB DP French ab initio home tuition in Mumbai should be spent on technique rather than on grammar, and the order matters. Start with Paper 1, because it is where technique converts fastest into marks. The sequence a tutor should drill is four steps and it never changes: read the task twice and underline the audience, the purpose and the text type; write the conventions of that text type in the margin in English; plan the content in English in six or seven words per point; then write in French using only structures the student can actually produce. The planning step in English is the one parents query and the one that matters most. A beginner who plans in French plans down to the level of her French and produces an empty answer about nothing. Planning in English lets her decide what to say, then the French becomes a translation problem with known tools, which is a problem she can solve.

The counterpart to that is writing to the task rather than to a memorised model. Students who learn whole paragraphs by heart can be identified from the first line of a script, because the paragraph answers a slightly different question than the one asked and the register does not fit the audience. A memorised passage dropped into a message to a friend reads as a textbook, and the message criterion notices. What is worth memorising is small and portable: ways to open and close each text type, four or five connectives, two ways to give an opinion, a reliable past-tense frame. Those travel to any task. Whole essays do not.

Then the reading paper, where almost all beginner losses come from one habit. The student recognises a word, assumes it means its English lookalike, and answers from the assumption rather than from the sentence. Training against this is boringly concrete: for every answer, point at the words in the text that produced it. If she cannot point, the answer is a guess and gets crossed out. Over a term that single rule moves a reading mark more than any vocabulary programme, because it also forces her to read the question's own wording carefully enough to find those words in the first place.

Listening is the component where the reading time before the audio is worth more than anything during it. Replay is limited, so the first play cannot be spent on comprehension in general. She should arrive at the audio already knowing what each question wants, whether it is a number, a place, a name, a time or a reason, and already holding a guess at the French words that would carry it. Then the first play is for catching those and the second is for the gaps. Finally, self-marking. From the second term the student marks her own practice against the criteria before the tutor does, and keeps a personal list of her own repeated errors, which she reads once before every timed piece as a pre-flight check rather than as a revision resource. A list of ten mistakes she actually makes is worth more than a grammar book, because she will catch three of them herself in the last five minutes of the paper, and those three are marks.
bullets: Underline audience, purpose and text type before writing anything

Memorise openings, connectives and a past-tense frame, never whole essays

sections.heading: What does realistic progress look like in Mumbai home classes?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see a change in process, not in marks. A student four sessions into technique work should be underlining the task before she writes, should be able to tell you what text type she was asked for and why, and should be planning in English on the page where you can see it. Marks usually have not moved yet, because a technique habit takes a few assessments to show up in a score. If the process has not changed in a month, the sessions are being spent on content and that needs saying out loud rather than waiting.

At one term the markers are checkable by a parent who speaks no French at all. Open a marked practice paper. Is there a plan on it, in English? Are there criterion names in the tutor's feedback? Is there a personal error list, with entries in the student's own handwriting rather than the tutor's? Can the student look at two of her own answers and tell you which is the stronger one and why? That last one is the single best predictor of what happens in DP2, and it is the point of teaching self-marking at all.

At one exam cycle, meaning the school's end-of-DP1 assessments, expect the components to move at different speeds and read the pattern rather than the total. Reading usually improves first and most, because the point-at-the-words rule is a fast fix. Writing follows once text types are secure. Listening moves slowest, and for a Mumbai beginner who hears no French between sessions a modest listening result after one year is ordinary rather than a warning sign. A tutor who reports a crisis over the first listening mark has misread the course; one who does not change the between-session habit because of it has misread the student.

The limits, stated plainly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and technique raises the ceiling of what a student's French can score without adding to the French itself. A student who has learnt very little vocabulary will write a well-structured text with very little in it. Tutoring supplies method, marked practice and an outside eye on which criterion is leaking; the six days between sessions remain the student's. Anyone describing it differently is selling confidence rather than teaching a paper.
bullets: Four weeks: process changes first, marks later, and that is normal

sections.heading: Booking IB DP French ab initio home tuition in Mumbai
paragraphs: Bring four things to the first conversation. The school and the DP year. The last two pieces of marked French work with the marks on them, which is the most useful single item and the one most families leave out. The criteria sheet the school has issued, if you have it. And your honest weekday evenings, including the slots already committed to other tuition and to the school bus, because a slot that does not survive a Mumbai Tuesday is not a slot and pretending otherwise wastes a term.

The first session at home is diagnostic and specific. The tutor reads the marked work, sets one short timed piece at the student's own desk, and marks it with her against the criteria rather than for her. By the end you should have in writing which component is being attacked first, which criterion is leaking the most marks, what the between-session habit will be, and what the student should be able to do by a named month. That written note is the thing to measure the arrangement against at four weeks and at the end of term.

What happens next is ordinary. A standing weekly in-person slot, usually ninety minutes once technique work starts involving timed pieces, often with a short online session midweek through DP1 for listening. Reviews at four weeks and each term end against the written plan. If the fit is wrong, one message changes the tutor and the marked work goes across with them. An IB private tutor Mumbai parents book for a weekday evening in Kharghar or Kasarvadavali will cost more in travel terms than the same tutor at a weekend hour, so be realistic about which evenings you are asking for.

On money, no figure appears on this page because tutors set their own and inventing one would be dishonest. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board and level, on how scarce the subject specialism is, on session length and frequency, on whether the tutor travels to you and how far, and on how much of the work is marked between sessions rather than during them. Beginner French is a narrow specialism in this city, so a French ab initio tutor in Mumbai tends to sit above a common subject at the same level. Ask each shortlisted tutor directly, in writing, before the first session, and ask whether marking time is inside or outside the hour.
