faqs.question: What does IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai actually cover in the first session?
faqs.answer: One component, diagnosed properly, rather than a tour of the whole course. A good first session has the student produce a short timed piece on the paper that is losing marks, then mark it herself against the criteria while the tutor marks it separately. Comparing the two judgements shows exactly where her reading of her own work differs from an examiner's. The session should end with a written plan naming the component, the two habits being built, and what she brings next week. IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai that begins with a general chat about ability has wasted an hour.

faqs.question: My daughter answers reading questions from general knowledge. How is that fixed?
faqs.answer: Mechanically, and faster than you would expect. The rule is that nothing goes on the answer line until the words carrying it have been underlined in the passage. For the first two weeks the tutor asks, on every answer, where in the text that came from, and the student has to point. It feels tedious and it retrains the reflex. Within about a month the underlining happens automatically and the general-knowledge answers stop appearing. This is the highest-yield fix in French B reading because the loss is pure technique, not comprehension: she understood the passage perfectly well and answered a different question.

faqs.question: The listening section is where he loses most marks. Can that genuinely be trained?
faqs.answer: Yes, because most listening losses are timing and strategy rather than ear. Three habits do the work: read the questions in the gap before the audio starts so the ear knows its targets, write a partial answer instead of a blank whenever anything was caught, and move on without arguing with the recording when an item is gone. Replay is limited, so a student who stays with one item loses three later ones. Practice also needs plural accents, because French is spoken across Senegal, Belgium, Switzerland, Quebec, Morocco, Haiti and more, and a student fed only one accent is unprepared.

faqs.question: Her written task was fluent and well expressed but scored badly. Why would that happen?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the text type and register did not match the task. A written task names a form and an audience, and a blog post, an email to a host family, a report and a speech each carry conventions a marker is looking for. A student who writes an elegant essay when the task asked for a leaflet loses marks that accurate grammar cannot recover. The fix is three minutes of planning before writing: name the text type, name the audience, fix the register, list three points. Then write to the task rather than to length, because padding costs marks for irrelevance and for the errors padding introduces.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Cuffe Parade for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor is matched inside South Mumbai rather than brought down from the suburbs. Distances on the island are short but the evening peak at Peddar Road and Haji Ali is slow, so a Worli to Cuffe Parade run that looks like fifteen minutes can take forty. Tutors living in Walkeshwar, Tardeo, Worli or Fort hold Cuffe Parade and Colaba slots reliably for two years. A tutor commuting from Andheri or Thane for a 7pm island slot will manage it for a month and then start rescheduling, which is worse for continuity than a slightly different tutor.

faqs.question: What happens at our society gate and building reception when a tutor first arrives?
faqs.answer: Tell us your building's policy when you book, because it decides what the tutor needs on day one. Most Mumbai societies want a photo ID at the gate, an entry in the visitor register, and a resident confirming the visit, either by app approval or a call from reception. Many complexes will issue a standing visitor pass once a weekly slot is established, which removes ten minutes of friction from every session. Tutors carry ID as standard. If your society requires police verification paperwork or a separate approval for repeat visitors, say so upfront and we will confirm the tutor can provide it.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a subject like French B?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not quote a figure because an invented price helps nobody. Level matters, since HL work takes longer to mark than SL. Subject scarcity matters, and French B specialists who have taken students through to examinations are thinner on the ground than Maths or Economics tutors. Travel distance matters, because a tutor crossing Mumbai in the evening peak is giving up more time than one walking across Khar West. Session length and frequency matter, as does whether part of the week runs online. Ask for the structure in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Does online really work for French B, or is home tuition always better?
faqs.answer: Both, for different components, which is why most families end up hybrid. Home tuition is clearly better for the marking conversation and written task work, because two people need to be looking at the same annotated page and the tutor needs to see the student's eye leave the passage. Online is better for listening, where headphone audio beats a laptop speaker in a busy room, and for oral rehearsal, where three short calls a week beat one long session. A reasonable structure is one home session weekly plus two fifteen-minute online calls for listening and speaking.

faqs.question: It has been a month and I cannot see any improvement. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Check for habits rather than marks, because marks at four weeks are noise. Ask to see her last three pieces of work and look for three specific things: is the reading passage underlined before answers are written, is there a short plan above each written task, and can she tell you which band her last piece reached and why. If all three are present, the work is on track and the marks will follow over a term. If none are present, the sessions are being spent on content instead of technique. Raise it with the tutor directly, and if nothing changes within two sessions, ask us to rematch.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help write or tidy up her written task before she submits it?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the text type, explain the criteria, and mark a draft with written comments the student then acts on herself. A tutor may never write, redraft, translate or supply any part of what your child submits. This is not a technicality we are being cautious about; it is an academic honesty boundary, and the consequences land on the student rather than the tutor. Say it out loud in the first session with the student present and it never becomes an awkward question in March. Any tutor who offers more than teaching and marking should be refused the slot.

faqs.question: Can you promise my son a specific French B grade by May?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who does is selling you something they cannot deliver. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, because your son sits the paper and an examiner marks it, and nobody in your living room controls either. What consistent technique work does reliably achieve is converting the French he already has into marks he was previously losing to procedure: answering from the text, finishing the listening section, matching text type to task. That is worth real points on a script. It is a different claim from a predicted number, and the difference matters when you are choosing between tutors.

An IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai is being hired for a specific technical skill, which is marking. sections.heading: Where the assessed writing and the oral sit in French B
paragraphs: French B in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) is assessed through a Paper 1 writing task, a Paper 2 made of listening and reading, and an individual oral. Only two of those three are productive. Paper 2 asks the student to understand French. Paper 1 and the oral ask her to produce it, under time or under questioning, and they are where most of the recoverable marks on this course sit. A home tutor who spends every session on comprehension exercises is working on the half that is easier to teach and harder to improve.

Paper 1 is externally examined. The student receives a task, a text type, an audience and a purpose, and writes by hand. The individual oral is different in kind: it is conducted and assessed internally by the student's own teacher, recorded, and then moderated externally. That internal element is why the oral is the single most schedulable component in the Diploma. Everything else happens when the examination timetable says so. The oral happens when your school says so, which means it can be prepared for with a precise date in mind.

The stimulus differs by level. At Standard Level the oral is built on a visual stimulus linked to one of the course themes: the student is given an image, describes and interprets it in connection with that theme, and then holds a conversation about it. At Higher Level the current guide uses an extract from a literary work studied in class instead. Both then open into general conversation across the course. Confirm the arrangement for your child's cohort with the Diploma Programme coordinator, because the IB revises guides on its own cycle and a page on the internet is not the source of record.

A French B IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai parents engage should treat the oral as a DP1 project rather than a DP2 emergency. The skill it tests, speaking analytically about something unseen while somebody asks follow-up questions, takes months to build and about four days to fake. Families who start image work in the first year arrive at the recording with a student who can think out loud in French. Families who start six weeks out arrive with a student holding a script.

sections.heading: Why is a blog post not the same task as a formal letter?
paragraphs: Because the reader is different, and in French B the reader is half the mark. Give a student the same content, a school trip to Lonavala, and ask for a blog post for her classmates and then a formal letter to the principal about the same trip, and almost nothing should survive the move except the facts. The blog opens with a title and a date, addresses the reader directly, uses tu or vous depending on who is being spoken to, asks a question or two, and invites comments. The letter opens with a formal salutation, holds vous without exception, uses impersonal and passive constructions, states its purpose in the first line and closes with a set formula.

An article is different again: a headline, an opening that makes the reader care, reported speech, statements attributed to people, a third-person stance even when the writer has an opinion. A speech is written to be heard, so it addresses an audience in the room, repeats for effect, asks rhetorical questions, and ends with something that works out loud. A report is organised under headings and prioritises clarity over style. A diary entry is dated, private, and in the first person. An interview alternates question and answer and keeps the two voices distinct.

Students lose marks here in predictable ways. They write a competent piece in no identifiable text type at all. They open a formal letter correctly and drift into tu by the third paragraph. They write a speech that reads like an essay, with no audience anywhere in it. They produce a blog post with no title, no date and no voice. The language in all four cases may be perfectly accurate. The convention marks go anyway, and the student usually has no idea why, because her teacher's comment said the French was good.

The discipline a home tutor should drill is reading the task before writing anything: who is the audience, what is the purpose, what text type is named, and what does that combination require in the first two lines and the last two. Two minutes spent on that before a pen moves is worth more than ten minutes of checking at the end. A good tutor will make your daughter annotate the task itself, in the margin, every single time, until she does it without being told.
bullets: Same content, different reader, almost nothing should carry across.
Formal letter: vous throughout, set opening and closing formulae.
Blog: title, date, direct address, a question, an invitation to respond.
Speech: an audience in the room, repetition, something that lands aloud.

sections.heading: Home tuition for French B in every Mumbai zone
paragraphs: Navi Mumbai is the zone where the home-visit question gets decided fastest, so start there. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are planned nodes, a short drive apart along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 underneath. A French B tutor living in Nerul will happily cover Belapur and Vashi weekly. A French B tutor in Juhu will agree to Kharghar once, enjoy the Atal Setu, and start rescheduling by the fourth week. Node-to-node matching is not a limitation we apologise for. It is the only pattern that survives two years.

Thane behaves the same way with different roads. The city runs west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road out to Kasarvadavali, and Ghodbunder sets every schedule: twenty minutes off-peak, close to an hour in the evening. Thane tutors cover Thane, with occasional crossover from Mulund along the Eastern Express Highway. For families out near Kasarvadavali, a Saturday morning home session plus a short online midweek slot is usually more reliable than a weekday evening that depends on one road behaving.

In Mumbai, Maharashtra proper the pattern is corridor-based. The Western Suburbs hold the deepest French B pool: Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz West and Juhu form one cluster along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, Andheri West, Versova and Oshiwara another, and Malad, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar a third, tied together by Metro Lines 2A and 7 and by Link Road. South Mumbai is short-distance and slow: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Worli, Babulnath and Tardeo, served by the Western and Harbour lines, Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road, with the Bandra-Worli Sea Link bringing suburban tutors as far as Worli before the Peddar Road signals take back the time saved.

The Central Suburbs run on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar. Kurla and Ghatkopar are the easiest nodes to staff. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund are covered by the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) bring in tutors from further away than the distance suggests. Wherever you are, settle the building access question before the first visit rather than during it.

sections.heading: Mumbai school deadlines that decide when the oral happens
paragraphs: Because the individual oral is internally assessed, your school fixes the recording window, and that single date reorganises everything else. Families at Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul are not all recording in the same month. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the window in the first term of DP2, or earlier if your school runs it early, and tell the tutor the moment you have it.

What that date does is convert vague oral preparation into a countable number of sessions. Eight weeks out, the student should be describing unfamiliar images aloud without notes. Four weeks out, she should be doing it with follow-up questions she has not heard before. Two weeks out, under something close to real conditions with a recording running, because hearing yourself back is uncomfortable and necessary. None of that works if the date arrives as a surprise in a corridor conversation.

The written side runs on a different clock. Mocks at most Mumbai IB schools fall in the early months of the calendar year, which is also when the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and a cluster of Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines are due. A DP2 student at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC or Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo carrying two sciences at Higher Level will deprioritise her French writing in exactly that fortnight. The practical response is to front-load timed writing into the quieter months of DP1 rather than to schedule more of it into February.

The monsoon removes evening home classes across the city from June to September, and the families who plan a makeup slot at the point of booking lose almost nothing while the families who improvise lose a month. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of the schools named on this page, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, or with any language-certification body.

sections.heading: Do home classes suit the writing better than online?
paragraphs: For marking, yes, clearly. IB DP French B home tuition in Mumbai lets a tutor sit beside the student with a second pen and annotate a handwritten page while she watches the annotations appear. The student sees where the marker's eye stops. She sees the same correction symbol land three times on one page and understands something that a returned file never conveys. Since Paper 1 is handwritten, practising on paper with a person who marks on paper removes an entire layer of translation.

A home tutor also controls the conditions. A timed task actually gets timed. The phone goes in another room. The student cannot look anything up. That is harder to enforce over a connection, where the tutor has no idea what else is open on the screen. For the oral, being in the room means the tutor can hand over a printed image the student has never seen and start asking questions ten seconds later, which is much closer to the real thing than a shared screen with a loading delay.

What home classes cost you is reach and flexibility. The French B pool is concentrated, so an IB home tutor in Mumbai is far easier to arrange in Khar West than in Panvel, and you are paying for travel time in one currency or another. An IB online tutor in Mumbai solves exactly that, works well for listening and reading, and makes a short midweek session possible when a second house call never would be. The rule for online is simple: writing stays longhand on paper, photographed and marked as an image, because typing hides accents, agreement and the handwriting legibility that a real script depends on.

Most families land on hybrid by the second term: one longer home session for writing and oral rehearsal, one short online session midweek for listening and error drilling. Parents who start by searching "IB tutors near me Mumbai" and expect a map of options usually discover the real constraint is subject scarcity rather than distance. The best IB tutor in Mumbai for your daughter is the one who has marked this course and can reach you every week without heroics. An IB private tutor Mumbai families keep for two years is almost always a local one.

A printed unseen image beats a shared screen for oral practice.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with a draft, and what she may never do
paragraphs: This is the boundary, and it should be stated plainly before anybody starts. A tutor may teach a text type, show a model she has written herself as an example, explain why a construction is wrong, mark a draft against the assessment criteria, annotate it, talk the student through every annotation, and mark the revised version afterwards. A tutor may never write, redraft or supply any part of what the student submits. Not a sentence to be copied out, not a corrected paragraph, not a phrase for the oral handed over to be memorised and presented as the student's own work.

The grey area in practice is correction. Marking a draft and saying that the second paragraph loses the formal register is teaching. Writing the second paragraph correctly in the margin so the student can transcribe it is not, even though it feels like help and even though the student will prefer it. The test is whether the words that reach the examiner originated with the student. If a tutor offers to polish a submission before it goes in, that is not a service, and the right response is to end the engagement and tell us.

Before a profile reaches a parent, each IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai on this platform has had government photo identification verified, the qualification they claim checked, and their French B history examined by component rather than in general terms. References are telephoned. Where a tutor states examining or moderating experience, we ask for specifics. None of this replaces your own checking, which should include asking her to mark a piece of your child's writing in front of you and explain the marks.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade. The oral is recorded and moderated, Paper 1 is marked by somebody nobody in the room has met, and no honest teacher claims to know the outcome. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school, the International Baccalaureate organisation or any language-certification body, and we do not guarantee grades. What a good match reliably buys is fewer marks lost to things that are not knowledge, which is a smaller promise and a true one.
bullets: Allowed: teaching, modelling, annotating, marking and re-marking a draft.
Not allowed: supplying sentences, rewriting sections, scripting the oral.
The test is whether the submitted words originated with the student.

sections.heading: How do you prepare for the individual oral without memorising it?
paragraphs: By rehearsing structures instead of sentences. A memorised oral sounds fluent for ninety seconds and then meets its first follow-up question and stops, because the student has prepared an answer rather than the ability to answer. What survives questioning is a set of reusable moves: a way to open a description, a way to move from what is in the image to what it suggests, a way to concede a point and come back, a way to buy two seconds without switching to English.

Describing a visual stimulus analytically is a trainable skill and most students are never taught it. The weak version lists objects: there is a woman, she is wearing a sari, there are buildings behind. The strong version says what the image is doing. Who is in it and what relationship is implied. Where and when it seems to be set, and what evidence in the image says so. What the photographer chose to include and leave out. What situation it represents in connection with the theme it was chosen for, and whether the student agrees with the view it implies. A tutor should be drilling that order with a different unfamiliar image every week until it becomes automatic.

Then come the follow-up questions, which are where orals are won and lost. The student needs practice being pushed: asked why, then asked why again about her answer, then asked to give an example, then asked whether the opposite might also be true. A home tutor is well placed to do this because she can see when the student is about to give up and keep going anyway. Useful habits include restating the question in French to buy thinking time, saying clearly that she had not considered something and then considering it aloud, and giving a concrete example from her own life in Mumbai rather than a general claim.

Rehearsal that works looks like this: a new image every session, five minutes of unprepared speech, then questions, then two minutes of feedback on language and two on content, then the same image again with the improvements. Record occasionally and make her listen, because students are usually wrong about which bits were weak. What does not work is a written plan she learns, a list of phrases she inserts regardless of relevance, or practising the same three images until she sounds polished on exactly those three. Examiners hear memorisation immediately, and a moderated recording preserves it.
bullets: Rehearse transferable structures, not prepared sentences.
Move from what is in the image to what the image implies.
Name the evidence in the picture for every inference made.
Practise being pushed: why, why again, an example, the counter-case.
A new unfamiliar image every session, then the same one again improved.

sections.heading: Building accuracy from your child's own errors, not a grammar book
paragraphs: Generic grammar drilling is the default because it is easy to plan, and it is mostly wasted. A student does not need every tense revised. She needs the four things she personally gets wrong, repeatedly, in every piece she writes. Those four things are discoverable in twenty minutes from two marked scripts and they are specific to her: the agreement she forgets with a preceding direct object, the preposition she picks by English instinct, the adjective she puts in the wrong position, the tu that appears on the third page of every formal piece.

So the tool is an error log, kept on paper in the house, added to from every marked piece, with a tally beside each entry. The entries are written in her own hand with a correct example she produced herself. Five minutes at the start of each session goes to the top three by tally, not to whatever chapter comes next. An error drops off the list when it has not appeared in three consecutive pieces. This is unglamorous and it is the single highest-return thing a home tutor does, because it attacks marks that are being lost for no reason rather than marks that require new learning.

What that produces, in time: at four weeks, the student starts catching her own errors mid-sentence, which is the first sign anything has changed. At one term, the top errors on the original list have been replaced by subtler ones and her written pieces are recognisably in the right text type. Across a full exam cycle, the gain is almost entirely in marks that were being thrown away rather than in a new level of French. That is a real and substantial improvement, and it is also why we do not guarantee grades and why a tutor who offers a number before meeting the student is telling you about herself.

If the arrangement is not working, say so in week three. The signals are specific on this kind of page: no error log has appeared, no timed writing has been done, the tutor talks more than the student, or the oral practice is the same two images every time. We rematch and ask the outgoing tutor for a handover note so the error log survives the change. Replacing a tutor is routine and nobody needs a case built against anybody.
bullets: Two marked scripts reveal the four errors that actually recur.
Keep a paper error log with a tally, in the student's own handwriting.
Five minutes a session on the top three errors by tally.
An error leaves the list after three clean pieces in a row.
No error log and no timed writing by week three means rematch.

sections.heading: Your first French B home tuition session in Mumbai
paragraphs: French B home classes Mumbai families book should start with work, not with a conversation about the course. Have three things ready: two marked pieces of writing with the teacher's comments still on them, the school's theme list, and the date of the individual oral if the coordinator has given one. If the oral date exists, the whole plan is built backwards from it, and if it does not exist yet, chasing it is the most useful thing you can do this month.

In the session itself, expect a timed written task set on the spot, marked in front of your daughter with the criteria named out loud, and an error log started on paper before the tutor leaves. Expect an unfamiliar image produced from a folder and five minutes of unprepared speech about it, followed by questions she did not see coming. If the hour instead goes on explaining the assessment structure to you, you have your answer about the tutor and you have only spent an hour finding out.

Set the physical arrangement up once. A table, good light, the phone in another room, a printer or at least a scanning app on a phone so written work can be sent for marking between sessions. If your building runs a visitor-pass system, put a standing weekly entry on the register with the society office before session one rather than calling the gate every Tuesday evening. Ten minutes of a paid hour lost at the gate each week adds up to a great deal over two years, and one email prevents it.

Then the pattern holds: one longer home session a week, a short online session midweek if the geography demands it, a file of marked writing you can open at any point, an error log that shortens, and a review at four weeks where you and the tutor say out loud what has changed. Whatever IB tuition fees in Mumbai come to for your match, that review is where you decide whether it is worth continuing, and a good tutor will expect to be asked.
bullets: Bring two marked pieces, the theme list and the oral date.
Expect a timed task marked in front of the student in session one.
Expect one unfamiliar image and five minutes of unprepared speech.
Arrange a standing society gate pass before the first visit.
Book the four-week review at the same time as the first session.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai do about the Paper 1 writing task?
faqs.answer: She sets it, times it, and marks it where your child can see the marking happen. A good IB DP French B home tutor in Mumbai works on the task brief before the writing starts, making the student identify the audience, the purpose and the named text type and annotate them in the margin. Then a timed piece by hand, then annotation against the criteria with each symbol explained aloud, then a rewrite of the weakest section rather than the whole thing. Over a term that cycle repeats across different text types until the conventions stop requiring conscious thought.

faqs.question: What text types could come up in the writing task?
faqs.answer: The course works across a range of them, and the usual suspects are a formal letter, an email, a blog post, an article, a speech, a report, a set of instructions, a diary entry, a brochure or leaflet, an interview and a review. Your school's teacher will be working from the current subject guide, so ask which list the class is using. The practical point is that each one has openings, closings, a person, a register and a layout of its own, and a student who has practised four of them and met a fifth in the exam is improvising conventions she could have learned in twenty minutes.

faqs.question: How do you practise the individual oral without writing a script?
faqs.answer: By practising with material she has never seen. A new unfamiliar image every session, five minutes of unprepared speech, then follow-up questions, then feedback split between language and content, then the same image again done better. What gets rehearsed is structure: how to open a description, how to move from what is shown to what it implies, how to concede and recover, how to buy two seconds in French. Phrases learned by heart and inserted regardless of relevance are audible to an examiner, and the oral is recorded and moderated, so a memorised performance does not pass unnoticed.

faqs.question: My daughter freezes when the examiner asks a follow-up question. What helps?
faqs.answer: Practice at being pushed, deliberately and often. Most students have only ever answered one question per topic, so the second one feels like an attack. The fix is a tutor who asks why, then asks why about the answer, then asks for an example, then asks whether the opposite might be true, every session. Useful habits: restating the question in French to buy thinking time, saying plainly that she had not thought about it and then thinking aloud, and reaching for a concrete example from her own life in Mumbai instead of a general statement. Freezing is a trained-out problem, not a personality trait.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor come to our flat in Kharghar on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes if the tutor is based in Navi Mumbai, and we will tell you honestly if that pool is thin for French B. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur and Panvel are all a short drive from Kharghar along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway. A tutor crossing from Juhu or Bandra over the Atal Setu for a seven o'clock weekday slot will manage it for a few weeks and then start rescheduling, which is worse for the student than a different arrangement would have been. For outer nodes a Saturday morning home session plus a short midweek online slot usually holds for two years.

faqs.question: Where in the home should the session actually happen?
faqs.answer: At a table, in a room with a door that stays open, with the student's phone somewhere else. The dining table is usually better than a study, because a study has a computer in it. You need good light for marking handwritten work and somewhere to spread two papers side by side. Avoid a bedroom. For the oral practice part, a wall without clutter behind the student helps if anything is being recorded. None of this is fussiness: a timed written task done on a sofa with a phone face-down nearby is not a timed written task.

faqs.question: Is the individual oral really marked by her own teacher?
faqs.answer: It is conducted and assessed internally by the school and then moderated externally, which is a meaningful difference from Paper 1. In practice that means the person asking the questions knows your daughter, the recording is reviewed by somebody who does not, and the school's marking can be adjusted. Two consequences follow. First, the date is set by the school, so you can plan backwards from it, which you cannot do with an externally timetabled paper. Second, a performance that sounds memorised is preserved on the recording for the moderator, so rehearsal has to produce fluency rather than recitation.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for French B home tuition?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length. French B is scarce in this city, because the number of teachers who have planned its themes and marked its written tasks is much smaller than the number who teach French, and scarcity moves a rate more than difficulty does. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level. Travel is a real input for home visits: a tutor driving from Khar West to Kharghar is pricing the road as well as the hour. We will not print a figure here, because any number on a page would be wrong for somebody reading it.

faqs.question: Can the tutor correct her draft before she hands it in?
faqs.answer: She can mark it and she cannot rewrite it. Marking means annotating against the criteria, naming the problems, explaining them aloud and marking the revised version afterwards. Rewriting means supplying corrected sentences in the margin for your daughter to copy out, and that crosses the line however helpful it feels at the time. The test is whether the words the examiner reads originated with the student. If a tutor offers to clean a piece up before submission, end the engagement and tell us, because that offer puts the student's whole Diploma at risk rather than just one task.

faqs.question: She knows the grammar rules but keeps making the same mistakes. Why?
faqs.answer: Because knowing a rule and applying it under time pressure are different skills, and generic grammar revision trains only the first. The fix is specific rather than broad: pull her four personal recurring errors out of two marked scripts, write them in an error log in her own handwriting with a correct example she produced, and spend five minutes at the start of each session on the top three by tally. An error leaves the list after three clean pieces in a row. This is far more productive than working through a grammar book she can already recite.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor's commute makes her late on Ghodbunder Road?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens rather than during it. The usual arrangement is that the session still runs for its full length where the household can absorb a later finish, or the missing minutes are added to the next one, and a cancellation with reasonable notice is rescheduled rather than charged. Ghodbunder Road between Majiwada and Kasarvadavali is the most reliable source of this problem in Thane, as the Western Express Highway is in the suburbs. Where a slot keeps slipping, the honest answer is usually a different time or a local tutor, not more apologies.

faqs.question: Does she need different tutors for the oral and the writing?
faqs.answer: No, and splitting them is usually counterproductive. The same errors show up in both, the error log serves both, and the analytical habits built for describing an image feed directly into the opinion sections of written tasks. One tutor who does both sees the whole picture and can shift the weekly balance as the oral date approaches and then back again afterwards. Where a split occasionally makes sense is at Higher Level, if the literary works are genuinely outside a tutor's experience, and in that case we would rather tell you than pretend otherwise.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram match an IB DP French B online tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Matching an IB DP French B online tutor in Mumbai involves one filter that does not apply to home tutoring: can this person run an hour in which she is not the one talking. A great many capable teachers are excellent in a room and become lecturers the moment a screen appears, because silence over a connection feels longer and explaining fills it comfortably. We ask candidates directly how they handle a student who goes quiet, and the answer tells you most of what you need.

The information we need from you is short. The level, the list of themes the school has already covered, one piece of marked writing, and whether the individual oral has been recorded. Then the practical layer: does the student have headphones, a camera and a reliable connection in the room she will use, and at what time of day. A Juhu flat on fibre at four in the afternoon and a Panvel flat on a mobile hotspot at nine at night are different engineering problems, and the honest answer in the second case is sometimes a shorter, more frequent session.

Two or three profiles come back with online French B teaching history attached rather than general tutoring experience, because the two are not the same credential. Then a trial hour, and the test for it is simple enough to apply yourself from the next room. Listen to who is speaking. If your daughter has talked for well under half of it, the tutor is the wrong tutor regardless of how good the explanations were. By the end of that hour a shared document should exist with her recurring errors and the useful phrases she reached for and could not find, and that document is the backbone of everything that follows.

sections.heading: Standard Level, Higher Level and what an online hour should contain
paragraphs: Both levels of French B in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) sit the same three components: a Paper 1 writing task, a Paper 2 built from listening and reading, and an individual oral. Higher Level adds the study of literary works in French, and in the guide currently in use the Higher Level oral is built on a literary extract while the Standard Level oral uses a visual stimulus linked to a theme. Confirm the structure for your child's cohort with the Diploma Programme coordinator, since the IB revises its subject guides on its own cycle.

What matters for online delivery is that three of those four skills transfer cleanly to a connection and one does not. Listening transfers perfectly, because audio plays to both parties at identical quality and the tutor can stop, replay and question in a way that is clumsier in a room. Reading transfers well with a shared screen. Speaking transfers very well indeed, and in some respects improves, since a camera is closer to a recorded oral than a sofa is. Handwritten timed writing is the one that needs a deliberate workaround, and that workaround is dealt with later on this page because it is the main honest objection to online French.

A productive online hour for a French B IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai families book looks roughly like this. A few minutes on the top recurring errors from the shared document. Then authentic audio, played at full speed, with the student summarising in French rather than answering comprehension questions in English. Then the largest block of the hour spent with the student speaking: an image, an argument, a reaction to what she just heard, with the tutor asking follow-up questions and typing corrections into the document while she keeps going. Then a short block of live writing correction. Then the longhand task set for the week.

Notice what is missing from that hour. There is no grammar lecture, because a grammar explanation is something a student can read in five minutes on her own and does not require a scarce French-speaking adult to be present. There is no vocabulary list read aloud. There is no slide deck. Anything that could be sent as a message and read later should be sent as a message and read later, and the hour should be spent on the things that only happen when another person is there.

sections.heading: Why is classroom French easier to follow than the listening paper?
paragraphs: Because a teacher in front of thirty students in Andheri slows down, enunciates, repeats, uses the vocabulary she has just taught, and watches faces for confusion. An authentic recording does none of that. It runs at the speed the speakers actually use, with elision, filler, interruption, regional accent and background noise, and it does not care whether your daughter caught the number in the third sentence. A student can be the strongest in her class and still lose marks on the listening section, and the gap is almost always exposure rather than ability.

This is the part of French B where a Mumbai student is genuinely disadvantaged compared with a student living in a French-speaking city, and it is worth saying rather than glossing over. Hindi, Marathi, English and Gujarati surround her all day. French does not exist outside her timetable. Every hour of French she has ever heard was delivered by a teacher who wanted to be understood. Listening comprehension is built by volume, and volume is the one thing a weekly session cannot supply on its own, which is why an online tutor's most important job may be setting and policing what the student listens to between sessions.

The material should be real and it should be varied. French is spoken as a first language across France, Belgium, Switzerland, Canada, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Haiti, Morocco and many other places, and accent, idiom and speed differ between and within all of them. Language acquisition courses tend to draw their material from a range of French-speaking communities rather than from one country, so a student who has only ever heard one accent is poorly prepared. News bulletins, interview podcasts, documentary clips, short films and series with French subtitles all count, and subtitles in French help far more than subtitles in English.

Reading has the same structure of problem with a gentler slope. Paper 2's reading section uses authentic texts, which in practice means articles, interviews, advertisements, blog posts and public information material rather than graded passages, so the student meets vocabulary nobody taught her and has to work out what a text is for before she can answer anything about it. An online tutor has an advantage here: she can put a text on a shared screen, watch the student's eyes stop, and ask what she just did when she stopped, which is a question that teaches more than the answer to the comprehension item does.
bullets: Classroom French is spoken to be understood; authentic audio is not.
Listening is built by volume, and volume comes from between sessions.

sections.heading: Online and home tuition for French B across Mumbai
paragraphs: The honest case for online French B in Mumbai, Maharashtra is geographic. The experienced French B markers in this city are concentrated in a narrow band: Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz West, Juhu and the South Mumbai pocket around Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Worli, Babulnath and Tardeo. The students are everywhere. A family in Dahisar, Panvel or Kasarvadavali searching for a French B specialist is not short of willing tutors, it is short of tutors who have marked the course, and online is what closes that specific gap without anybody spending two hours on the Western Express Highway.

Work out from the centre and the argument strengthens. In the Western Suburbs a home tutor based in Khar West will cover Bandra West and Santacruz West all year, reach Juhu with patience, and treat Borivali or Dahisar as a Saturday-only proposition even with Metro Lines 2A and 7 and Link Road in play. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali have no station of their own and are reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar along JVLR, so an evening slot there turns on which way the traffic is running. Kurla and Ghatkopar sit on the Central Line and are easier.

In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund are served by the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Freeway and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road doing more for travel times than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, linked by Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1. The Atal Setu has shortened the crossing from the island city, and a weekly crossing for a single evening lesson still rarely lasts two years. Thane runs from the station across Pokhran Road and Majiwada out along Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali, where the evening journey roughly triples.

So the pattern that actually holds across Mumbai is this: home classes where a qualified French B tutor genuinely lives nearby, online where she does not, and hybrid almost everywhere else. Families in Colaba and Bandra West can reasonably expect weekly home tuition. Families in Panvel, Dahisar or Kasarvadavali will usually get a better tutor online than they will get in person, and the right comparison is not online against an ideal home tutor but online against the home tutor who is actually available.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school week that leaves no room for French
paragraphs: Look at a DP2 weekday honestly before deciding how often a tutor should come. A student at Ascend International School in BKC, Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Singapore International School in Dahisar East or JBCN International School in Oshiwara is typically out of the house early, back late, and has travelled through the Western Express Highway or the Central Line at both ends. Add a co-curricular commitment, Creativity Activity Service hours and homework in six subjects, and the available slots for a second language are narrow and late.

This is the practical argument for online that has nothing to do with teaching quality. A thirty-minute online session on a Wednesday is possible. A thirty-minute home visit is not, because nobody travels across Mumbai for half an hour. Frequency matters more than duration for language retention, so two shorter contacts in a week usually beat one long one, and online is the only format in which the shorter contact is viable. Families at Billabong High International School, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East, Podar International School, Witty International School and Ryan Global School run exactly this pattern for the same reason.

The annual calendar then adds its own pressure. Mocks at most Mumbai IB schools land in the early months of the calendar year, alongside the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and a run of Internal Assessment (IA) deadlines, and the individual oral is recorded in a window each school fixes for itself. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for that window early, because it is the one date in the Diploma you can plan backwards from, and an online tutor can increase contact in the weeks before it without needing anybody to be anywhere.

The monsoon from June to September is the final argument. Evening home tuition in Mumbai gets cancelled in those months, often at short notice, while an online session runs through almost all of it as long as the connection holds. Families who keep an online slot alive year-round, even alongside a home tutor, lose far fewer weeks. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, or with any language-certification body.

sections.heading: Should you book online, a home tutor, or both in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition remains the default service and for many families it is the right answer. A home tutor marks handwritten work on paper with a second pen while the student watches, enforces exam conditions properly, hands over a printed unseen image for oral practice with no loading delay, and builds the kind of relationship that makes a sixteen-year-old turn up willingly on a Tuesday in August. If a qualified French B teacher lives within a reasonable distance of you, book her. Nobody at IB Gram will argue you out of it.

The case for an IB DP French B online tutor in Mumbai starts where that availability ends. It also starts where a family wants frequency rather than length, or where the student needs a different kind of hour. Online removes the thing that eats home sessions, which is travel, and converts it into contact time. It makes a second weekly slot affordable in time if not always in money. It gives access to markers who would never drive to Panvel. For a subject where the student's problem is almost always too little practice rather than too little instruction, more frequent contact is a real advantage.

The trade-offs should be stated rather than smoothed over. Handwriting needs the workaround described below. A student who is already disengaged is easier to lose on a screen than in a room, so for a reluctant fifteen-year-old a home tutor is usually the better first move. Connections fail, usually in the monsoon, usually at seven in the evening. And a tutor who cannot resist explaining will do more damage online than in person, because there is nothing in a video call to interrupt a monologue.

Hybrid is where most families finish. One longer home session a week for writing, marking and oral rehearsal, and one short online session midweek for listening and speaking. Parents who begin by typing "IB tutors near me Mumbai" into a search box, or looking for a home tutor for French B Mumbai agencies advertise, usually arrive here once the geography is clear. The best IB tutor in Mumbai for your daughter is the one who has marked this course and can show up reliably, and an IB private tutor Mumbai families keep for two full years is usually the one whose format made that easy.
bullets: Book home tuition when a qualified French B teacher lives nearby.
Online buys frequency, reach and the time otherwise lost to traffic.
A disengaged student is usually easier to hold in a room.
Hybrid: a weekly home session plus a short midweek online slot.
Keep an online slot alive through the monsoon regardless of format.

sections.heading: Checking an online tutor you will never meet in person
paragraphs: Every tutor on this platform has had government photo identification verified and the qualification they claim checked before any profile is shown, and their French B history is examined by component rather than in general terms: which year groups, which level, which themes, which written text types, how many cohorts through the individual oral. References are telephoned, not accepted as uploaded letters. For online work we also ask a practical question that sounds trivial and is not: how do you share audio, and what do you send the family after a session.

Your own checking should be different from ours and it is more useful. Ask for a trial hour and listen from the next room to who is speaking. Ask to see the shared document after that hour and look at whether it contains her errors or the tutor's notes. Ask what she sends after each session, because a tutor who writes three lines on what was covered and what the week's task is has a system, and one who sends nothing is relying on your daughter's account of her own lesson. Ask her to mark a piece of handwritten work from a photograph and show you the marked version.

There is one boundary that a shared document makes easier to cross than a notebook does, and it is worth agreeing out loud in the first week. A tutor may teach, model, explain, annotate and mark. A tutor may never write, redraft or supply any part of what the student submits. In a live document the temptation is for the tutor to simply type the correct sentence into the student's draft, which is faster for both of them and crosses the line. The rule we ask tutors to work to is that the tutor comments and the student edits, always, and that any model text the tutor writes lives in a separate part of the document from the student's own work.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade. Paper 1 is marked by somebody nobody in this arrangement has met and the oral is moderated externally, so there is no honest basis for the claim. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school, the International Baccalaureate organisation or any language-certification body, and we do not guarantee grades. What good online teaching reliably buys is more speaking practice per week than the student could get any other way in this city.
bullets: Photo ID, qualification and component-level French B history verified.
Listen to the trial hour from the next room and count who speaks.
Ask what written note arrives after every session.
In a shared document the tutor comments and the student edits.

sections.heading: Who should be talking in an online French session?
paragraphs: The student, for most of the hour, and if that is not happening nothing else about the arrangement matters. This is the single biggest difference between online French tuition that works and online French tuition that fills a slot in the week. A Mumbai student taking French B gets almost no speaking practice anywhere else in her life. The session is not where French gets explained to her. It is where she produces it, badly at first, under correction, for as long as the hour allows.

The failure mode is predictable and it looks responsible from the outside. A screen appears, slides go up, the tutor explains the subjunctive clearly and patiently in English, the student nods, the parent walking past hears a competent lesson, and sixty minutes pass in which the student has said perhaps forty words. The tutor is not lazy. Silence over a connection is uncomfortable, the explaining reflex is strong, and a student who answers in three words rewards the adult who fills the gap. What breaks the pattern is a tutor who asks a question and then simply waits, who refuses to translate, and who keeps a rough sense of the ratio in her head.

Live correction in a shared document is the mechanism that makes a talking-heavy hour workable. While the student speaks, the tutor types the broken phrase and the repaired version into the document without interrupting her. Flow survives, the correction is captured in writing rather than evaporating, and the last few minutes of the session are spent going back through what accumulated. Over a term that document becomes two things: a list of recurring errors with a tally beside each, and a phrase bank of the things she kept reaching for and could not find. She opens the same file while doing homework, which is why it has to be shared rather than sitting in the tutor's notebook.

Prompts that force production work better than conversation topics. Summarise this clip in French, now summarise it again in half the time. Describe this image and then defend an opinion about it. Argue the opposite of what you just said. Retell this article as if you were explaining it to a friend in Dadar. Read this paragraph aloud and then say it again in your own words. Then follow-up questions, repeatedly, because the oral is a conversation under pressure and the only way to prepare for being pushed is to be pushed. Video suits this particularly well: the camera makes it feel assessed, the session can be recorded for her to listen back to, and an image can be put on screen at the moment it is needed.
bullets: The student should be speaking for most of the hour, every hour.
A patient English explanation is the most common way an hour is wasted.
The tutor types the correction while the student keeps talking.
The shared file holds recurring errors with a tally and a phrase bank.
Prompts that force production beat open conversation topics.

sections.heading: The handwriting problem, and what progress actually looks like
paragraphs: Here is the honest counterweight to everything above. The written papers are handwritten, and a student who has done all her French B writing in a shared document for two years will sit Paper 1 with no idea how much she can produce by hand under time, no habit of planning on paper, and accents she has been getting right because software was helping. Typing hides agreement errors, fixes accents, flags spelling and removes the physical constraint. None of that is available in the examination hall.

The workaround is not complicated and it is not optional. Every week the student writes at least one full task longhand, on paper, timed, with no device in reach. She photographs the pages and sends them. The tutor marks the photograph, annotating the image itself rather than retyping the content, and returns it. That cycle keeps handwriting speed, legibility, planning habits and unassisted accent use alive while everything else runs online. Where a family also has a home tutor, the longhand task is the obvious thing to do in the home session and the online hour can go almost entirely to speaking and listening.

Progress on this arrangement is measurable in ways that home tuition is not, which is one of its quiet advantages. At four weeks, the shared document should hold a real error list with tallies, the student should be speaking for most of each session rather than a third of it, and she should be managing a few minutes of authentic audio without asking for a replay. At one term, the top errors from week one should have been displaced by subtler ones, her listening stamina should have grown noticeably, and her handwritten tasks should be arriving complete rather than unfinished.

Across a full exam cycle the realistic gain is in marks that were being lost to things other than knowledge: the unfinished second half of a task, the listening question missed because she was still writing the previous answer, the oral that ran out of material after two minutes, the tense that was wrong in every paragraph. That is a substantial and honest improvement. It is not a guarantee, we do not offer one, and a tutor who names a number before meeting your daughter is describing her sales process rather than your daughter. If the match is wrong, tell us in week three and we rematch with a handover note so the shared document carries over.
bullets: Typing hides accents, agreement and spelling; the paper does not.
One full longhand task a week, timed, photographed and marked as an image.
Four weeks: measurable speaking time and a populated error list.
One term: listening stamina grows and tasks arrive finished.
Rematch with a handover note so the shared document survives.

sections.heading: Starting online French B tuition in Mumbai, and when to add home classes
paragraphs: Setting up well takes twenty minutes and saves a term. Headphones rather than laptop speakers, because the listening work is the point and speaker audio in a Mumbai flat with a fan running is not usable. A camera at roughly eye level, because oral practice over video is closer to the real recording condition than a laptop pointed at a ceiling. A table, good light, the phone in another room, and loose paper and a pen within reach at all times. A scanning app so a handwritten page reaches the tutor as a clean image rather than a dark photograph taken at an angle.

For the first session, have the theme list, one piece of marked writing and the oral date if your school has fixed one. Expect the tutor to spend the hour making your daughter speak, not explaining the course to you. Expect a shared document to exist by the end of it, containing her own errors in her own words and the phrases she reached for and missed. Expect a longhand task set for the week. If instead the hour is a presentation, you have learned what you needed and it cost you one hour.

French B home classes Mumbai families add to an online arrangement usually come later and for a specific reason: a student who needs somebody physically present to enforce timed writing, a Higher Level literary text that goes better with printed pages across a table, or an oral date approaching where the student wants to rehearse with a person rather than a window. IB home tuition in Mumbai and an online slot are not competing products, and the tutor who runs the online hour can often be the one who comes to the house, which is a further reason to prefer a tutor based in this city.

After the first month the review is the thing that matters. Sit down with the shared document open and ask three questions: is she speaking for most of each session, has the error list changed, and are the longhand tasks arriving finished. Whatever IB tuition fees in Mumbai come to for your match, that conversation is where you learn whether the arrangement is earning its place, and any tutor worth keeping will want to have it.
bullets: Headphones, a camera at eye level, paper and a pen always in reach.
A scanning app so handwritten pages arrive as clean images.
Bring the theme list, one marked piece and the oral date.
Add home classes when timed writing needs somebody in the room.
Review at four weeks with the shared document open in front of you.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP French B online tutor in Mumbai do in a typical hour?
faqs.answer: A good IB DP French B online tutor in Mumbai spends the hour making the student produce French rather than receive it. A few minutes reviewing recurring errors from the shared document, authentic audio played at full speed with the student summarising it in French, then the largest block of the hour on speaking: an image, an argument, a reaction, with follow-up questions and corrections typed into the document while she keeps talking. Then live correction of a piece of writing, and a longhand task set for the week. Grammar explanations get sent as a message to read later rather than delivered live.

faqs.question: Does online French tuition actually work if my son never speaks French outside class?
faqs.answer: It works precisely because of that, provided the sessions are built around him talking. The reason a Mumbai student struggles with French B is almost never that nobody explained the grammar. It is that he has nowhere to use the language, so half-learned rules never get corrected by exposure and speaking stays effortful. An online session is the cheapest way to add a second contact in the week, and two shorter sessions beat one long one for retention. What it cannot do by itself is supply listening volume, which is why the audio he works through between sessions matters as much as the sessions do.

faqs.question: How do you handle handwritten practice when the sessions are online?
faqs.answer: One full task a week is written longhand on paper, under time, with no device within reach, then photographed and sent. The tutor marks the image itself rather than retyping the content, so your son sees annotations on his own handwriting. This is not a nice extra. Paper 1 is handwritten, and a student who has composed everything in a document for two years will not know his own writing speed, will have planned nothing on paper, and will have been getting accents right because software supplied them. A scanning app makes the photographs legible enough to mark properly.

faqs.question: What should he be listening to between sessions?
faqs.answer: Authentic French at normal speed, varied in accent, for fifteen minutes most days rather than an hour once a week. News bulletins, interview podcasts, documentary clips, short films and series with French subtitles all work, and French subtitles help considerably more than English ones. Vary the source: French is spoken as a first language in France, Belgium, Switzerland, Canada, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Haiti, Morocco and elsewhere, and the course material tends to be drawn from a range of those communities. The tutor should be setting specific clips and then asking him to summarise them in French, otherwise the listening quietly stops happening.

faqs.question: Can we switch to a home tutor later if online is not working?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a fair number of families do, usually in one of two situations. A student who is disengaged is easier to hold in a room than on a screen, and a student who will not do timed writing without somebody present needs that person present. Where a qualified French B tutor lives near you we will say so at the matching stage rather than waiting for you to ask. The switch is straightforward: same shortlist process, and we ask the online tutor for a handover note so the shared error document carries across rather than restarting from nothing.

faqs.question: Is online cheaper, and what do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Often somewhat, because nobody is paying for travel, but the main inputs are the same: board, level, subject scarcity, travel where it applies, and session length. French B is at the scarcer end in this city, since the number of teachers who have planned its themes and marked its written tasks is far smaller than the number who teach French, and scarcity moves a rate more than format does. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level. We will not print a figure, because a number on a page would be wrong for somebody reading it next month.

faqs.question: Our building has poor internet in the evening. Does that rule online out?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but test it before committing to a slot rather than discovering it in week two. Run a video call at the exact time of day you intend to book, in the exact room, with everything else in the flat running as it normally would. If it holds, book it. If it does not, the usual fixes are a different hour, a mobile hotspot as a standing backup, or a shorter session in the afternoon rather than at nine at night. Where nothing holds reliably, a home tutor is the better answer and we will tell you so.

faqs.question: Can the individual oral be practised properly over video?
faqs.answer: Video suits it unusually well. The camera makes the exchange feel assessed in a way a living room does not, the tutor can put an unfamiliar image on screen at the moment it is needed, and the session can be recorded so the student hears herself back, which is uncomfortable and more instructive than any feedback. What matters more than the format is the content of the rehearsal: unfamiliar material every time, genuine follow-up questions, and structures practised rather than sentences memorised. A memorised oral is audible to an examiner and the recording preserves it for the moderator.

faqs.question: How do I know the tutor is not just talking at him for an hour?
faqs.answer: Listen from the next room for ten minutes and count who is speaking. That single check tells you more than any report. If the tutor is explaining in English for long stretches, the hour is being spent on something your son could have read in five minutes. Then look at the shared document: it should be full of his errors and his missing phrases, not the tutor's notes on grammar. Ask him what he said in the session rather than what he learned. A student who can describe what he talked about has been talking.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during an online session?
faqs.answer: Not throughout, but be in the flat for the first two or three and keep the door open. You are checking three things, none of which require you to understand French: that the student is doing most of the speaking, that the session starts on time, and that written work is accumulating somewhere you can see it. After that the shared document and the weekly note from the tutor tell you more than sitting nearby would. Keep the session out of a bedroom and out of reach of a television, and keep his phone in a different room.

faqs.question: Is a tutor in another city better than one based in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Sometimes on paper, rarely in practice. A Mumbai-based tutor knows how the local school calendars run, knows when the mock and Internal Assessment crunch lands, and can convert to home sessions when the oral approaches or when a student stops engaging on screen. Those are real options that disappear with distance. If a tutor elsewhere has genuinely better French B marking experience and the student is working well, the case is reasonable. We would still rather match you locally first and tell you honestly when the Mumbai pool cannot supply what your child needs.

faqs.question: Can the tutor type corrections directly into her assignment?
faqs.answer: No, and in a shared document this needs saying explicitly because it is so easy to do. A tutor may comment, annotate, explain, mark against the criteria and write a model text of her own in a separate section. She may not type a corrected sentence into the student's draft for her to keep, rewrite a paragraph, or supply phrasing for the oral to be memorised and presented as the student's own. The rule we ask tutors to follow is that the tutor comments and the student edits. If a tutor offers to clean up a submission, end it there and tell us.

sections.heading: How IB Gram shortlists an IB DP french b private tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: A search for an IB DP french b private tutor in Mumbai almost always has a specific trigger behind it. A Paper 2 mock came back well below the predicted grade. The individual oral happened and the student froze after the first thirty seconds. A DP1 report said the student was coping, without saying how, and the parent could not tell whether that meant fine or barely. The first thing we ask for is that trigger in your own words, because it decides what kind of teacher should take the case. A student who understands spoken French but cannot produce written French under timed conditions needs a different tutor from one who has never properly learned how the tense system behaves.

The second thing we ask is where you are and when a session can realistically happen. A French B specialist is a narrower pool than a Maths or Physics tutor, so geography carries more weight on this page than it would on one about Chemistry. Matching a tutor who lives in Khar West to a family in Khar West produces a standing 6.30pm slot that survives a full term. Matching the same tutor to Kharghar produces a Palm Beach Road drive that works for three weeks and then quietly falls apart. We would rather say that on the first call than place someone who cannot hold the schedule once the monsoon or the exam season arrives.

The third is level and intention. French B at Higher Level, with two literary works sitting behind the individual oral, is a different brief from French B at Standard Level taken by a student who wants a solid grade without it eating the hours that Physics needs. So we ask which course the school has placed the student in, whether a change is being discussed at home, and what the school's languages coordinator has actually said rather than what the family has inferred. Placement is the school's decision, taken with the family, and a good tutor's job is to make the chosen course work, not to campaign for a different one.

Only after those three answers do we look at people. The shortlist stays short on purpose: two or three profiles that genuinely fit, rather than a long list that makes the parent do the filtering. Here is the sequence end to end.

sections.heading: French B, French ab initio or a different language: who decides?
paragraphs: Three routes exist for French inside the Diploma Programme (DP). French B is designed for a student who has already studied the language, usually across several years of the Middle Years Programme (MYP) or an IGCSE course. French ab initio is designed for a genuine beginner and is offered at Standard Level (SL) only. The third route is a different language entirely, or in some schools a second Language A. Which of the three a student takes is decided by the school together with the family, on the basis of the student's real prior learning rather than on which course looks easiest from outside.

Families sometimes read ab initio as the soft option and ask to be moved into it for a cleaner grade. It is not the easy-score route. Ab initio takes a student from nothing to assessed performance inside two years, which is a steep slope in its own right, and a student who already has real French does not belong in it. Schools check for exactly that, because the course is meant to match the starting point. A child who has studied French since Grade 6 will find ab initio an uncomfortable fit even though the vocabulary list looks shorter, and the school will usually say no for good reason.

A French B IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai families shortlist should treat both years as one arc, because whatever DP1 leaves unfinished, DP2 pays for with interest. The window for changing a language sits early. Most Mumbai schools will consider a move during the first term of DP1 and close it well before the second year opens, since the oral work and the reading built into the course cannot be rebuilt from scratch late. If a change is genuinely on the table, put it to the coordinator in writing early in DP1, with the student's prior French set out plainly, rather than waiting for the first full set of mocks to make the argument for you.

Students in Mumbai, Maharashtra frequently arrive at French B already running three or four languages between home, school and the autorickshaw queue, and that is an advantage rather than a complication. A child who moves between Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati and English across a single day already has the habit of holding two grammars in the head at once, which is most of what a third or fourth language asks for. French B also asks them to read across French-speaking cultures that include France, Belgium, Switzerland, Canada, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Haiti and Morocco. No one of those varieties of French is more correct than another, and a tutor who implies otherwise is teaching snobbery rather than language.
bullets: French B assumes prior learning; ab initio assumes a genuine beginner
Ab initio is a Standard Level (SL) course and is not a shortcut to a 7
Placement follows the student's actual prior French, school and family deciding
The practical change window is the first term of DP1, not DP2
A second Language A is a separate conversation with the coordinator
Multilingual students usually gain ground in a third or fourth language

sections.heading: What Paper 1, Paper 2 and the individual oral actually ask for
paragraphs: French B is assessed through a Paper 1 writing task, a Paper 2 that covers listening and reading, and an individual oral. Paper 1 asks the student to produce one piece of writing in a specified text type for a specified audience, and this is where strong classroom students most often lose marks they did not expect to lose. A blog entry, a formal letter, a set of instructions and a speech are not the same object with different vocabulary. Each carries conventions: how it opens, how it addresses the reader, whether it may use the first person, how it signs off. A good French B tutor in Mumbai will make the student write three text types badly and then fix them, rather than lecturing about registers in the abstract.

Paper 2 is the half that rewards volume of exposure. The listening component is unforgiving in a way practice papers alone do not fix, because speed and accent variation are the real difficulty rather than vocabulary. A student who has only ever heard the teacher's French and one set of recordings will struggle the first time a speaker from Dakar, Brussels or Montreal appears. The reading component punishes students who answer from the gist instead of locating the line that carries the answer. Both improve with a weekly routine of short, timed exposure rather than with a cram the fortnight before mocks.

The individual oral is the component families understand least and worry about most. At Higher Level it is built on an extract from one of the literary works studied, which is the element that genuinely separates HL from SL. At Standard Level it is built on a visual stimulus connected to the themes of the course. In both cases the student presents and then holds a conversation that follows on from what they said, so an answer memorised word for word is a liability: the follow-up question is where a rehearsed speech collapses. Structures, durations and the exact format are revised by the International Baccalaureate on its own cycle, so confirm the current shape with your school's coordinator or the current subject guide rather than with any page on the internet, including this one.

One boundary matters more than any technique. A tutor may teach, model, question, drill and mark. A tutor may not write or supply any part of a piece the student submits, in whole or in part, and no reputable French B teacher will offer to. If a student hands in prose that is not theirs, the problem is no longer a grade problem.
bullets: Paper 1: one writing task, a named text type, a named audience and purpose
Text-type conventions: openings, address, register, sign-off, all markable
Paper 2 listening: speed and accent range beat vocabulary as the real obstacle
Paper 2 reading: find the line that answers, do not answer from the gist
Individual oral: HL works from a literary extract, SL from a visual stimulus
Confirm current component structure with the school, not with a blog
