sections.heading: What can a home tutor do on the report, and what is off limits?
paragraphs: A tutor may teach the framework, explain the criteria, question the choice of issue, discuss the concepts, and comment on a draft the student has written. A tutor may never write, redraft or supply any part of the report, draft a paragraph for the student to adapt, or hand over a model report to work from. That boundary is not a house style. The IB treats work that is not the student's own as malpractice, the consequences land on the student rather than on the tutor, and a tutor who blurs it is exposing your child to a risk you did not agree to.

In practice the line is easy to apply once stated. Asking the student which concept the paragraph is using is teaching. Writing the sentence that uses it is not. Marking a draft against the criteria and explaining why a section sits in a lower band is teaching. Rewriting the section so it sits higher is not. Pointing out that a perspective is missing is teaching. Naming what that perspective would say in words the student then copies is not. Every tutor on IB Gram is briefed on this, and an IB private tutor Mumbai families keep for two years is one who refuses politely and often.

On the platform side, verification covers government photo identification, evidence of the qualifications claimed, and references that can be contacted. On your side, ask four things. Have you supervised a Global Politics engagement report through to submission? How do you mark a draft without writing in it? Can you hold this weekly slot for a full term? And how do you handle a student whose political views differ from your own? The right answer to the last one is that the tutor marks the argument and not the conclusion and keeps their own politics out of the session entirely.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, quotes a success rate, offers a sample report to adapt, or claims examiner status without naming the board and the years. Also be wary of anyone who encourages your child to arrange an engagement with a political organisation, campaign or protest outside the school's approval process. An IB DP global politics home tutor in Mumbai has no standing to authorise any of that, and the only correct response to a question about participation is to send the family back to the school.

sections.heading: Which activity and which issue can your child genuinely analyse?
paragraphs: Start from what the student can actually do, within the school's rules, in the weeks available, and work backwards to the issue. Ambition is the usual trap. A student who proposes something they cannot arrange spends two months not arranging it and then writes a report on whatever happened instead. The test for an activity is whether it will put the student in contact with a real disagreement between people with different interests, because a disagreement is what the analysis needs. A simulation where delegates defend assigned positions, an interview with someone responsible for allocating a constrained public resource, or structured volunteering through the school's service programme all do that.

The test for the issue is narrowness plus contestability. It must be something about which reasonable people disagree for reasons that can be set out fairly, and small enough that one report can test it. Access to a shared water supply in a defined area, how a civic body prioritises waste collection between neighbourhoods, whether a non-binding international agreement changes what states do, or how a school community decides between competing claims on a common facility are all workable. Each one lets a student ask who holds power here, whose claim is treated as legitimate, who is dependent on whom, and what justice would require, which is exactly the analytical vocabulary the course is testing.

Linking the experience to the theory is the part that has to be planned before the activity rather than afterwards. A student who knows in advance that they will be looking for competing readings of the same situation takes different notes. Write down, before the engagement, which two or three concepts are likely to be useful and what evidence would count for or against each. Afterwards, the report should set out how at least two perspectives understand the same facts, attributing each view to whoever holds it rather than endorsing or dismissing it, and only then reach a judgement. Attribution is what converts an opinion into evidence, and it is the single most reliable way out of the middle bands.

Two further rules save trouble. Keep the description of what happened short, because the marks are not there, and resist the temptation to make the report dramatic. And on safety and participation, follow the school rather than any instinct of your own: the school decides what engagement is appropriate, what supervision applies and what consent is needed, and a student should not arrange involvement with a political organisation, campaign or protest independently of it. A report built on a school-approved activity is both safer and easier to evidence than one built on something arranged privately.

sections.heading: How long does the engagement report actually take?
paragraphs: Plan on a full term of calendar time and a modest number of working hours spread across it, which is the opposite of how most students approach it. A realistic sequence runs like this: one or two sessions to settle the issue and the activity, a gap of several weeks while approval and arrangements happen, the engagement itself, then a session to turn notes into an analytical plan, a first full draft written by the student, a session marking that draft against the criteria, a redraft, and a final check. The gaps are not wasted time. They are when reading happens.

At four weeks into tutoring, judge the process rather than the mark. The student should have a defined issue, a confirmed activity with the school's approval, a written plan naming the concepts in play, and a page of notes that record competing views rather than impressions. A student who has all four in four weeks is in good shape even with nothing drafted. A student with a long unfocused reading list and no decision has made no progress, and that is a conversation to have with the tutor now rather than in December.

At one term, there should be a complete draft the student wrote, marked against the criteria, with specific written feedback the student can act on. Expect the first draft to be weaker than anyone hoped and heavily descriptive, because almost all first drafts are. Across a full examination cycle the report is one component among several, and improvement in it tends to pull Paper 2 essays up with it because the thinking transfers. An IB tutor Mumbai parents trust will tell you which of those is moving and which is not.

On limits: we do not guarantee grades, we will not predict one, and no tutor on the platform is allowed to promise an outcome. If the match is wrong, the signals are the usual ones, no written feedback, a tutor who talks through the hour, or a draft that is somehow improving without the student writing more. Tell us in week four. We shortlist again in your zone with the reason recorded, and a replacement partway through report work is normal enough that we keep the handover brief and factual.

faqs.question: What exactly is the Global Politics engagement project?
faqs.answer: It is an engagement with a political issue through an activity the student undertakes, plus a written analytical report on that issue which uses the experience as evidence. Both Higher Level and Standard Level students complete it. The report is assessed on analysis rather than on how interesting the activity was, which is the detail most families miss until the first mark comes back. Component names and requirements are revised on the IB's own cycle, so confirm the current format with your child's subject guide and the school's diploma coordinator before planning anything around it.

faqs.question: How do we choose an activity our child can actually do?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from what can realistically be arranged within the school's rules and the weeks available. School-mediated options are usually strongest: a model United Nations conference run through school, a structured interview arranged with the school's knowledge, a simulation, volunteering through the school's service programme, or attending a public lecture followed by applied work. The test is whether the student will encounter a real disagreement between people with different interests, because that disagreement is what the analysis needs. An ambitious activity nobody can arrange costs two months and produces a weaker report than a modest one completed in September.

faqs.question: Should our child get involved with a campaign or an organisation for this?
faqs.answer: Not independently. What engagement is appropriate, what supervision applies and what consent is needed are decisions for the school, and a student should not arrange involvement with any political organisation, campaign or protest outside the school's approval process. Ask the coordinator what is permitted before committing to anything, and route any proposal through whatever approvals process the school runs. Tutors on IB Gram are briefed to send participation and safety questions straight back to the school rather than advising on them. School-approved activities are also easier to evidence in the report, which is a practical benefit alongside the obvious one.

faqs.question: What should we sort out at the society gate before the first session?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a recurring entry rather than as a new visitor every week. Ask your building office whether they issue a standing weekly pass for a service provider and give them the tutor's name, identification number and the fixed day and time in advance. Tutors expect to share photo identification for the register. Settle parking as well, since a dispute at the gate is the commonest reason a session starts twenty minutes late. For report work, choose a table with room for printed drafts and a parent within earshot rather than in the discussion.

faqs.question: How much can the tutor help with the written report?
faqs.answer: They can teach the framework, explain the criteria, challenge the scope of the issue, discuss which concepts apply and comment on a draft your child has written. They cannot write, redraft or supply any part of it, cannot draft a paragraph for your child to adapt, and cannot hand over a model report. The IB treats work that is not the student's own as malpractice and the consequences fall on the student. In practice the distinction is simple: asking which concept a paragraph uses is teaching, and writing the sentence that uses it is not.

faqs.question: Our child wrote a report that just describes what happened. Can it be fixed?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and in one redraft, provided time remains. The repair is structural rather than cosmetic. Cut the narration down to a short factual passage, identify the two or three course concepts the material actually supports, and rebuild the body so each section applies a concept to evidence from the engagement. Then add the competing perspective properly, attributing it to whoever holds it, and finish with a judgement that answers the obvious objection. The student does all the writing. A tutor marks the existing draft against the criteria and shows where the bands change, which is what makes the redraft targeted rather than hopeful.

faqs.question: How narrow does the political issue need to be?
faqs.answer: Narrow enough that a single report could reasonably test it, and contestable enough that reasonable people disagree about it for reasons that can be stated fairly. Inequality is a library. How a civic body prioritises waste collection between two neighbourhoods, or whether a non-binding agreement changes what signatories actually do, are issues. The narrowing conversation usually takes most of a session and saves weeks later. A good check is whether the student can say in one sentence who disagrees with whom and why, without using the word everyone.

faqs.question: Will the tutor's own politics come into the sessions?
faqs.answer: No. The brief on IB Gram is that a tutor teaches the analysis, marks the argument rather than the conclusion, and keeps personal political views out of the room entirely. For this component that is practical rather than principled: a student who learns to perform agreement with a tutor loses exactly the marks the course awards for fair treatment of competing perspectives. A tutor will ask your child to state a view they reject in its strongest form and will challenge an unevidenced claim whichever direction it points. If a tutor editorialises, tell us and we will shortlist again.

faqs.question: We are starting late. Is there still time for the report?

If nothing has been arranged, the honest answer is that the choice of activity narrows to whatever can be organised immediately, which usually means a school-run option, and the report will be built on thinner material. What is defensible is the mechanism: clearer scope, concepts chosen before the engagement rather than after, a draft marked against the criteria the cohort is assessed on, and a redraft the student writes acting on that feedback. Students who do the writing between sessions usually improve. Students who attend and write nothing usually do not. sections.heading: Standard Level and Higher Level: where Global Politics sits in the IB Diploma Programme
paragraphs: Global Politics is a Group 3 individuals and societies subject in the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme, which means a Mumbai student usually takes it alongside two sciences or a science and a mathematics course, a language, and the core of Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and creativity, activity, service. Students meet it for the first time in DP1, because very few Mumbai schools run anything resembling it at Middle Years Programme (MYP) level. That matters for tutoring: there is no prior subject to build on, only general literacy and whatever the student has picked up from reading.

The course is organised around a set of key concepts, the course's own analytical vocabulary, and around thematic content. The concepts are the part that students underestimate. Words such as sovereignty, legitimacy, interdependence, power and development are not decoration in this subject; they are the tools an examiner expects to see used precisely, and a student who uses them loosely loses marks that have nothing to do with how much they know. A tutor's first job in DP1 is usually to make the student define these terms in their own words and then apply them to a case that has nothing emotional attached to it.

The split between Standard Level and Higher Level is structural rather than a matter of difficulty per topic. Higher Level adds an extension strand studied in more depth and assessed through presentations, so an HL student carries an additional workstream through DP2 that an SL student does not. Where a family is undecided, the honest answer is that the decision belongs with the school's DP coordinator, who knows the timetable blocks and the student's other five subjects. Do not take a structural decision on the strength of a tutor's opinion in week two.

What we are actually matching, in the full description a coordinator uses internally, is a Global Politics IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai families can keep for both years rather than swapping at the start of DP2. Continuity is worth something in this subject. A tutor who watched the student build a case file in DP1 knows which arguments that student already owns, and does not spend DP2 rediscovering them. Any IB tutor Mumbai parents engage for a single term before examinations is working with much less.

sections.heading: Papers 1 and 2, the engagement project and the HL extension presentations
paragraphs: The written examinations come in two papers with different demands. Paper 1 is built around source or stimulus material supplied in the examination itself, so the student must read material under time pressure and use it, which sounds obvious and is the single most common place marks leak away. Paper 2 asks for extended written responses in which a command term sets the shape of the answer and the student has to reach a judgement and defend it. A tutor who treats both papers as the same task is not much use, because the skill of handling given material is not the skill of constructing an argument from memory.

Alongside the papers sits the engagement project, in which the student connects a political issue to direct experience and writes it up. The sibling pages on this site deal with the engagement activity in detail; what matters here is that it runs in parallel with everything else, and a student who leaves it until the term before submission will be writing it during the same weeks as a science internal assessment. An online tutor is well placed to keep a light weekly check on it without taking it over, which is the line that has to be held: the work must be the student's own.

Higher Level students carry the extension, assessed through presentations rather than a written paper. Presentation assessment rewards a student who can hold a line of argument out loud, handle a question that cuts against it, and stay inside the time. That is a rehearsable skill and video lessons are genuinely good at rehearsing it, because the student can present to a screen, watch the recording back with the tutor, and hear how often they said the thing they meant to argue against as though it were obvious.

For the current structure of the papers, the assessment criteria and anything that looks like a weighting, a word count or a time limit, read the subject guide your school issues and ask the DP coordinator. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, and a figure that was accurate for one cohort can be wrong for the year your child actually sits. Any Global Politics tutor in Mumbai worth engaging will send you to the current guide rather than quote numbers from memory, and will mark your child's work against the criteria the school is actually using.

sections.heading: Mumbai school calendars, mocks and the months that squeeze
paragraphs: Mumbai's IB schools do not run a single shared calendar, but they cluster. Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School in the Bandra Kurla Complex, Ecole Mondiale World School, Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR in Goregaon East, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Singapore International School in Dahisar East and NES International School in Mulund West all set internal deadlines on their own schedules. The practical effect is that a tutor working with four students from four schools is tracking four different draft dates for the same piece of work.

The months that squeeze are predictable. For a May session cohort, the autumn term of DP2 stacks internal assessment drafts across subjects and the Extended Essay close to each other, mock examinations land in the window after the winter break, and the weeks between mocks and the real papers are when families suddenly want four sessions instead of one. For a November session cohort the same pattern sits roughly half a year earlier. Monsoon weeks add their own problem: a physical session in Chembur or on Ghodbunder Road is the first thing to be cancelled when the roads flood, and a run of cancellations in July costs a term's momentum.

That seasonal reality is the quiet argument for video as the backbone and home tuition as the supplement, rather than the other way round. A weekly online slot survives rain, a school trip, a wedding in the family and a tutor's own commute. Where families want the tutor physically present for mock preparation, we plan it in advance for a specific fortnight rather than hoping somebody is free in February. Schools in Thane such as Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School and in Navi Mumbai such as D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul sit far enough out that this planning is not optional.

Naming these schools is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, or with any examination board. We do not receive information from schools, we do not act for them, and nothing a tutor says about a school's internal deadlines replaces what the DP coordinator tells you. Where a school's instruction and a tutor's advice conflict, the school wins; a tutor who says otherwise is the wrong tutor.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online lessons or a hybrid of both across Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tutoring is still the service most Mumbai families ask for first, and for good reason. A home tutor sits at the same table as the student, sees the half-finished notes, notices when the phone comes out, and can point at a line on paper. For Global Politics specifically, a home tutor can also run the thing this subject most needs, which is a live argument with somebody in the room. An IB home tutor in Mumbai who comes to Powai or Khar twice a week gives a structure that is hard to replicate. The cost is geography: for a small-cohort subject, the nearest specialist may be two zones away, and a tutor who spends ninety minutes travelling will not keep the slot past a term.

Online is where this page lands because it solves exactly that. An IB DP Global Politics online tutor in Mumbai can be matched on subject expertise alone, keeps a slot that traffic cannot break, and can mark an essay in a shared document while the student watches each comment appear against their own sentence. What it costs you is the room. A video call is a poor substitute for a group of people disagreeing, and a tutor who does not compensate for that deliberately will run a pleasant, agreeable hour in which the student is never contradicted. That is the failure mode to watch for, and it is the subject of the next section but one.

Hybrid is what most families with a DP2 student settle on. A standing weekly video lesson carries the term, and a physical visit is added at the points where being in the room is worth the travel: before mocks, when a draft needs line-by-line attention, and in the fortnight before the written papers when the student has to practise writing by hand. IB home tuition in Mumbai booked as a planned block of four or five sessions is much easier to staff than an open-ended weekly commitment across the city, so hybrid often gets you a better tutor than insisting on home-only.

One honest warning about small group classes, since parents ask. A group of three arguing students is closer to what this subject rewards than one-to-one is, but only if the three are at a similar level and actually turn up. Groups assembled across zones for convenience tend to lose a member by week four and then run as an expensive pair. Global Politics home classes Mumbai parents organise within one society or one school year group hold together far better than groups put together from a list.

sections.heading: How a Global Politics tutor in Mumbai is verified, and what you should check yourself
paragraphs: Before a name reaches you, IB Gram checks identity documents, the qualifications claimed, and the teaching history specific to this course. Teaching history is the one that does the work. There are many capable graduates in political science in Mumbai and far fewer people who have marked Diploma Programme scripts against the published criteria. We ask what the tutor has taught, at which level, for how many cohorts, and whether they have examined. We also ask for a sample of written feedback on a student script, because feedback is where a tutor's actual standard shows. An IB DP Global Politics online tutor in Mumbai who cannot produce useful written feedback will not produce it for your child either.

There is a check specific to this subject that generic verification misses, and it is the tutor's neutrality. Not as a courtesy, but as a working method. The test we use in the trial is simple: ask the tutor to argue the side the student did not take, properly and in good faith, and then to swap and argue the other. A tutor who can do that, and who attributes positions to the people who hold them rather than presenting one as obviously correct, is teaching the skill the examination actually rewards. A tutor who cannot resist signalling their own view is training the student to write one-sided answers.

What you should check yourself takes about twenty minutes. Sit in on the last ten minutes of the trial lesson. Ask the tutor what they think the student's weakest assessment skill is and what they plan to do about it in the first month; a specific answer is a good sign and a general one is not. Ask to see the written feedback from the trial. Ask how they handle a topic where the student's family holds strong views, and listen for an answer about representing perspectives accurately rather than an answer about agreeing.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, offers predicted-grade influence, or hints at knowing what will come up in the papers. None of that is real. Be equally wary of a tutor who will not tell you which parts of the course they are weaker on, because every tutor has some. The useful conversation is about method and about what the first month will contain, not about outcomes nobody can promise.

sections.heading: Why is a discussion subject harder to teach through a screen?
paragraphs: Because the subject is taught through argument, and a one-to-one video call is a poor substitute for a room full of people who disagree with each other. In a classroom the counter-argument arrives free: somebody objects, somebody else half-agrees, and the student discovers their position has a weakness without anyone having to engineer it. On a call there are two people, one of whom is being paid, and the natural gravity of the situation is agreement. A good IB online tutor in Mumbai has to manufacture the opposition on purpose, every lesson, and that is a specific teaching skill rather than a personality trait.

The method that works is structured and slightly artificial, which students find funny for about two weeks and then stop noticing. The tutor takes the opposite side of whatever the student has argued and presses it honestly, using the strongest version of that case rather than a weak one set up to be knocked down. Then they swap, and the student has to argue the side they have just been attacking. The point is not to change the student's mind. The point is that representing an opposing perspective accurately enough that somebody holding it would recognise it is itself an assessed skill, and the only reliable way to learn it is to do it out loud against resistance.

The second thing a screen does well, better than a kitchen table in many cases, is marking. In a shared document the tutor marks the student's essay live while the student watches each comment appear against their own sentence, and the student can ask why, there and then, before the comment becomes a mark on a returned script they never reread. Paper feedback handed over at the end of a home tuition session gets glanced at. A comment that lands on your own clause while you are looking at it does not. This is the strongest single argument for video in this subject and families underuse it.

Third, the shared file. A Global Politics student needs evidence, and evidence that is attributed and dated rather than half-remembered. A tutor working online should be building, with the student, a running file of cases organised by concept, each entry carrying what happened in neutral terms, who said what and when, and which concept it illustrates. By DP2 that file is the student's own revision resource and it is searchable, which a notebook in Vikhroli is not. Connected to that is the reading habit: a current-affairs habit that is reading rather than scrolling, a small number of substantial sources read weekly at a set time, which a tutor can check in the first five minutes of each lesson.

The honest counterweight is the handwriting. The written papers are sat by hand, and a student who has spent two years typing every argument into a shared document will write slower and tire faster than one who has been drafting on paper. Any online programme in this subject has to build in handwritten timed work, scanned and sent for marking, from the middle of DP1 rather than the week before mocks. That single adjustment removes most of the real disadvantage of learning this subject through a screen.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, a term and an exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at marks. You should be looking at whether the student can state a position, state the strongest objection to it, and say which of the course's concepts is doing the work in each. If that is happening by session four, the tutoring is working even if the latest school mark has not moved. If the student is still producing paragraphs that describe rather than argue, say so in week five rather than week twelve. Four weeks is early enough to change tutor without losing the year.

At one term the measurable things are the quality of the source-handling in Paper 1 style questions and whether extended answers now reach a judgement instead of trailing off into a summary. The case file should have real content in it. The student should be reading something weekly without being chased. School feedback should have started to use different words, and the tutor should be able to predict roughly what the school will say before it says it, which is a good sign that they are marking to the same criteria.

At one exam cycle, after mocks, the gap between what the student knows and what the student gets onto paper under time becomes visible, and it is usually the larger problem. Handwriting speed, time split across questions and the discipline of answering the question asked account for more lost marks than missing content does. A tutor who looks at a mock script and talks only about content is missing most of it. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor can; what a good one can do is make the gap between knowledge and performance smaller and tell you honestly how large it still is.

When it is not working, say so early. A replacement is a short conversation, not an argument: tell the coordinator what is not landing, and a different name comes with a trial lesson in the same way as the first. Most mismatches in this subject are about argument style rather than competence. A gentle tutor and a combative student can both be good and still waste each other's time. An IB private tutor Mumbai families engage directly, outside any platform, is harder to replace precisely because that conversation has nowhere neutral to happen.

sections.heading: Booking Global Politics home classes or online lessons in Mumbai
paragraphs: To start, send four things: Standard Level or Higher Level, DP1 or DP2, the school, and two or three weekly windows that are genuinely free. Add the examination session if you know it. If you have a recent piece of marked work, send that too; it is worth more than any description of the problem, because a tutor reading two paragraphs of the student's own writing can tell you in ten minutes whether the issue is content, structure or the command term being ignored.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like it. Expect the tutor to ask the student to argue something, then argue against them, then ask the student to swap sides. Expect a short piece of writing, probably handwritten and timed, so there is a baseline. Expect to be told at the end what the tutor thinks the first month contains, in specific terms. If the first session is a tour of the syllabus, that is a weak first session and you should say so.

Whether you want Global Politics home classes Mumbai-wide, a weekly video slot, or the hybrid most DP2 families end up with, the request goes to the same coordinator and the same pool. Tell us which you prefer and which you would accept, because for a subject with this few specialists, flexibility on mode is often what gets you the better tutor rather than the nearer one.

Two practical notes before you book. Fix the weekly slot at a time the student is actually alert, because a 9pm lesson after a full school day and a sports session produces an hour of polite nodding and no argument. And set the reading habit in week one rather than week six: a short list of substantial sources, read at a fixed time, checked at the start of each lesson. Students who build that habit in DP1 arrive at DP2 with evidence of their own; students who do not spend DP2 borrowing examples from the tutor and never quite own them.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for a discussion subject like Global Politics?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor manufactures the disagreement deliberately. The risk with video is not the technology, it is that a one-to-one call drifts into agreement, and a student who is never contradicted never learns to anticipate an objection. A tutor who argues the side the student did not take, then swaps, reproduces most of what a classroom gives you. Video also marks essays better than a kitchen table does, because the student watches each comment land on their own sentence. The genuine loss is handwriting practice, which has to be scheduled back in.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Bandra West for an evening home tuition slot instead?
faqs.answer: Often yes in Bandra West, which is one of the easier parts of Mumbai to staff. Tell us the society name and the gate protocol, because a tutor who needs a fresh visitor pass every week loses ten minutes at the gate and eventually loses patience. Evening slots between 6pm and 8pm are the most contested across the Western Suburbs, so give us two options rather than one. For Global Politics specifically the specialist pool is small, so if no local name is free we will say so rather than offer you a general humanities tutor.

faqs.question: What does an online Global Politics lesson actually look like?
faqs.answer: A typical hour opens with five minutes on what the student read that week, which keeps the reading habit honest. Then a piece of writing is marked live in a shared document while the student watches and asks why. Then an argued exchange on a question from the school's current unit, with the tutor taking the opposing side and the two swapping halfway. The lesson usually closes by adding one or two entries to the student's case file, dated and attributed, so the evidence is usable in DP2 rather than half-remembered.

faqs.question: How is an essay marked if the tutor is not in the room with my child?
faqs.answer: In a shared document, live, with the student watching. The tutor comments against specific sentences while the student is looking at them, and the student can challenge a comment immediately instead of reading it a week later. This is one area where video beats a face-to-face session, where written feedback is typically handed over at the end and skimmed. Ask any tutor to demonstrate this in the trial lesson. A tutor who marks offline and emails a PDF back is giving you less than the format allows.

faqs.question: Will the tutor push their own political opinions on my child?
faqs.answer: They should not, and we test for it in the trial. In this subject neutrality is a working method rather than good manners: the examination rewards a student who can represent an opposing perspective accurately enough that somebody holding it would recognise it, and a tutor who signals their own view trains the student to write one-sided answers. Expect positions to be attributed to the people who hold them, expect generic framings where a real example would inflame rather than illuminate, and tell the coordinator immediately if you hear anything else.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a subject like this?
faqs.answer: Level, scarcity, mode and session length, mostly in that order. Higher Level with the extension strand costs more to support than Standard Level. Global Politics has a small specialist pool in Mumbai, and scarcity moves rates more than anything else does. Online removes travel from the calculation, which is why a video slot with a tutor two zones away is often cheaper than a local in-person one. Session length and frequency do the rest. We will not quote a figure here; ask the coordinator for a range once we know the level and the mode.

faqs.question: My daughter knows the content but freezes on Paper 1 source questions. Can video sessions fix that?
faqs.answer: This is one of the most fixable problems in the subject and it suits video well. Freezing on source material is almost always a process problem: the student reads the material once, panics, and then answers from memory while the supplied material sits unused on the page. The fix is a repeatable routine applied to a dozen past stimulus sets, timed, with the tutor watching the annotation happen on a shared screen. Expect visible change within four to six weeks if the routine is practised rather than discussed.

faqs.question: Do we need a parent at home during an online session, and where should the student sit?
faqs.answer: A parent does not need to sit in, but somebody should be at home, and the student should not be in a bedroom with the door shut. A dining table or a study corner with the screen visible from the room works best. Keep the phone in another room. For a subject that depends on the student speaking at length, a space where they are not self-conscious about being overheard matters more than it does for mathematics, so a quiet corner beats a busy living room with the television on.

faqs.question: We live off Ghodbunder Road in Thane and evening travel is impossible. Is online the only realistic option?
faqs.answer: For Global Politics in Thane, usually yes for the weekly slot. The Ghodbunder stretch between the station and Kasarvadavali decides everything about a 7pm arrival, and a tutor who manages it in March will be cancelling by July. A standing video lesson removes that risk completely. What we can usually add is a planned in-person block before mocks, agreed weeks in advance, where a tutor commits to four or five visits rather than an open-ended weekly trip across Thane.

faqs.question: The tutor is competent but my son is not responding after three weeks. What happens now?
faqs.answer: Tell the coordinator and ask for a different name; it is a short conversation and no justification is needed. Most mismatches in this subject are about argument style rather than ability. A tutor who presses hard suits a student who enjoys the fight and shuts down a student who needs to be coaxed into disagreeing at all. The replacement comes with a trial lesson in the same way the first did, and the new tutor is briefed on what did not work, so you are not starting the explanation from scratch.

faqs.question: My son types everything and handwrites slowly. Does online tutoring make that worse?
faqs.answer: It can, and this is the main honest drawback of learning this subject through a screen. Students who draft every argument in a shared document for two years arrive at the written papers writing slowly and tiring in the second half. The counterweight is deliberate: timed handwritten answers from the middle of DP1, photographed and sent to the tutor for marking, roughly every second or third session and more often as mocks approach. Ask any online tutor how they handle this. A vague answer is a bad sign.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor also visit our society in Kharghar once a month before the exams?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and it is worth asking at the start rather than in February. Navi Mumbai matches best node to node, so a tutor already in Kharghar, Belapur or Nerul can add a monthly visit without the Palm Beach Road or Atal Setu problem. If your video tutor lives in the Western Suburbs, we would instead pair the weekly online lesson with a separate local tutor for the in-person block. Give us the society name and the visitor pass procedure when you book, not on the day.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram shortlist an IB DP Global Politics private tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Most enquiries for an IB DP Global Politics private tutor in Mumbai arrive in one of two shapes. Either the student has been in the course for a term and the marks are lower than expected, or the student is still deciding whether to take it and the family wants somebody who knows what the two years actually involve. Those need different conversations, and we ask which it is before sending any names. A DP1 student in Mulund West still inside her school's subject change window has options that a DP2 student in Kasarvadavali in February does not.

For a student already in the course, the sequence is short. 1. You send the level, the Diploma Programme year, the school and one piece of marked work. 2. A coordinator shortlists two or three tutors who have taught this course, with a stated first priority for each. 3. You and the student speak to them. 4. One trial session runs on real work, either at your home or on video. 5. You fix a weekly slot or ask for a different name. For a family still choosing the subject, we usually suggest one paid diagnostic conversation with a specialist instead, which is cheaper than a term of tuition for a subject that turns out to be the wrong fit.

A one-to-one arrangement is what most families mean by an IB private tutor Mumbai agencies would describe as individual coaching, and in this subject the one-to-one format has a specific value. Global Politics punishes students who cannot be challenged. In a class of twenty-five nobody has time to press a single student on a weak claim for ten minutes. A private tutor can, and should, and that is most of what you are paying for. If a tutor spends the hour lecturing, you are buying an expensive version of something the school already provides.

We also ask about the rest of the timetable before matching, because this subject rarely fails on its own. A student struggling with Global Politics in January of the second year is often struggling with written output across three subjects at once, and the sensible answer may be one tutor working on argued writing rather than three subject tutors in parallel. Say what else is wobbling. It changes the shortlist, and occasionally it changes the recommendation to no tutoring at all for a fortnight while the student catches up on sleep.

sections.heading: Standard Level, Higher Level and the extension work before the DP1 window closes
paragraphs: Global Politics sits in Group 3 of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), alongside history, geography, economics, psychology, business management and the rest of individuals and societies. Students pick it at the start of DP1, almost always without having studied anything like it before, because very few Mumbai schools run a comparable course at Middle Years Programme (MYP) level. That makes the Standard Level (SL) and Higher Level (HL) decision unusually blind, and it is the decision families most often come back to in the first term.

Higher Level adds an extension strand, studied in more depth and assessed by presentation rather than by an additional written paper. In practice that means an HL student carries a workstream through the second year that an SL student does not, and it falls in the same months as the Extended Essay (EE) and the heaviest internal assessment clustering. A student whose written output is slow should think carefully before taking it at Higher Level, not because the content is beyond them but because the calendar is. A good home tutor will tell you that in week two rather than in October.

Every Mumbai school sets its own window for subject and level changes early in DP1, typically within the first weeks, after which the registration is fixed. If a change is being considered, the deadline is the first thing to establish with the school's DP coordinator, because the answer is a date and nothing else matters until you know it. Internally, what a coordinator is matching is a Global Politics IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai families keep for the whole course, and the earlier the level is settled the less of that time is spent on uncertainty.

One thing to understand about changing out of the subject after the engagement work has begun. The engagement project is tied to this course, so work already done on it does not transfer to history or economics; a student switching in week six has typically lost a few weeks of effort rather than a term, which is a real cost and usually a smaller one than two years in the wrong subject. Ask the DP coordinator exactly what has been registered and what has been submitted before deciding. Do not take that decision on a tutor's advice alone, and do not take the level decision on it either.

sections.heading: What Papers 1 and 2, the engagement project and the HL presentations ask of a student
paragraphs: The written assessment comes in two papers with distinct demands. Paper 1 supplies source or stimulus material in the examination and asks questions that depend on reading it properly under pressure. Paper 2 asks for extended written responses built around a command term, where the student must reach a judgement and defend it. The sibling page on this site covers that technique in detail. What matters when a family is choosing the subject is the shape of the demand: this is a reading-and-writing course assessed by argument, and a student who writes slowly will feel both papers as time problems rather than knowledge problems.

The engagement project asks the student to connect a political issue to direct experience and write it up, which sounds appealing in September and becomes a scheduling problem by the following year. It runs alongside everything else, it is the student's own work, and it needs starting earlier than most students start it. Families should know before choosing the subject that this component exists and that it is not a short essay produced in a weekend.

Higher Level students additionally present. Presentation assessment rewards a student who can sustain a line of argument out loud, take a question that cuts against it without collapsing, and keep inside the time. Some students are far better at this than they are at writing and it lifts them; others find it the hardest single thing in the diploma. A frank judgement on which of those a student is, made in DP1, is worth more than a term of tuition later.

Any Global Politics tutor in Mumbai you engage should send you to your school's current copy of the subject guide for the structure of the components and for the assessment criteria, rather than reciting figures. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, so anything resembling a weighting, a mark total, a word count or a paper duration should be read from the document your child's cohort is actually working to. A tutor who quotes those numbers from memory is telling you something about how recently they taught the course.

sections.heading: Private and home tuition coverage across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Thane
paragraphs: This subject has a thin specialist pool in Mumbai, and the Eastern Suburbs and Thane feel that more than the island does. From Chembur and Govandi up through Wadala, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund, the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway carry most of the movement, and the Eastern Freeway has made Wadala and Chembur noticeably closer to South Mumbai than the map suggests. A South Mumbai tutor can occasionally hold a weekly slot in Chembur because of that road. Holding one in Bhandup is a different proposition, and we would rather pair you with a nearer generalist for some sessions and a specialist on video for the rest than pretend otherwise.

Thane is one long east-west problem. From the station across Pokhran Road and Majiwada out along Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali, a journey that takes twenty minutes in the middle of the day takes close to an hour at seven in the evening, and the Thane-Borivali tunnel corridor has not changed that yet. Thane tutors cover Thane; Mulund tutors sometimes cross over on the Eastern Express Highway. An IB DP Global Politics private tutor in Mumbai living near Thane station is a realistic weekly fixture in Majiwada and a fragile one in Kasarvadavali, and the honest fix is usually a weekend in-person slot with weekday sessions on video.

Navi Mumbai works node to node along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are short hops from each other, and the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines plus the Atal Setu have shortened the run into town without making a twice-weekly creek crossing survivable for a tutor. A home tutor for Global Politics Mumbai families in Kharghar or Panvel ask for is best found within Navi Mumbai, and if nobody suitable is there in the next fortnight we will say so rather than leave the request open.

The rest of the city behaves as it always has. In the Western Suburbs, matching along the line works and matching across it does not: Khar to Santacruz West and Malad to Kandivali hold, Bandra to Dahisar at 6.30pm does not, whatever Metro Lines 2A and 7 have done for off-peak travel; Juhu, Andheri West and Goregaon East carry the largest Diploma cohorts. South Mumbai is short-distance and slow, with Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Worli matched within the island despite the Coastal Road, the Bandra-Worli Sea Link and Metro Line 3. In the Central Suburbs, Powai and Chandivali hang off JVLR with no station, reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, while Kurla, Ghatkopar and Mulund sit on the Central Line.

Mumbai, Maharashtra is one tutor market behaving like six, and searches such as IB tutors near me Mumbai are a poor filter for a subject this specialised. Start from who has taught the course, then ask what is reachable from where you live.

sections.heading: Is it too late to change subjects at a Mumbai IB school?
paragraphs: Ask the school, today, and ask for a date. Every Mumbai IB school sets its own cut-off for subject and level changes in the first weeks of DP1, and after that the registration is fixed with the IB. Families at NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School, Chembur, Witty International School in Chembur, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, Billabong High International School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all work to their own calendar, and the only authority on yours is your own DP coordinator. A tutor's opinion on whether a change is still possible is worth nothing next to that date.

Timetable blocking is the practical constraint nobody warns parents about. A student may be allowed to change subject in principle and still be unable to, because the replacement subject runs in the same block as a subject they are keeping. That is why the conversation has to happen with the school rather than at home: the coordinator can see the blocks, and often the honest answer is that two of the three alternatives are impossible and the choice is between staying and taking the one that fits.

If the decision is to stay, the second term of DP1 is the best possible time to start home tuition, and almost nobody does. Schools in the Western and Central Suburbs such as Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, JBCN International School, Borivali and Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai cluster their first serious written assessments in that part of the year, which is exactly when a weak writer can be identified and fixed cheaply. The families who call in the second year are usually paying more for less.

Naming schools here is local context only. sections.heading: Home classes, one-to-one online, or a hybrid across Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tutoring remains the default request and for a student who is drifting it is the right one. An IB home tutor in Mumbai arriving at a fixed hour creates an appointment the student cannot quietly skip, sees the state of the notes, and can argue with the student across a table where neither of them can mute the other. For this subject the argument across the table is the point. A student who has never had a weak claim pressed for ten minutes writes differently from one who has.

Online suits a subject this scarce. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can be matched on having actually taught the course rather than on living within six kilometres, which in the Eastern Suburbs and Thane is frequently the difference between a specialist and a substitute. Video also marks writing well, because the tutor can comment in a shared document while the student watches each comment land on their own sentence. The weakness is that a call drifts towards agreement unless the tutor engineers the opposition on purpose, which the sibling page on online teaching covers properly.

Hybrid is the arrangement most second-year families end up with, and the split is worth planning rather than drifting into. IB home tuition in Mumbai booked as a defined block of four or five visits before mocks is far easier to staff than an open-ended weekly commitment across two zones, and a tutor is far more likely to agree to it. Keep the in-person visits for timed handwritten work and for sitting with a marked script; use video for the argued sessions and the weekly reading check.

Small group teaching deserves one honest paragraph, because parents compare private rates against it. Three students arguing is closer to what this subject rewards than one-to-one is, but only when the three are at similar levels and all actually attend. Global Politics home classes Mumbai parents organise inside one society or one school year group tend to survive; groups assembled across zones for price reasons usually lose a member by the fourth week and then run as an expensive pair at a group rate. A private tutor costs more per hour and wastes less of it.

sections.heading: What should you check about a private tutor in Mumbai yourself?
paragraphs: IB Gram verifies identity, qualifications and teaching history on this specific course before a name is sent, and asks for a sample of written feedback on a real student script. That last item filters more candidates than anything else, because any IB tutor Mumbai parents might consider can describe their approach and far fewer can produce annotations that point at assessment criteria. An IB DP Global Politics private tutor in Mumbai who has marked Diploma Programme work will show you comments about judgement, attribution and command terms. Someone who has not will show you comments about style.

The check that is specific to this subject is the tutor's handling of their own views, and it is a method question rather than a manners question. Ask the tutor to argue, properly, the side the student did not take, using the strongest version of that case, and then to swap and argue the other. A tutor who can do that, attributing each position to the people who hold it, is teaching the thing the criteria reward. A tutor who cannot resist making clear which answer is correct is training your child to write one-sided essays, which is the fault that costs marks in this subject more than any gap in knowledge.

Your own twenty minutes matter more than our paperwork. Sit at the table or on the call for the last ten minutes of the trial. Ask what the student's weakest assessed skill is and what the first four weeks will do about it; a specific answer is the signal you want. Ask what the tutor will not help with, because a tutor who claims to cover the Extended Essay, the engagement project, three other subjects and university applications is overselling. Ask whether they will write two lines after each session so you know what happened without cross-examining a teenager.

Be wary of a tutor who promises a specific grade, implies influence over a predicted grade, claims to know what the papers will contain, or offers an opinion on which universities will take the student. That last one matters on this page in particular. Entry requirements vary by institution and by individual course, they change between admission cycles, and the only reliable source is the university's own published requirements read alongside your school's counsellor. A tutor stating a named university's requirement is guessing, however confidently.

sections.heading: Who should take Global Politics, and what students get wrong about it
paragraphs: The student who chooses this subject because they follow the news is the one most likely to be disappointed, and it happens every year. Following events closely is useful background and it is not the subject. The course assesses whether a student can define contested terms precisely, set out competing perspectives fairly, attribute each position to those who hold it, weigh evidence and reach a judgement that follows from the weighing. None of that is the same as having views. A student who arrives expecting to write what they think, and who has been praised for being opinionated, often finds the first term genuinely humbling.

The second misjudgement is the writing load. This is a reading-and-writing course. There are no diagrams to carry a weak paragraph and no calculations to be right about; everything is prose, assessed as argument, under time, by hand. A student who writes slowly or hates writing will feel that in both papers and again in the engagement write-up. Families considering the subject should look honestly at how long the student takes to produce a page of their own argued prose, because that number predicts more about the next two years than enthusiasm does. Home tuition can make a slow writer faster, and it cannot make an unwilling one willing.

On how it compares with its Group 3 neighbours, the useful framing is demand rather than difficulty. History works on sources about the past and carries a heavier factual memory load. Geography combines physical and human material and asks for data handling and fieldwork. Economics requires diagrams, definitions and quantitative reasoning, and rewards a student who likes a model. Global Politics asks for less memorised detail than history and more disciplined argument than most students expect, with concepts used as analytical tools rather than labels. Easier is the wrong question; the right question is which kind of work the student can sustain in the second year when everything is due at once.

The student with strong convictions is a special case and often becomes the strongest candidate in the cohort, but only after an uncomfortable term. The skill that has to be learnt is representing an opposing perspective accurately enough that somebody who holds it would recognise themselves in the description. A student who writes a caricature and defeats it scores badly however sound their own conclusion. This is why a tutor's willingness to argue the other side, in good faith, matters so much in this subject; it is also why some students improve faster with a tutor who disagrees with them than with one who does not.

Then the practical questions. If the subject turns out to be wrong, the change window in DP1 is short and set by the school, and engagement work already started does not move to another subject. If the student stays, the SL or HL decision should be made on written output and timetable load rather than on interest. And on universities, requirements vary by institution and by course and must be checked at source rather than assumed from what a cousin was told two admission cycles ago. A good private tutor helps with the first two of those and is honest about having no standing on the third.

sections.heading: Progress, honest limits and the university question
paragraphs: In the first four weeks look at behaviour rather than marks. The student should be defining contested terms before using them, writing the opposing case before their own, and finishing timed answers rather than abandoning the last one. A school mark in week four usually reflects work set in week one, so it tells you little. If none of those behaviours has shifted by the fifth session, raise it with the coordinator then. That is early enough to change tutor without losing anything that matters.

By the end of a term, extended answers should reach a defended judgement by habit, concept words should be doing analytical work rather than decorating sentences, and the student should be able to summarise a position they disagree with fairly enough to satisfy somebody who holds it. If the family chose the subject recently against advice, this is also the point at which you will know whether the fit was right, which is worth more than the marks.

After mocks, the honest measurement is the gap between what the student knows and what reaches the page under time. In this subject that gap is usually wider than the knowledge gap, and it is made of handwriting speed, time allocation and answering the question that was asked. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, no tutor can, and anybody suggesting otherwise should be struck off your shortlist immediately. What good tutoring does is narrow that gap and describe accurately how wide it still is while there is time to act.

On universities, the limit is firm. Entry requirements differ between institutions and between individual courses at the same institution, they are revised between admission cycles, and some courses ask for specific subjects while others do not. The only sources worth acting on are the university's own published requirements and your school's university counsellor. We will not tell you what any named university requires and will say so if asked. A tutor who offers that detail confidently, alongside Global Politics home classes or weekly sessions, is giving you an opinion dressed as information.

When a match is not working, the replacement is a conversation and a new trial, not an argument. Most failures in this subject are about argument style rather than competence: a tutor who presses hard suits a student who enjoys the exchange and silences one who needs coaxing. Tell the coordinator what did not land, and the incoming tutor is briefed so you are not explaining it twice.

faqs.question: Should my daughter take Global Politics if she mainly enjoys arguing about the news?
faqs.answer: Enjoying the news is a reasonable starting point and a poor predictor of success. The course does not assess opinions; it assesses whether a student can define contested terms precisely, present competing perspectives fairly, attribute positions to those who hold them and reach a judgement the evidence supports. Students who arrive expecting to write what they think usually find the first term hard. Students who are willing to argue a case they personally reject tend to do well. Ask her to write the strongest version of an argument she disagrees with and see how it goes.

faqs.question: How much writing does Global Politics involve compared with history?
faqs.answer: Both are writing-heavy, and the difference is in what the writing carries. History asks a student to hold a larger body of factual detail and work with sources about the past. Global Politics asks for less memorised detail and more disciplined argument, with the course's concepts used as analytical tools in every answer. Neither has diagrams or calculations to carry a weak paragraph. If your child dislikes writing extended prose under time, that is the material fact, and it applies to both subjects rather than distinguishing them.

faqs.question: Should we choose Higher Level or Standard Level for this subject?
faqs.answer: Decide it on written output and timetable load, with the school's Diploma Programme coordinator, not on interest. Higher Level adds an extension strand assessed by presentation, and it falls in the same months as the Extended Essay and the heaviest internal assessment clustering in the second year. A confident speaker who writes at reasonable speed often thrives on it. A student who takes two hours to produce a page of argued prose will feel the extra strand as a calendar problem. A tutor can give you an honest read on the writing speed; the decision stays with the school.

faqs.question: My son has already started his engagement project. Can he still switch subjects?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on your school's change deadline and its timetable blocks, so ask the coordinator for the date before anything else. Engagement work is tied to this course and does not transfer to history, geography or economics, so a switch means that effort is lost. Weighed against two years in a subject that does not suit him, a few weeks of lost work is often the smaller cost. What you should not do is make the decision on a tutor's view of his ability after three sessions.

faqs.question: Do universities accept Global Politics as a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Requirements vary by institution and by individual course, and they are revised between admission cycles, so this has to be checked at source rather than taken from a page like this one. Read the published entry requirements for the specific courses your child is considering, and work through them with your school's university counsellor, who knows both the student's profile and how your school's cohorts have been assessed. We will not name a university's requirement here, and a tutor who states one confidently is offering an opinion rather than information.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a private tutor in this subject?
faqs.answer: Scarcity first, then level, mode and session length. Global Politics has a small specialist pool across Mumbai, and scarcity affects rates more than any other single factor. Higher Level with the extension strand needs more support than Standard Level. Travel is a real cost that shows up either in the rate or in reliability, which is why an online slot with a specialist two zones away is often better value than a local in-person session. faqs.answer: Usually yes in Mulund West, which sits on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway and is one of the easier parts of the Eastern Suburbs to staff. Evening slots between 6pm and 8pm are the most requested, so offer two options rather than one. faqs.question: Our building in Thane requires a fresh gate pass for every visitor. Does that cause problems?
faqs.answer: It costs about ten minutes a week and it is worth fixing once. Most Thane societies will issue a recurring entry for a named tutor at a fixed day and time if a resident requests it in writing, and a few will not. Tell us the procedure when you book rather than on the first evening. Where a society genuinely insists on a per-visit pass, either someone at home should be ready to authorise it at the gate, or the weekday sessions are better run online with in-person visits at the weekend.

faqs.question: My daughter holds strong political views. Will a tutor clash with her?
faqs.answer: A good tutor will argue with her and will not tell her what to think, which is different from clashing. The skill the course rewards is representing a position she rejects accurately enough that somebody holding it would recognise themselves in her description, and the only way to learn that is to practise it against resistance. Expect the tutor to take the opposite side in good faith and then swap. Expect positions to be attributed to those who hold them. Tell the coordinator at once if you hear anything that reads as advocacy rather than method.

faqs.question: Is Global Politics an easier option than economics?
faqs.answer: Easier is the wrong frame, because the two make different demands. Economics asks for definitions, diagrams and quantitative reasoning and rewards a student who likes working inside a model. Global Politics asks for extended argument, precise use of contested concepts and fair treatment of competing perspectives, all in prose under time. A student who writes well and reasons carefully may find this the more comfortable course; one who prefers a method with a right answer usually will not. Judge by the kind of work your child can sustain in the second year.

faqs.question: How is a private tutor different from the group classes running near our society in Vikhroli?
faqs.answer: A private tutor can press one student on one weak claim for ten minutes, which is most of the value in this subject and is impossible in a group. Groups are better at one thing: three students arguing is closer to the classroom dynamic the papers reward than a pair is. The practical catch is attendance. Groups assembled across the Eastern Suburbs for price reasons usually lose a member by the fourth week and then run as a pair at group pace. Within one society or year group they hold together much better.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is competent but my son simply does not get on with them?
faqs.answer: Ask for a different name and give no justification; it is a short conversation with the coordinator and a new trial session follows. Style mismatches are the commonest reason a match fails in this subject and they are not a judgement on either party. A tutor who argues hard suits a student who enjoys the exchange and shuts down a student who needs drawing out, and the reverse pairing produces two comfortable years of no progress. The incoming tutor is briefed on what did not work, so you explain it once.

sections.heading: Shortlisting an IB DP global politics tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Global Politics requests arrive with a particular complaint attached. The student is articulate, reads the news, debates at school, and the marks sit stubbornly in the middle. Parents assume the problem is knowledge. It almost never is. Before shortlisting anyone, IB Gram asks to see two things: the most recent marked essay with the examiner-style comments on it, and the most recent source-based paper. Those two scripts show within minutes whether the student is losing marks on structure, on evidence, on concept use or on simply not answering the command term as written.

The second question is where the student is in the two years. A DP1 student in September is still learning what the course means by power, legitimacy or interdependence as technical terms rather than as ordinary English. A DP2 student in November is trying to write a judgement that survives the obvious counter-argument, under timed conditions, without drifting into assertion. These need different tutors. An IB DP global politics tutor in Mumbai who is strong on concept teaching is not automatically the right person for timed essay triage in the last term.

The third filter is temperament, and for this subject it is not a soft consideration. A tutor who argues their own position, however reasonably, teaches a student to perform agreement rather than to analyse. We shortlist tutors who can set out a perspective they personally reject, accurately and without editorial, because that is precisely the skill the examination rewards. Parents who want a home tutor for Global Politics Mumbai schools teach are usually relieved to hear that the brief is technique and not persuasion.

sections.heading: The conceptual framework the Diploma Programme course is built on
paragraphs: International Baccalaureate (IB) Global Politics is a concept-led course, and that single fact explains most of the marks students lose. The syllabus is organised around thematic study of power and sovereignty, rights and justice, development and sustainability, and peace and conflict, and across all of them a set of key concepts does the analytical work: power, legitimacy, interdependence, sovereignty, equality, justice, development, globalisation, violence and non-violence, among others. Unit names and course structure are revised on the IB's own cycle, so confirm the current arrangement with the subject guide and your school's coordinator rather than with anything you read online, including this page.

A concept in this course is a tool, not a topic. Legitimacy is not a synonym for popularity. Power is not a synonym for military strength, and the course expects students to distinguish between the different forms it takes and to notice when an actor has one and not another. Sovereignty is not simply independence. A student who uses these words loosely writes answers that read fluently and score in the middle, because the examiner cannot see any analysis happening. A student who uses two concepts precisely on one example, and shows where they pull in different directions, scores above their year group without knowing more facts than anyone else.

Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) share the thematic studies and the engagement requirement. Higher Level adds an extension in which students research global political challenges in depth and present their analysis for assessment. The extension is where concept precision stops being optional: a presentation that narrates a situation and ends with an opinion will not reach the upper bands, while one that applies two or three concepts to the same material and reaches a defended judgement will. Check the current format of the extension with the coordinator before planning any preparation around it.

The practical consequence for tutoring is that the first month is usually spent on vocabulary rather than on content. A tutor will take a single piece of material, a government introducing a trade restriction for example, and ask the student to analyse it three times: once through power, once through interdependence, once through legitimacy. The same facts produce three different arguments. Once a student can do that reliably, essays stop being opinion pieces with examples attached and start being analysis.

sections.heading: Papers 1 and 2, the engagement project and the HL extension
paragraphs: Paper 1 is the source-based paper. Students are given stimulus material and asked a graded series of questions that move from comprehension to comparison to a judgement using the sources and their own knowledge. The commonest failure is treating the sources as decoration: a student reads them once, then writes the essay they wanted to write anyway. The marks live in the handling. What does this source claim, who is making the claim, what would a reader who disagrees say about it, and what does putting two sources side by side reveal that neither says alone. A Global Politics tutor in Mumbai spends a surprising proportion of early sessions on nothing but source comparison.

Paper 2 is the essay paper, and it rewards a structure most students do not arrive with. An essay that lists three arguments and then asserts a conclusion scores below one that states a position, builds it on evidence, gives the strongest version of the opposing case, and then explains why the position still holds once that case is taken seriously. Giving the strongest version is the part students resist. A straw man costs marks twice, once for weak analysis and once for the missing counter-argument.

The engagement requirement asks students to undertake a political engagement activity and write an analytical report linking it to course theory. It is a substantial piece of work with real practical and safety constraints that the school sets, and it has its own detailed treatment elsewhere on this site rather than here. What belongs on this page is the warning that the report is assessed on analysis and not on the activity: a report that narrates an interesting experience and never applies a concept will score poorly however unusual the experience was.

Command terms govern everything. Identify, describe, compare, examine, discuss, evaluate and to what extent each set a different ceiling, and a student who writes a strong discussion in answer to an evaluate question has not done what was asked. Tutors drill this by taking one piece of material and rewriting the answer to four different command terms, which also teaches students how much of their essay was filler. Papers, criteria and command-term lists change between syllabus versions, so work from the guide your child's cohort is actually sitting.

sections.heading: Which months in the Mumbai school calendar hurt a Global Politics student?
paragraphs: November to January, and it is not close. The Mumbai IB year opens in late May or early June and finishes the following April with Diploma Programme examinations in May, which puts the engagement report, the Higher Level extension work, mock examinations, the extended essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) deadlines into roughly the same eight weeks of DP2. Global Politics suffers disproportionately in that window because its own deadlines are writing-heavy and because it is rarely the subject a student prioritises when four deadlines collide.

Families at Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, Activity High School on Peddar Road, JBCN International School in Parel, NES International School in Mulund West, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Singapore International School in Dahisar East and Smt. Parents who have it can plan tutoring around it instead of reacting to it.

The earlier pressure point is quieter and more damaging. Somewhere in the first term of DP1 a student decides whether this subject is an extension of their opinions or a discipline with its own rules. A student who settles on the first answer writes confident essays for a year and then discovers in DP2 that the technique was never there. September and October of DP1 are the cheapest months to fix that, and the most commonly skipped. A student in Chembur or Vile Parle who learns concept precision in DP1 is not doing remedial work in January.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named here, and naming a school is local context only: it indicates which calendar and board pathway a family is working to. We do not guarantee grades and no tutor on the platform is permitted to promise one. What a good match buys is a realistic plan across the months that remain, which in DP2 is a shorter number of working weeks than most families have actually counted.
