sections.heading: Hindi B at Standard and Higher Level in the exam term
paragraphs: Hindi B is a language acquisition subject of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), sat at Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL), and distinct from Hindi A, which studies language and literature. In the exam term the difference between the two levels shows up less in what a student knows and more in what they have to sustain: Higher Level asks for more, including engagement with literary text, and the written demands are correspondingly heavier under time pressure. A student who copes comfortably in a homework-paced term can still run out of road in a timed paper.

The structure of the papers, the criteria they are marked against and the expectations attached to each level are set out in the current Hindi B subject guide, which the IB revises on its own cycle. Get the current version through your school's DP coordinator, and get the school's own mock timetable while you are asking. Any figure about lengths, durations or weightings that a tutor quotes from memory is a figure to verify, and a tutor who is comfortable saying check the current guide is more trustworthy than one who is not.

Which language course a student sits is a decision the school makes with the family, and it is not reopened in DP2 on the advice of a tutor. What is worth saying to families comparing options is that Hindi B is not the soft route some people assume. The written task and the reading component regularly cost marks for confident Hindi speakers, because fluency and examination technique are different things. Students coming from the Middle Years Programme (MYP) are usually meeting formally assessed writing in Hindi for the first time at this scale.

sections.heading: What does each Hindi B paper reward?
paragraphs: Hindi B is examined through a Paper 1 writing task, a Paper 2 comprising listening and reading, and an individual oral run inside the school. Each of those rewards a different behaviour, and a student who approaches all three the same way leaves marks on all three. Paper 1 rewards obedience to the task. The reading component rewards discipline about evidence. The listening component rewards composure. The oral rewards having something to say and the machinery to keep saying it.

Obedience to the task is the one students resist most. The writing task names a situation, an audience and a text type, and every one of those is scored. A student who produces beautifully accurate Hindi in the wrong text type, or who addresses a municipal official in the register they would use with a friend, has lost marks that have nothing to do with their command of the language. Writing to the task also means writing to the task and not to length: an answer that keeps going past the point where the task has been fulfilled picks up errors without picking up credit.

Discipline about evidence is what the reading component tests. Whatever question formats appear in the current guide, the governing rule does not change: an answer must be licensed by the passage in front of the student, not by what they already happen to know about the topic. A student who has strong general knowledge about, say, water shortages will answer a question about a water shortage passage from memory, and the examiner will mark what the passage supports. The habit that fixes this is physical. Before writing an answer, underline the words in the text that permit it. If nothing can be underlined, the answer is coming from the wrong place.
bullets: Paper 1 scores the text type, the audience and the register, not only accuracy

sections.heading: Daytime home tuition across Mumbai during study leave
paragraphs: Exam term changes the geography of this city, and that is the single most useful local thing to know about booking home tuition at this stage. Once mocks and study leave begin, a DP2 student is at home on a weekday morning, and a tutor who could never reach them at 7pm can reach them at 11am without difficulty. The Western Express Highway between Bandra, Santacruz, Andheri and Goregaon at eleven in the morning is a different road from the same stretch at seven in the evening, and an IB DP Hindi B home tutor in Mumbai who covers Khar, Juhu, Vile Parle, Andheri West, Malad and Kandivali can hold two daytime sessions in a morning that would have taken a whole evening.

The Central Suburbs gain the most from this. Powai and Chandivali sit off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road with no station of their own, so they are always a road journey from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and in the evening that journey is what rules Powai out for half the tutor pool. In study leave it stops being an obstacle. The same applies along the Central Line through Kurla, Ghatkopar, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund, and across the Santacruz Chembur Link Road, which at midday is genuinely quick. Families in Powai who spent DP1 settling for whoever was local often find their options widen considerably in the weeks that matter most.

The pattern repeats elsewhere with local variation. In South Mumbai, where Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Babulnath, Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Worli are short distances made slow by the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals, the midday window is the easiest travel of the entire year, helped by the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3. In Navi Mumbai, Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are short hops on Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway at any hour, with the Atal Setu and the Harbour Line linking back to the island. In Thane, a daytime slot means Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali takes twenty minutes rather than an hour, and Pokhran Road and Majiwada are straightforward. Plan the exam-term schedule around this and you buy back time nobody charges you for.

sections.heading: When do Mumbai schools run Hindi B mocks?
paragraphs: Mock examinations at most Mumbai IB schools fall in the winter months of DP2, and the exact fortnight comes from your school rather than from any general rule, so ask the DP coordinator early in the year and write it in a calendar. The mock matters more in Hindi B than families expect, because it is usually the first time a student writes the full paper under time, and almost every technique problem described on this page becomes visible in that script. A mock that is treated as a progress report is wasted. A mock that is treated as evidence is the most useful document of the year.

The sequencing around the mock is the planning problem. By that point the individual oral has often already been recorded, so spoken work drops out of the schedule and the whole weight moves to the written papers. At the same time a DP2 student is handling a subject Internal Assessment (IA) and a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay, which is why Hindi B so often gets suspended in exactly the fortnight when timed practice is worth most. The way out is short and frequent: a single timed reading passage with the tutor, marked together, takes a fraction of a full session and keeps the technique alive.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or both in the exam term?
paragraphs: For exam technique specifically, home tuition has an advantage that is hard to argue with: the tutor can run a genuine timed paper and observe it. Exam conditions are not just a stopwatch. They are the student sitting upright at a table without a phone, writing continuously, with someone present who will not answer a question halfway through. Replicating that over a video call is possible and it is never quite the same, because the student knows the camera can be ignored. IB DP Hindi B home tuition in Mumbai in the final two terms is largely about building the behaviour of sitting a paper properly, and behaviour is best shaped in person.

Online keeps a real place in the exam term, and for some families it is what makes the frequency work at all. Marking a script the student has already written, going through annotations, drilling the recurring error list, working through a reading passage line by line, rehearsing listening strategy: all of that runs perfectly well over video. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can also be fitted into a half hour that would not justify a journey, which during study leave is often what a student needs most. The written piece itself is handwritten on paper and photographed either way.

The arrangement that suits most DP2 students is one weekly home session with a full timed component in it, plus one short online session for marking and error drilling. Decide it deliberately in advance of the mock, not in the panic afterwards. The honest limitation of the hybrid week is that it requires someone to hold the plan, and in exam term that is usually the parent rather than the student. One shared document with the error list, the papers attempted and the dates is enough to keep it from drifting.

sections.heading: Checking a Hindi B home tuition tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Identity, stated qualifications, claimed Hindi B teaching experience and references from earlier families are checked before any tutor is offered for IB DP Hindi B home tuition in Mumbai. For exam-technique work there is one extra thing we look for, which is whether the tutor marks to criteria or marks by impression. The test is simple: given a student's script, can they say which criterion a particular weakness sits under and what specifically would move it, or do they produce general praise and a list of corrections? Only the first of those is useful to a student five months from a paper.

Your own check belongs in the diagnostic. Ask the tutor to mark one timed piece in front of you against the published criteria and explain each judgement. Ask what they would do differently for a student losing marks in reading versus one losing marks in writing. Ask how they would improve handwriting speed. Three concrete answers mean you are talking to someone who has prepared students for this paper. A tutor who answers all three by describing more practice has not.

The limit on what a tutor may do does not relax as a deadline approaches, and in the exam term it comes under the most pressure. A tutor teaches, sets practice, marks drafts, annotates against criteria and explains losses in detail. A tutor does not write, redraft, dictate or supply any part of anything the student submits for assessment. A parent asking for just a little help with the final version is asking for something that puts the diploma at risk, and a good tutor will say no. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade this close to a paper, and treat a promise of a specific score as a signal to look elsewhere. We do not guarantee grades.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: the technique that actually moves marks
paragraphs: Start with reading, because it is where the quickest gains sit for a student in Mumbai, Maharashtra who already understands spoken Hindi. The discipline is evidence. Read the question first, go to the passage, find the span of text that answers it, mark that span, then write. Where the question permits it, use the language of the passage rather than paraphrasing into vocabulary the student prefers, because paraphrase is where meaning quietly shifts. Answer the number of points the question asks for and no more, since an extra wrong point can cancel a right one. If a question cannot be answered from anything in the passage, the student has misread the question, not the text.

Listening is a composure problem more than a comprehension problem. Use the time before the audio to read the questions and underline what each one is actually asking for, so the ear is hunting for something specific rather than listening in general. Write in shorthand while the recording plays and complete the sentences afterwards. The failure that costs most is freezing on one missed word and losing the next three answers while trying to recover it. Practise with authentic Hindi at full speed, in short segments repeated several times with a different task each time, rather than long segments slowed down, since slowing the audio removes the exact difficulty being tested.

The writing task breaks into planning, production and handwriting, and families usually only think about the third. Planning is a few minutes spent deciding the text type and its conventions, the audience, the register that follows from that audience, and three content points in order. A student who starts writing immediately will produce a better first paragraph and a worse piece. Production means writing to the task and stopping when the task is done. Handwriting is the piece nobody wants to practise and it is examinable in effect, because an illegible conjunct is an unmarkable conjunct. Devanagari degrades in predictable ways under speed: the shirorekha breaks, matras drift off their letters, and pairs that are already close start to merge. Ten minutes of timed copying three times a week fixes most of it inside a month, and the target is legible at speed rather than beautiful.

Two habits tie all of it together. The first is the student's own error list, built from their own scripts rather than from a textbook, with script errors, grammar errors and register slips kept separately, and sessions working down it rather than covering everything equally. The second is the most underused exercise in this subject: the student marks their own script against the published criteria before the tutor does, writes down the mark they think it deserves and why, and then the two compare. Students are usually generous on register and harsh on accuracy, and finding that out about yourself is worth more than being told. After six or seven rounds of it, a student starts writing with the criteria in their head, which is the actual goal.

sections.heading: What technique work changes at four weeks and over a term
paragraphs: Technique moves faster than language does, which is the encouraging part. Inside four weeks a student who was answering reading questions from memory can be reliably answering them from the text, because that is a habit rather than a skill. Within the same month, planning before writing can become automatic and handwriting speed can improve measurably if the copying practice is actually happening. What does not move in four weeks is vocabulary range or grammatical accuracy, and a tutor who promises those on that timescale is selling something. Judge the first month of IB DP Hindi B home tuition in Mumbai on habits, not on marks.

Across a term the marks usually do move, and they move unevenly. Reading tends to improve first and most visibly. The writing task improves in jumps, because fixing the text type moves a whole band at once and then progress flattens until register and accuracy catch up. Listening improves slowly and steadily with exposure. The useful sign at a term is not a higher mock percentage but a script in which the losses have changed character: no longer scattered, but concentrated in the two or three things still being worked on. That is what a well-run term produces.

Across a full exam cycle, the truthful account is that preparation, teaching and the student's starting point all contribute and none of them is a promise, and we will not pretend otherwise. On cost, what matters is what fees depend on rather than any published figure: the level, how scarce experienced Hindi B teachers are next to tutors in larger subjects, travel, session length and frequency, and whether sessions are at home or online. IB tuition fees in Mumbai are quoted as a range against your actual request. If the tutor is not working, say so and we replace them, carrying across the error list and the marked scripts so nothing restarts from zero.

sections.heading: Arranging Hindi B home tuition in Mumbai before the exam term
paragraphs: Three things to have in hand before the first call, and the first one does most of the work. Send the most recent mock or class test script with the question paper attached, because where the marks were lost decides which tutor you need. Send the school's mock fortnight and, if the oral has not happened yet, its window. Then send the slots that are genuinely workable, and split them honestly into term-time evenings and study-leave daytimes, because those are two different availability problems and the second one widens your choice of tutor considerably.

The diagnostic session should look like a small examination with a conversation after it. Expect the tutor to set one timed piece and watch it being written, to run one reading passage and ask the student to show which words licensed each answer, and to look at a page of handwriting produced at speed. Expect them afterwards to tell you which of the four components is costing the most and what the first six weeks will change, in writing. A session spent discussing the syllabus in the abstract has told you what their teaching looks like.

Whichever one you typed, a counsellor reads your message and the script you attach, and calls you back with two or three names rather than a brochure. faqs.question: My son understands the reading passage but still loses marks. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always he is answering from what he knows rather than from what the passage says. Understanding a text and demonstrating that understanding against the question asked are two different performances, and the second is the one being marked. The fix is mechanical and works quickly: before writing anything, find and mark the words in the passage that license the answer. If nothing can be marked, the question has been misread. Students who adopt this habit tend to see reading marks move within a month, faster than any other part of the paper.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our home in Ghatkopar during study leave in the daytime?
faqs.answer: Yes, and daytime during study leave is the easiest week of the year to arrange IB DP Hindi B home tuition in Mumbai's Central Suburbs. Ghatkopar sits on the Central Line and Metro Line 1, so tutors can reach you from Powai, Kurla, Vikhroli, Andheri East or Mulund in a fraction of the evening time. Tell the counsellor at the outset that you want daytime exam-term slots, because it widens the shortlist considerably and some excellent tutors who cannot do 7pm anywhere are completely free at 11am. Fix the slots before study leave starts rather than during it.

faqs.question: How long should a student spend planning before starting the Hindi B writing task?
faqs.answer: A few minutes, spent on four decisions rather than on an outline of the content. Which text type the task requires and what conventions come with it. Who the audience is. Which register follows from that audience. And three content points in the order they will appear. That is the whole plan. Students who start writing immediately almost always produce a strong opening paragraph and a weaker piece overall, because the text type and register get decided accidentally by the first sentence instead of deliberately before it.

faqs.question: Is practising handwriting worth the time, or is that effort better spent elsewhere?
faqs.answer: It is worth it if handwriting is degrading under speed, and in Devanagari that is easy to check. Have the student copy a passage for ten minutes under a timer and look at the last third against the first. If the shirorekha is breaking, matras are drifting off their letters or similar letters are merging, that is lost marks, because an illegible form cannot be credited. Ten minutes of timed copying three times a week usually fixes it within a month. The target is legible at speed, not attractive.

faqs.question: My daughter writes long answers and still loses marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because length is not what is being rewarded, and extra text carries extra risk. Once a task has been fulfilled, continuing adds opportunities for grammatical error and register slips without adding anything the criteria credit. It also eats time that the rest of the paper needs. The habit to build is finishing deliberately: when the three planned points are made in the right text type and register, stop and use the remaining minutes to check agreement and script. Students find stopping genuinely hard, so it needs practising like anything else.

faqs.question: How do we practise listening under exam timing at home?
faqs.answer: With short authentic clips at full speed and a stopwatch, rather than long clips played slowly. Pick a two or three minute news segment or interview, give the student the questions first with a minute to read and underline what each one wants, play it under the same conditions the paper would use, and mark immediately. Repeat the same clip with a different task rather than reaching for a new one. The skill being built is composure: not freezing on a missed word and losing the next three answers while trying to recover it.

faqs.question: Should the student mark their own script against the criteria?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most underused exercise in this subject. Have the student mark their own timed piece against the published criteria, write down what they think it deserves and why, and only then compare with the tutor's marking. The disagreements teach more than the agreements. Students are typically generous to themselves on register and unduly harsh on small accuracy errors, and discovering that pattern about their own judgement changes how they write. After six or seven rounds, the criteria start operating while they write rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: The listening recordings feel too fast. Should we slow them down to practise?
faqs.answer: No, because the speed is part of what is being tested and removing it removes the practice. Use short segments at full pace and repeat them instead, with a different task on each pass: gist first, then specific details, then the speaker's attitude. Three passes over two minutes of real Hindi builds more capacity than ten minutes played at reduced speed. Students in Mumbai who are used to the Hindi spoken around them sometimes find an unfamiliar accent or a more formal delivery harder than the pace itself, and exposure is the only cure for that.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Juhu for a morning slot during the mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: Yes, and mornings are when travel in the Western Suburbs stops being the limiting factor. Juhu is reachable from Vile Parle, Santacruz West, Andheri West and Khar in a short run off-peak, and the Western Express Highway at eleven in the morning behaves nothing like it does at seven in the evening. Book the mock fortnight slots a few weeks ahead, because that period is when demand concentrates across the city. If the school has already set exam leave dates, send them with your first message so the slots can be held.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Hindi B student work through?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families assume, each one worked much harder. A paper attempted under time, marked by the student, marked again by the tutor, discussed, and then partially redone with the corrections applied is worth five papers attempted and filed. Volume without analysis simply rehearses the same errors. Your school is the proper source for past material, and the honest answer on quantity is that it depends on how much of the technique is already in place. A student still answering reading from memory needs analysis, not more papers.

faqs.question: What should the last two weeks before the Hindi B exam look like?
faqs.answer: Consolidation and calm, not new learning. Short daily contact with Hindi, one or two full timed pieces rather than many, a focused pass over the student's own recurring error list, and continued reading of authentic material to keep the eye quick. Nothing new should be introduced. Sleep and routine do more for performance in a language paper than another late revision session, and a student who arrives tired writes slower and less legibly, which in Devanagari costs real marks. The error list is the right revision document at that stage.

sections.heading: Finding an IB DP Hindi B home tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: The request that reaches us is rarely just the subject name. It is usually a parent saying the written work comes back marked down for reasons nobody at home can interpret, or that the oral is in a few weeks and the student freezes. So when a family asks for an IB DP Hindi B home tutor in Mumbai, the matching conversation is about components rather than about the subject in general. A student whose problem is Paper 1 needs a tutor who marks writing closely and insists on redrafts. A student whose problem is the oral needs someone who will spend most of the hour making them talk, which is a different temperament.

Here is the order things happen in. 1. You tell us the year, the level, the school, and which component the school's comments are pointing at. 2. A counsellor asks you to send a photograph of the most recent piece of marked Hindi writing, with the teacher's comments still on it. 3. We shortlist two or three tutors whose Hindi B experience matches that component and whose travel radius reaches your address at the hour you are free. 4. You book a paid first session, which should end with the tutor naming specific, repeated errors. 5. If the naming is vague, tell us and we change the tutor.

The marked script is the most useful single thing a parent can send, and far more useful than a report grade. A teacher's comment such as unsuitable register or incorrect text type tells an experienced Hindi B tutor exactly which kind of teaching is needed, and it is the sort of comment parents most often read as mysterious. A page returned with matra corrections points somewhere else entirely. Families in Chembur, Walkeshwar and Bandra East have all arrived with the same opening sentence about marks going down, and the marked pages underneath told three unrelated stories.

sections.heading: Hindi B at Standard and Higher Level in the Diploma Programme
paragraphs: Hindi B belongs to the language acquisition group of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), and it is offered at Standard Level (SL) and at Higher Level (HL). It is not Hindi A, the language and literature course, and the difference is not a matter of difficulty labels. Language acquisition courses are built around developing the four skills across prescribed themes; language and literature courses are built around studying texts. The assessment criteria differ accordingly, so experience of one is not a substitute for experience of the other when you are choosing a tutor.

Higher Level asks for more than Standard Level does, including engagement with literary text, and both are examined against the current Hindi B guide rather than against anything a tutoring page can summarise. The IB revises its subject guides on its own cycle, which is why the sensible move is to ask your school's DP coordinator for the current component structure and the school's own internal deadlines. A tutor who quotes you a confident set of paper lengths or component weightings from memory is quoting something that may have changed.

Whether a student sits Hindi B or another language course at all is the school's placement decision taken with the family, usually after looking at previous schooling and a school assessment. This page describes what the Hindi B course asks for so that you can read your child's reports properly. It does not tell you which course your child belongs in, and a tutor should not either. Students coming up from the Middle Years Programme (MYP) language acquisition phases often find the jump in written demand into DP1 is the real change, more than any change in vocabulary load.
bullets: Language acquisition at SL or HL, assessed against the current Hindi B guide

sections.heading: What is assessed in Hindi B writing and the individual oral?
paragraphs: Hindi B is assessed through a Paper 1 writing task, a Paper 2 built from listening and reading components, and an individual oral conducted and marked inside the school before it goes for moderation. The writing task and the oral are where a home tutor makes the clearest difference, because both are productive skills that need a live audience to improve. Paper 2 can be practised reasonably well alone once a student knows how to approach an unseen passage; a written task and a spoken performance cannot.

For Paper 1 the student writes to a task and produces a specific text type, and the text type is a scored element rather than a format preference. A blog, a formal letter, a report, a speech, a set of instructions and a diary entry each have their own conventions in Hindi exactly as they do in English. A formal letter opens and closes with conventional forms of address. A report states rather than persuades and is organised under its own internal structure. A speech addresses the people in front of it. A blog can speak to its reader directly and in a lighter register. Writing an excellent blog when the task asked for a formal letter loses marks that have nothing to do with the student's Hindi.

The individual oral works from a visual stimulus. The student is not describing the picture as an inventory of objects; they are reading it, connecting it to one of the course themes, making a point about it and supporting that point with what is actually in the image. Then the conversation opens out, first around the stimulus and then into the wider themes, and the examiner inside the school will follow where the student leads. This is why a memorised paragraph is a liability: it survives the first thirty seconds and then collapses on the first unscripted question.

sections.heading: Which months put the most pressure on Mumbai Hindi B students?
paragraphs: The oral is the component that decides the shape of a Hindi B year in Mumbai, because its date comes from the school rather than from the examination session. Schools schedule and mark it inside an IB window, and then send the recordings for moderation, which means a DP2 student's spoken preparation has to peak weeks before their written preparation does. Families regularly discover this late. Ask your coordinator for the school's oral window at the start of DP2, and build the tutoring schedule backwards from it rather than from the May session.

The written pressure stacks differently. Most Mumbai IB schools run mock examinations in the winter months, so a DP2 student is often producing Paper 1 practice, a subject Internal Assessment in another subject, and a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay draft inside the same fortnight. Hindi B tends to be the thing that gets dropped in that fortnight, which is precisely when the writing practice is most valuable. The monsoon months from June to September cost sessions to waterlogging around Sion, Kurla, Dadar and the Milan and Andheri subways, so a home tutor and a family should fix a monsoon fallback in advance rather than improvising on the evening.

sections.heading: Is a home tutor better than online for Hindi B in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For assessed writing and for the oral, a home tutor has two advantages that are hard to replicate. The first is that an IB DP Hindi B home tutor in Mumbai sits beside the page while it is being written, so a timed task becomes observable: how long the student spends planning, where the pen stops, which letter is formed hesitantly, whether a paragraph was abandoned. The second is social. The oral is a conversation with a real person who can look unconvinced, ask an awkward follow-up and refuse to accept a vague answer, and a student rehearsing against a live interlocutor in the room learns to recover from being thrown.

Online is a real alternative and sometimes the honest recommendation. If your only free slot is late on a weekday, if the student needs three twenty-minute conversation sessions rather than one long one, or if a tutor coming into the flat does not suit the household, IB home tuition in Mumbai is not the only route to the same result. Document sharing makes live correction of a sentence visible as it happens, authentic Hindi audio and video is easier to play, and oral practice over video suits the format. The weakness is handwriting: typing Devanagari is slow and builds the wrong habit, so handwritten work has to be photographed and sent for marking.

Hybrid is what many DP2 families end up running, usually one home session for written work and marking plus one shorter online session for conversation and reading. The trade-off to accept openly is administrative: two modes means corrections can end up in two places, so insist that the tutor keeps a single error log the student can see. A good Hindi B tutor in Mumbai will have a view on which mode suits your child's weak component and will say so before you ask.

sections.heading: Checking a Hindi B home tutor before the first Mumbai session
paragraphs: Screening on our side covers identity, the qualifications a tutor states, their claimed Hindi B teaching and marking experience, and references from earlier families where they exist. For this subject there is one further question that separates candidates quickly: ask them to describe the difference between teaching Hindi and teaching Hindi B. A tutor who answers in terms of text types, register, the oral stimulus and the assessment criteria has taught the course. A tutor who answers in terms of grammar chapters and vocabulary lists has taught Hindi, which is a fine thing to have done and not the same job.

There is checking only you can do, and it takes one session with a pen. Hand the tutor a piece of your child's marked writing and ask them to explain, criterion by criterion, where it lost marks and what the redraft should change. Ask how they would rehearse the oral without the student memorising answers. Ask what they would do with an error that keeps recurring after three weeks. Concrete answers to those three questions are worth more than any claimed track record, and vague answers are worth exactly nothing.

One rule does not bend. A tutor may teach, set practice tasks, mark a draft, annotate against criteria and explain in detail why a paragraph does not work. A tutor may never write, redraft, dictate or supply any part of what your child hands in for assessment, in Hindi or in any other language. An offer to help with the actual submission is a threat to the diploma, not a service. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, and treat anyone who promises a specific score after glancing at one page as someone to pass on. We do not guarantee grades either, and nobody honest in this city does.

sections.heading: Text types, register and the oral: the work a home tutor actually does
paragraphs: Register is where fluent speakers in Mumbai, Maharashtra most often lose marks, and it is the least obvious loss to a parent reading a report. Hindi marks social distance explicitly. The choice between aap, tum and tu pulls the verb forms along with it, honorific plural agreement follows, and the vocabulary a writer reaches for shifts with the setting. Every one of those registers is correct Hindi in its own setting. The scored question is whether the register matches the task: a complaint to a municipal office and a message to a cousin use different language, and a student who writes the first in the voice of the second has made a task error, not a language error. Teaching this is quick once it is named, and it almost never gets named by general Hindi practice.

Text types are the second piece of that work, and the drill that works is comparative rather than sequential. A tutor takes one situation, say a complaint about a flooded lane in Chembur during the monsoon, and has the student write it three ways: as a formal letter to the ward office, as a blog for a neighbourhood page, and as a short speech to a residents' meeting. The content stays constant, so everything that changes between the three versions is exactly what the text type and the register demand. One session of that teaches more than a week of reading model answers, because the student produces the difference instead of recognising it.

The oral needs the opposite of memorisation, and a home tutor is well placed to enforce that. The method is volume and variety of stimulus: a new image every session, the student given a short planning window, then asked to interpret rather than list, then pushed with follow-ups they could not have anticipated. What gets rehearsed is transferable machinery, not content: ways to open, ways to link an image to a theme, ways to buy a second while thinking, ways to say that something is unclear and offer two readings of it. Alongside that runs the error log, which is the single most underrated tool in this subject. Three columns, built from the student's own work rather than from a textbook: script errors such as a misplaced matra, an unstable conjunct or a missing nukta; grammatical errors such as gender agreement or the wrong postposition; and register or vocabulary slips. Sessions work down that list. When an item stops appearing in fresh writing for a month, it comes off.

sections.heading: What four weeks, a term and an exam cycle actually change
paragraphs: Four weeks buys diagnosis and the start of a habit, not a mark. By then you should have an error log with real entries, two or three pieces of timed writing that were marked and then redrafted, and at least two oral rehearsals on different stimuli. The test of whether the sessions are working at one month is whether your child can tell you what their three recurring errors are. If they cannot, nobody has told them, and that is the tutor's omission rather than the student's.

A term changes accuracy and it changes nerve. Script errors that were random become rare, register stops being accidental, the student stops writing to length and starts writing to the task, and the oral starts to sound like someone with an opinion rather than someone reciting. Teachers tend to comment on this before any internal mark moves, so a report comment that has become more specific is usually a good sign rather than a worse one. A term is also long enough to judge the logistics honestly: a weekly home session that actually happens beats two that are cancelled by traffic on the Eastern Express Highway.

Over a full exam cycle, the truthful account is that teaching, practice and the student's starting point all contribute and none of them is a promise. Fees reflect this work rather than any outcome, and what they depend on is worth stating plainly: the level, the scarcity of experienced Hindi B teachers compared with Maths or Economics tutors, the travel the slot demands, session length and frequency, and whether sessions are at home or online. IB tuition fees in Mumbai are quoted as a range for your specific request before anyone visits. If a tutor is not working out, you say so, we replace them, and the error log and marked work go across so the new tutor is not starting from a blank page.

sections.heading: Booking Hindi B home tuition in Mumbai
paragraphs: Three things to have ready, and none of them takes preparation. The most recent marked piece of your child's Hindi writing, photographed with the teacher's comments visible, because that single page tells a counsellor more than a term's worth of grades. The school's oral window if you already know it, or a note to ask the coordinator for it at the next opportunity. And the two or three weekly slots that genuinely survive school, travel home and whatever sport or music already owns a weekday evening. A slot that looks free on a timetable and fails in practice costs a month of momentum before anyone admits it is not working.

The first session should be a diagnostic with a pen in it. Expect the tutor to set a short timed piece of writing, watch it being produced by hand, run one oral stimulus cold, and then tell you in plain words what they saw and what the first six weeks will cover. Expect a written summary afterwards. A first session that was mostly conversation about credentials has told you something, and what it has told you is to ask for someone else.

faqs.question: Will the tutor mark my son's Paper 1 practice writing at home every week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and weekly marking of timed writing is the main reason to book a home tutor for this subject rather than a group class. The useful version is not a tick and a score: it is annotation against the criteria, a short conversation about why a particular paragraph fails, and then a redraft that the student produces themselves. A piece of writing that is marked but never redrafted teaches very little. Ask any prospective tutor how many redrafts they expect per term; a tutor who expects none is marking rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Our society in Chembur requires a gate pass for every visitor. How does that work for a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: It is routine and it only needs setting up once. Most Mumbai complexes will accept a standing visitor entry for a named tutor on a fixed day and time once a resident registers it, which removes the weekly argument at the gate entirely. Send the tutor your society's rules, the name they should give at the gate, and whether they need to carry identification. In Chembur and the Eastern Suburbs generally, ask them to arrive with a short buffer, because the Eastern Express Highway and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road both misbehave without warning.

faqs.question: How do you rehearse the individual oral without the student memorising answers?
faqs.answer: By changing the stimulus every single session and keeping the preparation window short. A memorised paragraph survives the opening and then falls apart at the first question it did not predict, and the oral is designed to ask exactly that question. What gets practised instead is transferable: how to open, how to connect an image to one of the course themes, how to make a claim and support it from what is visible, how to handle an ambiguity by offering two readings. The student also needs practice at being interrupted, which is uncomfortable and necessary.

faqs.question: Why does the text type matter so much in the Hindi B writing task?
faqs.answer: Because the text type is part of what is being assessed, not a presentation choice. A formal letter, a report, a blog, a speech and a set of instructions each carry their own conventions in Hindi, including how they open and close, how formal the language is, how the writer addresses the reader and how the whole thing is organised. A student can write grammatically excellent Hindi and still lose marks by producing the wrong text type for the task. The quickest fix is writing the same content three ways and seeing what has to change.

faqs.question: Can the tutor correct the draft my daughter submits to the school?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor can teach the skill, set a parallel practice task, mark that practice piece in detail and explain exactly which criteria it misses. A tutor cannot write, redraft, dictate or supply any part of work that goes to the school for assessment, and no deadline changes that. Teachers in Mumbai read a lot of their students' writing and recognise prose that does not sound like them, and the consequences for a diploma are serious. Practising on a parallel task is also better teaching, because the student has to transfer the skill rather than receive a correction.

faqs.question: What is register in Hindi, and why do confident speakers lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: Register is the level of formality a piece of language carries, and in Hindi it is marked unusually clearly. Choosing aap, tum or tu changes the verb forms that follow, honorific agreement comes with it, and the words a writer reaches for shift with the setting. All of those registers are correct Hindi. Marks are lost when the register does not match the task, which happens easily to someone whose Hindi comes mainly from conversation at home and with friends. It is a task-awareness problem, quick to teach once a tutor names it.

faqs.question: Do we need a separate study room, or can home classes run at the dining table?
faqs.answer: The dining table is fine and often better. What a Hindi B session needs is a flat writing surface, decent light, a chair the student can sit upright in for timed writing, and no television in earshot during the listening and oral work. What it does not need is a dedicated room. Two practical requests: keep the phone out of reach during a timed piece, and let the oral rehearsal happen somewhere the student is not performing in front of a younger sibling, because self-consciousness does more damage to spoken practice than noise does.

faqs.question: The same mistakes come back every week. Should we switch to a workbook instead?
faqs.answer: No, the repetition is the signal that the error log is working and the drilling has not gone deep enough yet. A general workbook gives a student a hundred exercises, of which perhaps six touch their actual problem. The better response is narrower: take the two errors that recur most, build short daily practice around only those, and have the tutor check fresh writing for them specifically rather than marking everything equally. An error leaves the list when it has not appeared in new work for about a month, which is a real test rather than a feeling.

faqs.question: Should the tutor coordinate with our school's Hindi teacher?
faqs.answer: Coordination is helpful and should run through you rather than around you. The genuinely useful information from the school is the oral window, the internal deadline calendar and the teacher's own view of the weak component, and a parent can relay all three in a message. A tutor should not be contacting a school directly or presenting themselves as part of the teaching team, because IB Gram is an independent platform and not affiliated with any school. What the tutor should do is work to the school's calendar rather than invent a parallel one.

faqs.question: How long before the oral should preparation start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families start, and ideally once the school confirms its window at the beginning of DP2. Spoken fluency improves with distributed practice rather than concentrated practice, so eight short rehearsals spread over two months do far more than four long ones in the last fortnight. The last two weeks should be about calm and familiarity with the format, not about new learning. If you are already inside those last two weeks, the sensible plan is frequent short sessions on fresh stimuli and nothing else.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Walkeshwar for an early evening slot on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in South Mumbai that slot is usually filled from inside the island rather than from the suburbs. Walkeshwar, Babulnath and Peddar Road addresses are commonly covered by tutors living around Girgaon, Tardeo, Worli or Parel, who reach you without touching the evening peak on the Western Express Highway. The constraint is the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals, so an early evening start is more reliable than a 7pm one. Tutors brought down from Andheri or Borivali for a weekday evening rarely sustain the schedule across a full term.

sections.heading: Matching an IB DP Hindi B online tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Families ask for online for one of three reasons, and the reason changes the match. The first is travel: a node in Navi Mumbai or an address past Majiwada on Ghodbunder Road where no tutor will reliably arrive at 7pm for eight months. The second is frequency: a student who needs three short conversation sessions a week rather than one long sitting. The third is household: a flat where a tutor in the living room every Wednesday does not work. When somebody asks for an IB DP Hindi B online tutor in Mumbai, the counsellor's first question is which of those three it is, because a travel-driven request often converts well into a weekend home session plus midweek video.

The sequence is short. 1. You send the year, the level, the school and the reason online suits you. 2. A counsellor calls and listens to the student speak Hindi for two minutes, which happens over the same video setup the lessons will use, so the connection and the audio get tested before anyone pays. 3. You get two or three tutor profiles that state Hindi B experience and how each tutor runs a video session, including how they handle handwritten marking. 4. You book one paid diagnostic session. 5. After it you continue, switch to a home tutor, or ask for someone else.

Asking a tutor to describe their online method before you book is not an imposition, it is the whole decision. Two tutors with identical subject knowledge can run completely different sessions on a screen, and the difference is visible in a single question: what proportion of the hour does the student speak? A tutor who answers with a number and a reason has thought about it. A tutor who answers by describing their materials has not, and on video that gap widens, because a screen makes presenting easy and makes conversation take effort.

sections.heading: Hindi B in the Diploma Programme, and which parts suit a screen
paragraphs: Hindi B is a language acquisition subject in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), taught at Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL), and it is a separate course from Hindi A, which is language and literature. The practical meaning for an online schedule is that Hindi B is built around four skills rather than around a set of texts, and the four skills do not all transfer to video equally. Listening and speaking transfer well. Reading transfers adequately. Writing in script transfers only with a workaround, which the rest of this page describes.

Higher Level demands more than Standard Level, including engagement with literary text, and the official structure of papers and criteria lives in the current Hindi B subject guide. The IB revises those guides on its own schedule, so treat your school's DP coordinator as the authority on what your child is actually sitting, and treat any tutor who recites component weightings from memory with mild suspicion. What a tutor should be able to do confidently is describe the skills each component tests and how to build them.

Whether a student is placed in Hindi B rather than another language course is settled between the school and the family, typically after looking at previous schooling and a school assessment. This page does not advise on that, and a tutor should not either. One thing worth saying plainly to families weighing it up: students who already speak Hindi comfortably sometimes assume the course will be light work, and the written components regularly correct that assumption. Students arriving from the Middle Years Programme (MYP) usually find the written demand is the step change, not the vocabulary.

sections.heading: Which Hindi B components work well over video?
paragraphs: Hindi B is assessed through a Paper 1 writing task, a Paper 2 made of listening and reading, and an individual oral held at the school. Ranked by how well they suit online teaching, the individual oral comes first, listening second, reading third and the writing task last. That ranking should determine the shape of your schedule rather than being discovered three months in.

The oral is the strongest case for video and it is underrated. The component is a conversation conducted from a visual stimulus, so a screen is close to the native format. A tutor can put a fresh image up instantly, keep a bank of stimuli the student has never seen, run the planning window on a visible timer, and record the rehearsal so the student can hear their own hesitations afterwards. Hearing yourself pause before every postposition is more persuasive than being told about it. Listening practice benefits similarly, because the tutor can share audio directly instead of holding a phone up in a room.

Reading works online with one discipline attached: the passage has to be on paper in front of the student, not on the same screen as the tutor's face. A student reading an unseen Hindi passage on a laptop while a video call runs beside it is practising something other than what the exam asks. Print it or put it on a second device. The writing task is the component that online handles worst, and pretending otherwise is the most common dishonesty on pages like this one. An IB DP Hindi B online tutor in Mumbai can teach text type, structure, planning and register perfectly well through a screen. What a screen cannot do unaided is watch a hand form a conjunct.

paragraphs: Navi Mumbai is where online earns its place most clearly. The nodes are planned and close to each other on Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are matched to each other for home classes and that works well. What does not work is pulling a tutor across the creek from the island city for a weekday evening, and the Atal Setu has shortened that crossing without making it sensible as a twice-weekly habit. So the pattern that holds for a Kharghar or Panvel family is a local home tutor at the weekend for written work, and video midweek for conversation, listening and oral rehearsal. The Harbour Line, the Trans-Harbour Line and the Navi Mumbai Metro between Belapur and Pendhar matter for the weekend tutor and are irrelevant to the midweek one, which is exactly the point.

Thane runs on the same logic for a different reason. The city spreads from the station east across Pokhran Road and Majiwada and out along Ghodbunder Road, and that Ghodbunder stretch sets everything: a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening crawl. For a family out towards Kasarvadavali, an evening video session simply happens, while an evening home session is a negotiation with traffic every week. Thane tutors cover Thane, Mulund tutors sometimes cross over the Eastern Express Highway, and the Thane Borivali tunnel corridor will change the arithmetic again when it is in use.

In the Western Suburbs, Bandra, Khar, Juhu, Andheri West, Malad and Borivali are well served for home tuition along the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7, so online there is usually about frequency rather than distance. sections.heading: How do Mumbai school calendars fit an online schedule?
paragraphs: An online schedule is easier to protect than a home one, and that advantage is worth spending deliberately. Mumbai IB schools run their academic year from after the summer through to the spring, with the May session at the end of DP2, mock examinations in the winter months and the individual oral scheduled by the school inside an IB window. The weeks that destroy tutoring schedules are the mock fortnight, the examination leave period and the monsoon. Video removes the monsoon problem entirely, which in this city is not a small thing: the evenings when Sion, Kurla, Dadar and the Andheri and Milan subways go under are the evenings a home session is cancelled.

Use the flexibility rather than just enjoying it. During the heaviest weeks, when a DP2 student has a subject Internal Assessment (IA) due alongside a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay draft, a full hour of Hindi B often gets cancelled outright. Two twenty-five minute video conversations survive the same fortnight, keep the spoken work alive and cost the student far less. Through the long DP1 stretch from August to the winter break, when there is genuine room, the ratio should tilt the other way towards longer sessions with written work in them.

Students booking Hindi B support online come from across the city's IB schools, including Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR, JBCN International School, Borivali, Singapore International School in Dahisar East and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai. Naming them says something about calendars and nothing about relationships. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any of those schools or with the International Baccalaureate organisation, and we do not guarantee grades.

sections.heading: Online, home classes or both for Hindi B in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition remains the lead service and it is the right first answer for a specific profile: a student whose handwriting in Devanagari is itself the problem, a student who will not stay in a video call without someone in the room, or a family close enough to a capable tutor that travel is not a factor. An IB home tutor in Mumbai sitting at the table watches the pen, catches the matra as it goes in the wrong place and can simply take the paper and point. Nothing on a screen matches that for script work in the first few months.

Online is the right first answer for a different and equally real profile. A Kharghar, Panvel or Kasarvadavali address where tutors cancel. A student who needs frequency more than duration. A household where an outsider's weekly visit is inconvenient. A family who want a specialist Hindi B teacher rather than whoever is available within four kilometres, which for this subject matters more than it does for Maths, because experienced Hindi B teachers are not evenly spread across the city. IB home tuition in Mumbai cannot always supply a subject specialist to a distant node; video can.

Hybrid is the arrangement most DP2 families converge on and it deserves to be chosen rather than drifted into. One home session a week for timed writing and face-to-face marking, one or two short video sessions for conversation, listening and oral rehearsal. The trade-off is honest: two modes create two places for notes to live, two sets of scheduling, and a slightly higher chance that something gets dropped. The fix is one shared file and one calendar. Ask a prospective tutor to describe the hybrid week they would run for your child, and if the answer is a shrug, that tutor should be doing one mode only.

sections.heading: What to check before the first online Hindi B session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Our screening covers identity, stated qualifications, claimed Hindi B teaching experience and references from previous families where they exist. For an IB DP Hindi B online tutor in Mumbai there are two further checks we make that do not apply to a home tutor. The first is whether they have actually taught this subject on video rather than improvising it, which shows up immediately in whether they have a stimulus bank and a marking workflow. The second is their audio, because a tutor with poor microphone quality is teaching a listening-heavy subject through a filter.

Your own checks fit inside the diagnostic session. Watch how much your child speaks. Ask the tutor to share a document and correct one of your child's sentences live, so you can see whether correction is a conversation or a lecture. Ask them to show you how handwritten work comes back marked. Ask what Hindi audio or video they would use this term and whether they play it at full speed. A tutor who slows every clip down is removing the difficulty the listening component exists to test.

The boundary is identical online and at home, and the screen makes it easier to cross, which is why it needs saying twice. A tutor may teach, set practice, mark a draft against criteria and explain every lost mark in detail. A tutor may never write, redraft, dictate or type any part of what your child submits for assessment. A shared document is a teaching tool and not a drafting service, and a tutor who starts typing into your child's actual submission has stopped being a tutor. Be wary of anyone offering a guaranteed grade, and read a tutor who promises a specific score as a reason to look elsewhere.

sections.heading: The script problem: typed Devanagari is not writing practice
paragraphs: This is the thing online Hindi B gets wrong most often, and in Mumbai, Maharashtra it bites hardest because so many students here speak Hindi daily and have done almost all their formal writing in English. Typing Devanagari on a phone or a laptop is usually done by transliteration: the student types a word in Roman letters and picks the Hindi form from a list. The machine supplies the matra, chooses the conjunct and places the nukta. The student recognises the right answer instead of producing it, which is a different cognitive act and a much easier one. In a handwritten examination nothing supplies anything. A student who has typed their way through two years can read fluently, compose well and still slow to a crawl when the hand has to do the work.

The workable rule is a split. Type for thinking, write by hand for producing. Planning, outlining, vocabulary work and live sentence correction belong in a shared document where the tutor edits in a visible colour and the student watches the change happen and says why it was needed. Actual production, every timed piece and every redraft, is handwritten on paper. The student photographs the page, one page per image, in daylight or under a lamp rather than in their own shadow, and sends it before the session. The tutor annotates it and returns it, and the session is spent on the annotations rather than on reading the work cold. Families who set this up in week one stop noticing it by week four; families who never set it up discover the problem during mocks.

Two more things belong in a well-run online session. The first is authentic Hindi at real speed: news bulletins, interviews, podcast segments, documentary clips, played at full pace and in short pieces repeated three times rather than long pieces played once. Online makes this trivially easy because the tutor shares audio directly. The second is a single shared file that both of them keep open. One half is the student's recurring errors, taken from their own photographed scripts: unstable conjuncts, gender agreement, the postposition that keeps going wrong. The other half is a growing bank of phrases the student can actually deploy, for opening an oral, linking an image to a theme, conceding a point, or signposting a paragraph. Sessions work down the first half and the student revises from the second between them. For a Hindi B tutor in Mumbai teaching remotely, that file does the job the shared table does at home.

sections.heading: Progress over four weeks, a term and an exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks the honest measures for an online arrangement are mechanical, and you should check them. Is the photographed handwriting workflow actually running every week, or did it lapse after the second session? Does the shared file have entries in both halves? Can your child name their recurring errors? Is the student doing most of the talking? Those four questions catch almost every failing online setup, and none of them is about Hindi. A tutor who has let the handwriting workflow lapse has quietly turned the course into a conversation class.

A term shows up in speed and in nerve. Spoken Hindi loses its hesitations, the student stops translating from English mid-sentence, unseen reading stops producing panic, and handwritten pieces come back with fewer script errors and are finished inside the time. The oral is where online students often move fastest, because video rehearsal is cheap to repeat and they have simply done more of it than their classmates. Writing speed is the thing to watch most carefully, since it is the one that a screen does not fix on its own.

Over an exam cycle the fair statement is that teaching and practice and starting point all contribute and none of them is a promise. What fees depend on is worth saying without inventing figures: the level, the scarcity of experienced Hindi B teachers, session length and frequency, and whether travel is involved, which is why IB tuition fees in Mumbai usually come out lower online than for home classes at the same length. We do not guarantee grades. If a tutor is not working, tell us and we change them, and the shared error file transfers so the next tutor starts from what is already known.

The tutor listens to your child talk for several minutes before saying anything substantive, runs one unseen oral stimulus cold, sets a short handwritten piece to be photographed afterwards, and checks a reading passage on paper. Then they tell you what they found and what the first six weeks will cover, in writing. If the session was mostly the tutor sharing slides, you have learned what their normal lesson looks like.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor make sense for Hindi B when the exam is handwritten?
faqs.answer: It does, provided every piece of production is written by hand on paper and photographed for marking. Online teaches text type, planning, register, reading strategy and the oral at least as well as a tutor at the table, and in some cases better. What it cannot do by itself is supervise the physical act of writing Devanagari. A tutor who accepts typed Hindi as practice is removing the exact difficulty the examination tests. Ask about the handwriting workflow in the first conversation and treat a vague answer as disqualifying.

faqs.question: How does the tutor mark handwritten Hindi if the session is on video?
faqs.answer: The student photographs each page, one page per image in decent light, and sends it before the session rather than during it. The tutor annotates it, usually on a PDF or marked-up image, returns it, and the session is spent discussing the annotations and producing a redraft. Sending it in advance is the part families skip, and it is what makes the difference, because a tutor reading a script cold on screen loses a third of the lesson. Set the habit in the first fortnight and it stops being a chore.

faqs.question: Can we switch to a home tutor in Thane later if online is not working?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a fair number of families do, usually after a term. The switch is handled as an ordinary rematch: you tell us what is not working, we find a tutor whose travel radius covers your address at your hour, and the shared error file and marked scripts go across so nothing is relearned. In Thane the practical constraint is Ghodbunder Road in the evening, so an address near Kasarvadavali may suit a weekend home slot better than a weekday one. Many families keep both and run a hybrid week instead of choosing.

faqs.question: We are in Kharghar and tutors keep refusing the commute. Is online the answer?
faqs.answer: Often yes, at least for part of the week. Navi Mumbai is matched node to node, so a Kharghar family can usually find a capable tutor in Kharghar, Belapur or Nerul for a weekend home session, while the midweek work moves to video. What does not hold is a tutor crossing from the island city twice a week; the Atal Setu makes it possible and the schedule still breaks by November. Online also widens the choice to specialist Hindi B teachers anywhere in the city rather than only those within driving distance.

faqs.question: What equipment does an online Hindi B session actually need?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect, with two exceptions. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, a stable connection and headphones are enough for most of it, and headphones matter because the listening component rewards clear audio. The two exceptions are a phone camera good enough to photograph a handwritten page legibly, and paper. A second screen or a printout is useful for reading passages, so the student is not reading Hindi on the same surface as the tutor's face. No special software, no Devanagari keyboard.

faqs.question: Is the individual oral easier to practise over video?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, and it is the strongest argument for online in this subject. The oral is a conversation built from a visual stimulus, which is very close to what a video call already is. A tutor can present a fresh image instantly, keep a bank the student has never seen, time the planning window visibly, and record the rehearsal so the student hears their own hesitations played back. Repetition is the thing that improves spoken performance, and video makes repetition cheap. The school conducts the real oral in person, which is a minor adjustment.

faqs.question: Does my child need to type in Devanagari for online sessions?
faqs.answer: Not for anything that counts as writing practice, and this is worth being firm about. Transliteration typing means the student types in Roman letters and selects the Hindi form from a list, so the software chooses the matra, builds the conjunct and places the nukta. That is recognition, not recall, and the examination asks for recall by hand. Typing is fine for planning notes, vocabulary lists and live sentence correction in a shared document. Every timed piece and every redraft should be handwritten on paper and photographed.

faqs.question: How do we stop an online session turning into the tutor talking?
faqs.answer: Ask for a target at the start and check it at the end of the first month. A reasonable expectation in a language acquisition subject is that the student speaks for most of the session, and a tutor who has thought about video teaching will have a plan for achieving it: open questions, genuine silences left unfilled, the tutor muting themselves while the student works through an answer. Screens make presenting easy and conversation effortful, which is why passive sessions are the characteristic failure mode of online language teaching.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a session?
faqs.answer: The tutor reconnects or calls on audio, and the missed minutes are made up rather than absorbed. Agree the rule before it happens: a short drop is recovered within the session, and a loss of more than about ten minutes is rescheduled or credited. Mumbai connections fail most often during heavy monsoon weeks, so a sensible pair of tutor and family also agrees a phone fallback for the conversation part, which works surprisingly well for listening and speaking even though it is useless for anything on screen.

faqs.question: Can the tutor use real Hindi news and video, or is that too difficult for a Hindi B student?
faqs.answer: Authentic material at full speed should be part of the course from early on, and the way to make it manageable is short clips repeated rather than long clips slowed down. A two-minute news segment played three times, with a different task each time, builds more listening capacity than ten minutes played once at reduced speed. Slowing audio down removes the exact difficulty being tested. Online makes this easier because the tutor shares the audio directly instead of playing something from a phone across a room.

faqs.question: Do online sessions cost less than home tuition in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because the travel comes out of the equation, and travel is a real cost in this city for an evening slot in Powai or on Ghodbunder Road. Everything else that sets the fee stays the same: the level, the length and frequency of sessions, and how scarce experienced Hindi B teachers are compared with tutors in larger subjects. We quote a range for your specific request rather than publishing a price list, because a weekend home session in Kharghar and three short video conversations are not the same product priced differently.

A counsellor tests the audio on the call, listens to the student speak, and sends two or three Hindi B tutor profiles with their video method described, not just their qualifications. You book one paid diagnostic and get written findings. If a tutor at the table would serve your child better, we will say so and arrange it instead.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram find an IB DP Hindi B private tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: A request for an IB DP Hindi B private tutor in Mumbai arrives in one of two shapes. Either a DP1 student has been placed in Hindi B and the first report card came back below what the family expected, or a DP2 student is a few months from the May session and the writing paper is the hole. Those two students need different tutors, and the shortlist should not look the same for both. The first part of a match is spent working out which one you actually have.

Hindi B is a small pool in Mumbai compared with Maths or Economics. Plenty of people teach Hindi. Far fewer have taught the Diploma Programme (DP) version of it, marked a Paper 1 writing task against the assessment criteria, or run an individual oral under something close to real conditions. So the filter is not whether somebody speaks Hindi well. It is which year groups they have taught, which text types they have set, and whether they can show a script they have marked with the criteria written in the margin.

Before any profile is sent we ask what the school has actually placed the student in, and whether the Diploma Programme coordinator has been consulted. That is not a formality. A good share of the requests that arrive as "my child needs Hindi B help" are really "my child may be in the wrong course or the wrong level", and no tutor can fix that from the outside. The school decides placement together with the family. A tutor's job is to describe what the course demands honestly enough that the conversation is an informed one.

Then you get a short list rather than a catalogue. Two or three profiles, each with a line explaining why that person fits this student. You run one diagnostic session, the tutor sets a short written task and marks it where you can see the marking happen, and you decide after that rather than before it.

5. Keep that tutor, or ask for a rematch after the first week.

sections.heading: Hindi B, Hindi A or another language: whose decision is it?
paragraphs: The school decides, together with the family, and nobody else. In the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) a student takes one subject from language and literature and one from language acquisition. Hindi A sits in the first of those groups and Hindi B in the second, and which one a student is placed in depends on the school's own policy, what the student has studied before, and a conversation with the Diploma Programme coordinator.

Language acquisition courses assume prior learning of the language. Hindi B is built for a student who has studied Hindi before and can already work in it. There is a separate beginners' route inside the language acquisition group for students with no background in a language at all, and it is not interchangeable with Hindi B. Schools in Mumbai usually timetable a small set of language options rather than the full catalogue, so the real choice a family faces is often Hindi B, French B, Spanish B or Hindi A, bounded by what that particular school runs in that particular year.

Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) are the other half of the decision. Both levels sit the same named components, a Paper 1 writing task, a Paper 2 made of listening and reading, and the individual oral. Higher Level asks for more range in the written work and carries a demand that Standard Level does not. Exactly what that demand is for the year your child sits the exam is a question for the current subject guide and your school's coordinator, because the IB revises its subject guides on its own cycle and a figure or a structure quoted on a website can be out of date by the time you read it.

There is usually a window early in DP1 when a subject or level change is still administratively possible. It is short, it varies by school, and it tends to close well before the first substantial assessment tells you anything useful. If a change might be on the table, raise it with the coordinator in the first term rather than waiting for a DP1 end-of-year result. A tutor can give you a read on whether the student is coping with the written demand. The registration decision stays with the school and the family.
bullets: Hindi A is language and literature; Hindi B is language acquisition.
The beginners' acquisition route is a different course, not a lighter Hindi B.
A Hindi B IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai families book covers both years, not one.
