faqs.question: If we go online, does a tutor still travel to our building at all?
faqs.answer: Not unless you want them to, and plenty of families never have a tutor at the door. Fully online is a normal arrangement and works well for students who write without supervision. Even so, most of our year two History families end up asking for a few home visits anyway, usually for the first diagnostic session and for timed handwritten papers during mock season. Those can be booked individually rather than as a standing weekly slot, which avoids the whole problem of a tutor committing to a weekday evening drive across the city. Tell us at the start if you want that option kept open, because it changes who we shortlist.

faqs.question: Can we keep one home session a week and do the rest online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Diploma Programme History that is the arrangement we recommend most often. The usual pattern is one home session for work that benefits from presence, such as timed handwritten essays and the longer sit-down conversations, plus one shorter online session midweek for planning and marking. It gives you the supervision of home tuition without requiring a tutor to cross Mumbai twice a week, which keeps both the cost and the cancellation rate down. Families in Powai, Chembur and Thane use this split particularly often, because those are exactly the places where a second weekly drive is the thing that breaks the arrangement.

faqs.question: What happens to an online class on a monsoon evening when the power goes?
faqs.answer: Agree the answer in week one and it never becomes an argument. The standard arrangement is that a session interrupted in the first ten minutes is rescheduled, and one interrupted later finishes with written marking of whatever was being worked on, sent the same night. Most tutors will continue on a phone connection if the student can, since History needs voice and a document rather than high bandwidth. Mumbai monsoon evenings genuinely disrupt both power and connections, which is one reason online tends to survive July and August better than a tutor trying to reach Kandivali or Kasarvadavali by road.

faqs.question: Does online really work for History, or is it just the cheaper option?
faqs.answer: It works, and an IB DP History online tutor in Mumbai is not merely the budget option. History is read, argued and written, with no practical component, so almost all of it moves onto a screen intact. The specific gain is marking: comments appearing next to a student's own sentences while they watch are read and acted on in a way that end-of-essay feedback never is. The specific loss is handwriting under time, which has to be covered separately by photographing timed work and having it marked. A student who will not work between sessions is the one case where online is genuinely weaker, and we will say so.

faqs.question: How does marking in a shared document actually work in a session?
faqs.answer: The student's essay is in a file both people can open, and the tutor leaves comments anchored to specific sentences while the student follows along. In a well-run session the tutor has already read and annotated the essay before the call, so the live time goes on discussing four or five located problems rather than on reading. The student then revises one paragraph there and then, with the tutor questioning rather than dictating. Everything stays in the file afterwards, so in March the student can reopen an essay from August and see exactly what was said about it.

faqs.question: My son types everything. Will that hurt him in the examination?
faqs.answer: Yes, if nothing is done about it, and this is the main risk of a fully online arrangement. Diploma Programme History examinations are handwritten under time, and a student who has typed for two years will write more slowly, tire faster and often leave the final answer unfinished with good material still in their head. The fix is unglamorous: regular timed essays written by hand, photographed, and marked for pace and legibility as well as content, starting in year one rather than in mock week. Any tutor on the platform who works with your son online is expected to insist on this.

faqs.question: We are in Kandivali and want a specialist in a particular regional option. Is online the answer?
faqs.answer: Very likely yes. Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar sit at the far end of the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, and a specialist who happens to teach the regional option your child is taking may well live nowhere near that stretch. Insisting on home tuition in that situation usually means accepting a generalist, whereas going online opens the whole pool. If some in-person contact matters to you, book occasional home sessions with a local tutor for timed written work and keep the specialist online for teaching and marking.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for online sessions?
faqs.answer: Level, subject scarcity, session length, frequency and how much marking is involved, and we will not quote a figure because any figure would be invented. Online removes travel from the calculation, which is one of the larger components of an in-person rate in a city this size, but it often adds asynchronous marking time, which is real work that a tutor is right to charge for. History is scarcer than Maths in the Mumbai market and Higher Level work costs more than Standard Level. Ask any tutor to state the rate, what marking is included and the cancellation rule in writing before the second session.

faqs.question: How do you stop an online session becoming the tutor talking for an hour?
faqs.answer: By insisting the student is the one typing. The structural fix is simple: every session should produce something in the shared file that the student wrote, whether a plan, a rewritten paragraph or an annotated source. A tutor who lectures leaves nothing behind, and the file makes that visible within a fortnight. You can check it yourself without sitting in on a class. If after three sessions the document contains only the tutor's material, that is a teaching problem rather than a medium problem, and it is worth raising with us immediately.

faqs.question: The tutor is in another city. Does that matter for Mumbai school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Only if nobody tells them the dates. A tutor outside Mumbai will not absorb your school's internal deadline calendar by osmosis, so send the deadline sheet in the first week and mention the mock window explicitly. Beyond that, the subject is the same everywhere and a specialist elsewhere is often a better match than a generalist nearby. Where local knowledge genuinely counts, such as which library collections a Mumbai student can realistically reach for the internal assessment, say so at the outset and we will weight the shortlist towards tutors who know the city.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor promise a better grade?
faqs.answer: No, and the offer itself tells you something about the tutor. Diploma Programme History is marked by external examiners against published criteria, with internally assessed work moderated externally, and nobody selling tuition has any influence over either process. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. What a serious online tutor will give you is a candid read on the marked work after the first session, a statement of what realistically can change in the time available, and a revised view as evidence accumulates in the shared document. That document is also the reason an online arrangement is easier to audit than an in-person one.

Others are still deciding, or quietly regretting a choice made in a rush. This page is about the decision: who History suits, what students misjudge before picking it, and how home tuition fits around a choice that is still open.

sections.heading: How a private History tutor in Mumbai is matched when the choice is still open
paragraphs: The first question asked is which problem you are solving. A family whose child has chosen History and needs help writing is a different request from a family three weeks into Diploma Programme year one wondering whether the subject was a mistake. The second request needs someone who will give an honest reading of fit, which means it needs a tutor who is willing to lose the booking.

What gets looked at is wider than one subject. The whole six-subject grid matters, because History sits in a timetable alongside five other courses with their own written workloads, and the question is never whether a student can cope with History in isolation. A student carrying two essay-heavy subjects plus an extended essay in a third will feel History differently from a student whose other five are quantitative. A History tutor in Mumbai who only looks at History will give you a cheerful answer and the wrong one.

Then come the practical filters. Which prescribed subject and which regional option the school teaches, because that is fixed by the school and not by the student. Whether the family wants a short diagnostic consultation or an ongoing weekly commitment. Which zone the family lives in, and whether a home tutor can realistically reach them on a school evening. Whether the student will speak freely in front of a parent, because a frank conversation about whether she actually wants this subject needs a room where she will say so.

Most families start with one or two sessions framed explicitly as a review rather than as tuition. The tutor reads a piece of the student's writing, talks to her about what she reads for pleasure and what she expects the subject to be, and gives a view. Sometimes that view is that she should stay and the writing load is manageable. Sometimes it is that she should talk to her coordinator this week, before the change window closes. Both are useful answers and you should be told which one you are getting.
bullets: 1. Tell us the school, the level under consideration, and all six subjects on the grid.
2. Say whether you want a fit review or ongoing weekly teaching, since they need different tutors.
3. Send one piece of the student's own written work, timed or untimed.
4. Two or three tutors are shortlisted by prescribed subject, zone and availability.
5. A first session gives a plain verdict on fit before any term-long commitment is discussed.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level History: which decision are you actually making?
paragraphs: You are deciding how much written examination the student sits and how deep one body of material has to go. In the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), History at Standard Level (SL) and Higher Level (HL) share the source paper and the world history essay paper. Higher Level adds a further examined paper on a regional option, and both levels complete the internal assessment known as the historical investigation, which sibling pages here cover in their own right.

The decision is less about ability than about appetite for one particular kind of effort. The extra Higher Level paper is not broader, it is narrower and more detailed, so it rewards a student who is happy to know a smaller amount of history extremely well, including names, sequence and specifics she can produce without notes. A student who likes the sweep of history and dislikes detail often finds Standard Level the better fit and does noticeably better in it. Students and parents tend to read the two levels as a statement about seriousness. Examiners read them as different tasks.

The combination rules are not yours to invent, and they are the most common source of confusion in a first conversation. How many subjects a student may take at each level, which groups must be covered, and how the school's own timetable blocks constrain the grid are all decided by the current guide and by your school's coordinator. Do not plan around what a cousin did two years ago or what a figure in an old brief says, because subject guides are revised on the IB's own cycle. Ask the coordinator for the version the school is teaching and build the plan from that.

A History IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai parents bring in during the first term can help test the level decision in the only way that actually works, which is by having the student attempt a piece of Higher Level style work and seeing what happens. An IB private tutor Mumbai families use purely to deliver more content will not surface the level question at all, because content is the part most students are already fine with.
bullets: SL and HL share the source paper and the world history essay paper
HL adds a regional option paper that rewards depth and precise recall
Both levels complete the historical investigation as internal assessment
Level choice is about appetite for detail more than general ability
Combination and group rules come from the coordinator and the current guide

sections.heading: What History asks of a student who simply likes history
paragraphs: Liking history and being suited to the course are related but not the same thing, and this is the single misjudgement that brings most families to this page. A student who reads popular history, watches documentaries and can talk about the Mughal administration or the Second World War for an hour is enjoying narrative. The course assesses argument. She will be asked, repeatedly and under time, to take a position on a question she did not choose, support it with specific evidence, deal with the strongest objection to it, and reach a verdict. The pleasure of knowing things is not the skill being marked.

The second thing students fail to register is volume. This is a writing subject in the most literal sense. Across two years a History student produces a large quantity of extended prose by hand, under time, in addition to the internal assessment. Students who choose it expecting reading and discussion are genuinely surprised by the hours spent writing, and so are students coming from a Middle Years Programme or an IGCSE background where assessment felt more varied. Before committing, it is worth having the student write one full essay under time and then asking her whether she would willingly do that most weeks for two years.

The third is the gap between spoken and written fluency. Mumbai classrooms are full of students whose spoken English is excellent, who argue well out loud, and who write slowly and flatly on paper. Teachers often read the oral confidence as evidence the writing will come, and it frequently does not come by itself. This student is not in the wrong subject, but she needs the writing treated as a separate skill from day one of Diploma Programme year one rather than discovered at the mock exams. If her spoken reasoning is strong, History can be a good choice, provided somebody is working on written production deliberately. That work is exactly what a home tutor for History Mumbai families book in the first term should be doing.

There is also the regional option to understand before choosing. The examined regional material at Higher Level is selected by the school, not by the student, so a student fascinated by one part of the world may find herself examined on another. A private tutor can feed her interest with extra reading, and cannot change what the paper asks. Ask the school which option it teaches before the student builds an expectation around a region. On any contested ground within that option, including Partition, nationalism and territorial disputes, the course expects students to set out how historians have disagreed and what evidence each position rests on rather than to assert a settled verdict, and a student who wants history to confirm what she already believes will find that frustrating.
bullets: The course marks argument under time, not enthusiasm or general knowledge
Expect a large volume of handwritten extended prose across both years
Strong spoken English does not automatically produce strong written answers
The school picks the regional option; the student cannot choose independently

sections.heading: Private and home tutors across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Thane
paragraphs: Coverage runs across all six zones of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and it is worth starting with the areas usually described last. Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel each sit a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and the Navi Mumbai Metro line running from Belapur towards Pendhar has made some of those hops easier. Matching is node to node. The Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line from Thane to Vashi have both shortened the crossing, and neither makes it sensible to pull a tutor from the island city into Kharghar at seven on a Tuesday evening for the whole term.

The Eastern Suburbs are the other underserved stretch worth naming precisely. Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Mulund sit on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Express Highway and the Monorail from Chembur towards Wadala in between, and the Eastern Freeway puts South Mumbai within reach from Chembur and Wadala far faster than the distance suggests. The Santacruz-Chembur Link Road is the piece that makes a Chembur family reachable from the western side at all, and it is also the first thing to fail in the evening peak. Thane sits north of this, spreading from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road out to Kasarvadavali, with the Thane-Borivali tunnel corridor set to change how Thane and the far Western Suburbs connect.

In the Western Suburbs, matching works along the line rather than across it: Bandra, Khar West and Santacruz as one group, then Juhu and Andheri, then Oshiwara, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar East served by Metro Lines 2A and 7, the Link Road and the Western Express Highway, with the Bandra-Worli Sea Link carrying the traffic that crosses to Worli. The Central Suburbs run Kurla, Ghatkopar, Kanjurmarg and Mulund on the Central Line and Metro Line 1, with Powai and Chandivali reached by road off JVLR. South Mumbai is matched within the island, Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Fort, Tardeo and Walkeshwar, served by the Western and Harbour lines, Metro Line 3 up to BKC and the Coastal Road.

Searches like "IB tutors near me Mumbai" return the whole city, which is exactly the problem. IB DP History private tuition in Mumbai is only worth booking if the weekly slot survives the term, and that is a travel question before it is a teaching question. Where a family lives far from any specialist in their school's regional option, the honest answer is a hybrid arrangement, not a heroic commute. Home tutors are matched within zone first, and the pool is widened only when the subject specialism genuinely cannot be found closer.

sections.heading: When can a Mumbai student still change out of History?
paragraphs: Early in Diploma Programme year one, and the exact deadline belongs to your school rather than to any general rule. Most schools allow subject and level changes in the opening weeks while timetables are still movable, then close the window once candidate registration is submitted. After that, a change becomes difficult or impossible, and the honest advice is to ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the actual date in writing rather than relying on what the student heard from a classmate. Families who delay this conversation by one term usually find they no longer have a decision to make.

The practical complication is work already done. A student who has begun the historical investigation and then switches subject loses that work, because the internal assessment is tied to the subject. The calculation is therefore not only about the next eighteen months, it is about what has to be restarted. A few weeks of preliminary reading is nothing. A substantially advanced piece is a real cost, which is why the fit conversation belongs in the first term and not the second. A tutor can tell you how advanced the work genuinely is, which is often less advanced than the student believes.

The Mumbai calendar sets the rest of the rhythm. The first term carries the change window and the early essay work. The months around September and October in the final year stack internal assessment drafts across several subjects at once, so a History student is often writing her investigation in the same fortnight as two other subject deadlines. Mocks land in January and February of the final year, and the examination session follows in May, with the November session running the same shape six months offset. Diwali and the Christmas break interrupt the term at inconvenient points, and families travel.

Families across the city work to slightly different versions of this. Ascend International School in BKC, Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, the JBCN International School campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Witty International School in Malad and Chembur, Ryan Global School at Kandivali and Worli, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East, Podar International School at Santacruz and Powai and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all run their own internal deadlines and change policies. Those names are local context only. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school listed here, or with the International Baccalaureate organisation. Families booking IB home tuition in Mumbai during the change window should expect a tutor to ask which school policy applies before advising anything.

Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the actual deadline in writing

sections.heading: Private home tuition, online or hybrid in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition leads for this request, and for the subject-choice conversation it leads by a wider margin than usual. A decision about whether a student should continue with History needs the student's school reports, her marked work and often a parent in the room, and all of that is in the house already. It also needs the student to be candid about whether she wants the subject, which happens more readily at her own table than on a call. IB DP History private tutoring in Mumbai delivered at home also means the tutor sees the study space, which tells you something about whether the writing workload is survivable where she actually works.

The cost of home sessions is the tutor's evening. Travel across the Western Express Highway, the Eastern Express Highway or Ghodbunder Road in peak hours consumes time nobody is paid for, which shows up as fewer slots, less flexibility on rescheduling and a narrower choice of specialists for an unusual regional option. Weekly History home classes Mumbai families fix in the first fortnight of term get the best tutors. The same request in the third month gets whatever is left.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai suits a piece of this request unusually well. A single ninety-minute subject-choice consultation, with the grid and the reports shared on screen, does not justify a cross-city journey for either side, and online makes it possible to reach a tutor who knows the school's specific prescribed subject even if she lives in another zone. Ongoing online teaching for a writing-heavy subject works, provided the family actually photographs and sends handwritten work before each session, which is the step most households drop by week four.

Hybrid is what the majority of these arrangements become, and setting it up deliberately beats drifting into it. One home session a week for sustained written work, one shorter online slot for planning and review, and the ratio shifting as the year moves. A home tutor who insists on a fixed pattern for two years is not accounting for a calendar that changes shape every term.

Travel narrows a home tutor's slots and the pool of option specialists

sections.heading: How is an IB DP History private tutor in Mumbai checked?
paragraphs: Identity is verified, qualifications are evidenced against documents rather than accepted from a profile, and teaching experience is recorded specifically: which programme, which level, which prescribed subject. Claims about examining or moderating are the most commonly overstated in this market, so they are treated as claims until a tutor can document them. Family references are collected directly, and tutors are matched to the regional options and prescribed subjects they can actually name.

For this particular request there is a second thing worth checking yourself, because it is a conflict of interest the platform cannot remove. A tutor paid weekly to teach History has an obvious incentive to tell you the student should continue with History. The way to test it is to ask directly, in the first session, what would have to be true for the tutor to recommend changing subject. A tutor who has a real answer, naming the signs she would look for, is giving you advice. A tutor who says the student will be fine with enough sessions is giving you a quotation. An IB home tutor in Mumbai worth engaging will also tell you plainly when a question belongs with the coordinator rather than with a tutor.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, a predicted score or a promise attached to a fixed number of sessions. No tutor can promise a specific outcome in a subject marked by examiners they will never meet. Be equally wary of advice about a named university's entry requirements, because requirements vary by institution, by country and by course and they change between admission cycles. The only sound answer is to read the specific course page at source and to speak to the school's counsellor, and a tutor who recites a requirement from memory is a tutor to discount.

Session notes are the cheap ongoing check. For a student in the decision phase, useful notes record what was attempted, how long it took and what the tutor concluded about fit. For a student past the decision, notes should name what was practised. Either way, a note that only reports a positive mood is not information, and three of those in a row is reason to ask a direct question.
bullets: Identity verified and qualifications checked against documents
Examining and moderating claims treated as claims until documented
Ask what would make the tutor recommend changing subject
Discount any tutor who quotes a named university's requirements from memory

sections.heading: History, global politics or economics: how do you compare the choices honestly?
paragraphs: Compare them by what the final hours in the examination hall look like, because that is the part nobody pictures when choosing in a classroom. History ends in extended handwritten argument with a source-based paper attached. Economics ends in a mixture of written response, diagram work and quantitative handling, so a student who dislikes numbers but writes well often finds economics harder than she expected and a student who dislikes extended prose finds it easier. Global politics ends in written response built around contemporary cases, with an engagement component that asks the student to work on a political issue in a sustained way, which suits a student who follows current affairs and bores one who does not. Geography is assessed as a social science with its own quantitative and model-based demands, and it has its own page here rather than a paragraph.

The second comparison is weekly load rather than examination format. Essay subjects stack badly. A grid with History, English Literature and a language all taken at a demanding level produces weeks in the final year where four extended pieces are due together, and the student who copes is usually the one whose remaining subjects are quick to revise rather than the one who is cleverest. Ask the student to map her own six subjects against the months of her final year and see which fortnights collapse. This exercise changes more minds than any description of a syllabus.

The third is honest self-knowledge about reading. History demands reading for position rather than for information: noticing that two accounts of the same event disagree, working out why, and treating that disagreement as the interesting part. Students who find that intriguing do well and often enjoy the subject more as it gets harder. Students who want the answer find two years of it tiring. There is no diplomatic way to establish which kind of student you have other than to try it, which is why a short piece of real work beats a long conversation about interests.

Where the comparison usually lands is less dramatic than families fear. Most students who ask the question should continue with History and should change how they work, not what they study. A minority should change, and they are almost always identifiable in the first term by one pattern: they can discuss the material fluently and produce very little on paper, and the gap is not closing with practice. IB DP History private classes in Mumbai booked at that point are worth more as a diagnosis than as a term of teaching, and a good tutor will say so out loud instead of quietly booking twelve weeks.
bullets: Compare subjects by what the examination hall actually demands, not by topic interest
Essay-heavy subjects stack into the same fortnights in the final year
Map all six subjects against the final year calendar before deciding
History rewards reading for disagreement rather than for information
Most students who ask should change method rather than subject

sections.heading: What four weeks, one term and one exam cycle should actually change
paragraphs: Four weeks should end the uncertainty rather than the difficulty. If the question was whether to continue, you should have a clear recommendation, the coordinator's deadline in hand and a decision made. If the student is continuing, four weeks should produce a measurable change in written output: a longer piece completed inside the same time, or a structure the student can reproduce without prompting. What four weeks will not produce is a transformed essay mark, and anyone suggesting otherwise is describing something that does not occur in a subject assessed on judgement.

One term should show the writing load becoming routine. The student should be finishing timed pieces rather than abandoning them, and she should be able to say what a question is asking before she starts answering it. Parents frequently ask who the best IB tutor in Mumbai is for History, and the useful reframing is to ask which tutor got the diagnosis right in the first fortnight, because a tutor who correctly identifies that the problem is written production rather than knowledge will outperform a more decorated tutor who keeps teaching content.

One exam cycle, from mocks to the real session, should leave the student sitting papers that reflect what she knows. Some students jump considerably. Others consolidate, which is the point when the earlier problem was abandoning answers halfway. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. No tutor controls which questions appear, how a particular examiner reads a script, or how a student sleeps the night before.

The thing to insist on throughout is that the plan visibly changes. An IB tutor Mumbai families keep across both Diploma Programme years is almost always one who revised their own approach when the first version stopped producing results. If notes in week ten name the same difficulty as notes in week two with nothing new attempted, ask for a different approach or a different tutor. Requesting a replacement is routine, the student's work and notes transfer, and the new tutor starts from where the last one reached rather than from the beginning. A home tutor who takes that request badly is telling you something useful about the next twelve months.
bullets: Four weeks: the decision resolved, or written output measurably up
One term: timed pieces finished and questions correctly interpreted
One exam cycle: papers that reflect what the student actually knows
A correct first-fortnight diagnosis matters more than a decorated profile

sections.heading: Booking an IB DP History private tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Four things make the first session worth the money, and you already have all of them. The student's full six-subject grid with levels. Her last school report and any marked History work. The coordinator's change deadline, if the choice is still open. And a straight answer from the student on whether she picked History because she wanted it or because something else did not fit the timetable.

The first session is a diagnosis, not a lesson. Expect a short piece of real written work produced in front of the tutor, a conversation about what the student reads and why, and a plain verdict: continue and work on written production, continue at a different level, or speak to the coordinator this week. You should be told which of those you are getting, in those words, before anything weekly is discussed.

If the answer is to continue, the arrangement gets set up at the same session: the weekly slot, whether the term starts as home tuition or hybrid, how a missed session is rescheduled and what the notes will contain. If the answer is to change subject, that is where the engagement ends, and it should.

Send the school, the year group, the level under consideration and one piece of the student's writing. You will be matched with two or three History specialists who cover your school's prescribed subject and can reach your zone on a weekday evening, and you choose after meeting one of them.
bullets: Have the six-subject grid, a report and one piece of written work ready
Ask the coordinator for the change deadline before the first session
First session ends with a plain verdict on fit, in those words
Weekly slot, reschedule rule and note format agreed only after that

faqs.question: Our daughter loves reading history. Is that enough reason to choose it?
faqs.answer: It is a good sign and not sufficient on its own. The course marks argument produced under time, so the relevant test is not how much she enjoys reading about the past but whether she enjoys taking a position, defending it with specific evidence and dealing with the strongest objection to it. Students who read for narrative and students who read for argument look identical in conversation and perform very differently in the examination hall. Have her write one full timed essay on something she has already studied, then ask whether she would do that most weeks for two years.

faqs.question: Can a private tutor travel to our society in Kharghar for an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the slot set honestly. Navi Mumbai is matched node to node, so a tutor based in Kharghar, Belapur or Panvel is the realistic option for a weekday evening, and a tutor crossing from the island city will arrive late often enough that the arrangement fails by the second month. Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway make the node hops quick off-peak. Society gate protocol is worth settling in week one: most complexes want the tutor added as a recurring visitor, which takes one call from the flat owner and saves an argument every week.

faqs.question: Should we book home tuition before the subject choice is final?
faqs.answer: Yes, and book it as a review rather than as a term. One or two sessions framed explicitly as a fit diagnosis cost far less than discovering the problem at the mock exams, and they give you something the school cannot easily give: an outside reading of the student's written production against what the subject will demand. Ask for a tutor comfortable saying the student should change subject. If the verdict is to continue, the same tutor can usually carry on. If it is to change, you have saved eighteen months.

faqs.question: What does an IB History private tutor charge in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: No single rate exists, and a quote offered before anyone has seen the request is a guess. IB tuition fees in Mumbai move with the level, since Higher Level work on a specific regional option needs a narrower specialist than Standard Level; with how scarce that specialism is; with travel distance and the hour, because a tutor crossing a zone in the evening peak gives up another booking; with session length and frequency; and with whether the arrangement is home, online or hybrid. A short diagnostic consultation is priced differently from ongoing weekly teaching. Ask against your actual zone and slot.

faqs.question: Can our son switch from History to another subject partway through the first year?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the deadline is your school's rather than a general one. Most schools keep changes open during the opening weeks of Diploma Programme year one while timetables are still movable, then close the window when candidate registration is submitted. Ask the coordinator for the actual date in writing this week rather than relying on what classmates say. Timetable blocking also constrains the options, so the subject he wants may not be available in his slot even inside the window. The sooner the question is asked, the more choices remain.

faqs.question: Does taking History at Higher Level help with university applications?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the institution and the course, and nobody should tell you otherwise from memory. Entry requirements vary by university, by country and by individual programme, and they are revised between admission cycles, so the only reliable sources are the specific course page published by that institution and your school's university counsellor. What can be said generally is that History develops extended written argument and source handling, which some degree courses value. Treat any tutor who states a named university's requirement as a tutor who is guessing, and verify everything at source before the subject grid is locked.

faqs.question: He speaks confidently in class but writes slowly. Is History a mistake for him?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but it is a subject that will expose the gap rather than hide it. Spoken fluency and written production are separate skills, and teachers often read strong classroom discussion as evidence the writing will follow, which does not reliably happen. If his reasoning out loud is genuinely good, History can suit him well, on one condition: written output is treated as its own project from the first term, with timed writing practised weekly, rather than being discovered when the mock results arrive. If nobody is willing to do that work, a less writing-intensive subject is the kinder choice.

faqs.question: What happens to the historical investigation if she changes subject now?
faqs.answer: It is lost, because the internal assessment belongs to the subject rather than to the student. The practical question is how much has genuinely been done. A few weeks of preliminary reading and a provisional question is a small cost. A substantially drafted piece is a real one, and that is the reason the fit conversation belongs in the first term. Students routinely overestimate how advanced their investigation is, so get a tutor or the subject teacher to say plainly what stage it has reached before the switch is weighed up.

faqs.question: Do you cover Mulund and Vikhroli for weekday home sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Eastern Suburbs from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup up to Mulund are served by tutors based along the Central and Harbour lines, and matching stays within that corridor wherever the subject specialism allows. The Eastern Express Highway carries most of the movement, the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road connects across to the western side and both are slow in the evening peak. Mulund tutors sometimes cross into Thane and the reverse happens less often. Fix the slot around the highway rather than around the school bell.

faqs.question: What if the tutor turns out to be the wrong fit?
faqs.answer: Ask for a different match, which is a routine request rather than a complaint. The common causes are specific: the tutor knew the prescribed subject but not the regional option the school teaches, or kept delivering content when the difficulty was written production, or the student will not talk honestly in front of her. Name what was missing, because the replacement is then matched against that rather than chosen at random. The student's written work and the session notes transfer, so the next tutor resumes instead of restarting from the beginning.

faqs.question: Will a tutor tell us honestly if our child should drop the subject?
faqs.answer: A good one will, and you should test for it rather than assume it. An IB DP History private tutor in Mumbai paid by the week has an obvious incentive to recommend continuing, so ask directly what would have to be true for them to advise a change, and listen for a specific answer about signs they would look for. No honest tutor will offer a guaranteed grade or a promised outcome as part of that conversation. Where a question is really about registration, timetable blocks or deadlines, the tutor should send you to the Diploma Programme coordinator rather than answering it.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB DP History tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: Most parents open with the report card. We would rather see the last essay your child wrote with a teacher's comments still on it, because a grade tells us almost nothing and a marked essay tells us nearly everything. A 4 in History can mean a student who writes fluently and never states a position. It can mean a student who has a position and cannot find evidence to defend it. It can mean a student who understood the question perfectly and ran out of time with two paragraphs still in their head. Those are three different problems, they need three different kinds of teaching, and no amount of conversation about attitude or effort will tell them apart. So the first thing we ask for is paper.

From there the match gets practical. We note whether your child is in year one or year two of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), whether they are taking Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), which regional option and which prescribed topics their school has chosen, and where in Mumbai you actually live. Subject scarcity is real here. This city has many more Diploma Programme Maths and Physics tutors than History ones, so the pool is smaller and geography bites harder. A parent in Malad who insists on a tutor from Colaba will wait weeks; a parent willing to look along their own railway line usually has names within a day or two. Some parents type the whole thing into a search box: History IB Diploma Programme (DP), Years 1-2 tutor Mumbai, and what they mean by it is somebody who has taught both years of the course rather than a graduate who merely knows the period. Another version of the same search is IB tutors near me Mumbai, which returns everyone within a postcode and tells you nothing about who has marked an essay against the criteria.

You then get two or three profiles. Each one states what that person has genuinely taught or examined rather than a vague humanities background, which subjects they cover at Higher Level, whether they prefer to come to the flat or work on screen, and which evenings they can actually hold for a full term. A History tutor in Mumbai who can only do alternate Saturdays is not a match for a year two student, however good they are, and we would rather say that than send the profile.

The first session is paid and it is a diagnostic, not a sales call. The tutor reads the marked work in advance, asks your child to talk one argument through out loud, and usually sets twenty-five minutes of timed writing on a question nobody has prepared. That is uncomfortable, and it is the point. By the end you should hold a written plan naming the two things to fix first, in that order, with a stated reason for the order. If no such plan arrives, say so in week one rather than week six.

2. Attach the last marked History essay or mock paper with the teacher comments left on.

4. A paid diagnostic session ends with a written two-item plan you keep.

sections.heading: Where History sits in the IB Diploma Programme
paragraphs: History is one of the choices in the individuals and societies group of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP), which students take alongside five other subjects plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and creativity, activity, service. Three subjects are usually taken at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL). The broad difference in History is depth and breadth rather than difficulty of individual tasks: Higher Level adds a further externally assessed component drawn from a regional option, so an HL student carries more content and more essay practice than an SL classmate studying the same world history topics. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator can confirm exactly which options and prescribed topics your child's cohort is following, and the current subject guide is the only reliable source for the structure of each component.

The two years do not feel the same. Year one is where the content base is laid and where most students write their first genuinely argued essays, usually badly, which is normal and useful. Teachers at this stage are often marking for coverage and effort as much as for argument, so a student can post respectable year one grades on a technique that will not survive year two. That gap is the single most common reason a family in Mumbai starts looking for a History tutor in Mumbai in the first term of year two rather than earlier.

Year two is where everything arrives at once. The internal assessment has to be finished, mocks land in the middle of the winter term, university applications are open, and the Extended Essay is due for students who chose to write theirs in History. A tutor's job at this point is partly triage: deciding what can still be improved in the time left, and saying plainly what cannot. A student twelve weeks from the examination session will not rebuild their knowledge of three prescribed topics from nothing, but they can learn to write a defensible opening paragraph in ninety seconds, and that is worth more marks per hour of work.

Families sometimes ask whether to start in year one at all. Our honest answer is that the cheapest useful intervention is early and light: a fortnightly session in year one that fixes essay structure before bad habits set, rather than weekly emergency work in year two. That is not always what a household can arrange, and a late start is still worth doing, but it is a different job with a different realistic ceiling.

sections.heading: Why does a student who knows the content still lose marks?
paragraphs: Because Diploma Programme History is marked on argument, not on recall. A student who has memorised a narrative will reproduce that narrative in order, and an ordered narrative is a chronology. Chronologies sit in the lower bands however accurate they are. The marks move when the same facts stop being the answer and start being the defence of a claim the student has already made.

This is the hardest thing for a diligent child to accept, and it is why History produces more frustrated high-effort students than almost any other Diploma Programme subject. Flashcards work in Biology. In History, a student can hold three hundred dates and still write a paragraph that no examiner can mark favourably, because the paragraph narrates instead of arguing. Meanwhile a classmate who knows half as much writes a tighter essay and scores higher. Parents read that as unfairness. It is not unfairness, it is the subject behaving exactly as its criteria say it will, and a History tutor in Mumbai who cannot explain that distinction in the first hour is the wrong tutor.

The components each test a different face of the same skill. The source paper puts documents in front of a student who has not seen them before and asks what each one is, who made it, for whom, and what that origin and purpose make it worth and also what it limits. Then it asks for two sources to be set against each other, and finally for sources and the student's own knowledge to be combined into a short argued response. That last task is where most marks leak: students either retell the sources or ignore them and write an essay from memory, and both approaches are penalised.

The essay papers work differently. There a student chooses questions across world history topics, and at Higher Level a further paper goes deeper into a regional option. Nothing is handed to them. They must select which examples to use, decide what the question is actually asking, and sustain one line of argument over several paragraphs while a clock runs. The content is the raw material. The mark comes from what is built with it, and that is a teachable skill rather than a talent, which is the useful news in all of this.
bullets: An accurate chronology is still a chronology and still scores in the lower bands
Source work asks what a document is worth and what it cannot tell you
Combining sources with own knowledge is where most students leak marks
Essay papers hand the student nothing: selection of examples is part of the test
Higher Level adds depth through a regional option, not a different kind of thinking

sections.heading: Which Mumbai areas do History tutors cover?
paragraphs: All six zones of Mumbai, Maharashtra: South Mumbai, the Western Suburbs, the Central Suburbs, the Eastern Suburbs, Navi Mumbai and Thane. Coverage is not uniform, though, and a page that pretends otherwise is wasting your time. Demand for an IB DP History tutor in Mumbai is spread fairly evenly across the whole city; supply is not. History is a smaller subject pool than Maths, so in some pockets the honest answer is a strong online tutor plus a monthly visit rather than a weekly one.

In South Mumbai we place home tutors across Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Fort, Peddar Road, Walkeshwar, Babulnath, Tardeo and Worli. Distances look trivial on a map and are not: eight kilometres from Worli to Colaba can still cost forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals on a weekday evening, so we match inside the island rather than pulling someone down from the suburbs. The Coastal Road has helped the north-south run, and Metro Line 3 has changed how a tutor living near Bandra Kurla Complex reaches Cuffe Parade, but a six-thirty start from a suburb remains a promise most tutors cannot keep in December.

The Western Suburbs run as a corridor, and matching along the corridor works where matching across it does not. We cover Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Oshiwara, Andheri West, Versova, Goregaon, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar. The Western Line, the Western Express Highway, Link Road and Metro Lines 2A and 7 define who can realistically reach whom. Khar to Santacruz is nothing; Malad to Bandra at six in the evening is an hour each way and the arrangement collapses by the third week. In the Central Suburbs we work across Powai, Chandivali, Andheri East, Kurla, Ghatkopar and Kanjurmarg, with Powai the awkward case: it is central and has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road along the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road or up from Ghatkopar on Metro Line 1.

The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Wadala and Chembur through Govandi, Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway, which makes South Mumbai far closer to Chembur than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Seawoods, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, linked by Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, with the Atal Setu shortening the run from the island city. Thane spreads from the station east along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali and Hiranandani Estate, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the schedule more than any other road we deal with. Across all of it, the Bandra Worli Sea Link is the one crossing that makes a west-to-south match viable at all.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar a DP History student is working against
paragraphs: Mumbai has an unusually dense cluster of schools offering the Diploma Programme, and their calendars set the pressure points whatever the tutoring arrangement looks like. Families we work with have children at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in Bandra Kurla Complex, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, not endorsed by any of them, and not connected to the International Baccalaureate organisation. We name them because a parent reading this wants to know we understand the calendar their child is on.

Most Mumbai Diploma Programme schools run an academic year that opens as the monsoon arrives and closes in the spring, with the main examination session in May. The rhythm this produces is predictable. The first term is long and unglamorous and is the only stretch of the year with real slack in it. By the time the Diwali break ends the slack has gone, and a family that waits until then to start looking is competing with every other family that waited.

The winter months are where History bites. Year two mocks are usually run in that window, the internal assessment deadline set by the school sits near it, and the Extended Essay final submission is often in the same fortnight for students writing in History. A year two student in Chembur can genuinely be looking at a mock essay paper, an investigation deadline and a Theory of Knowledge essay in the same ten days. A tutor who schedules around that calendar instead of pretending it does not exist is worth considerably more than one who simply books a weekly hour and works through the syllabus in order.

Schools also differ in how much essay feedback a student actually receives, which is nothing to do with teaching quality and everything to do with class size and the number of cohorts a department is carrying. Some students bring us essays covered in annotation. Others bring a single grade and a line of comment. The second kind needs a tutor who will mark properly and slowly, and that changes the shape of the sessions more than the school's name on the gate ever does.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online and hybrid classes for DP History in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default and what most families here ask for first. When a parent asks for an IB home tutor in Mumbai, what they are usually describing is one fixed evening, the same person each week, in the flat. An IB DP History tutor in Mumbai who comes to the flat gets things a screen does not give: the student cannot quietly close a tab, handwritten timed essays happen under genuine observation, and the folder of past essays is physically on the table where it can be spread out and compared. For a child who avoids writing because writing is where the discomfort lives, somebody sitting beside them while the clock runs is worth more than any resource. The History home classes Mumbai families run at the dining table work for exactly this reason: two years of past essays can be spread out side by side and compared. IB home tuition in Mumbai also removes the half-hour of travel at each end for the student, which in year two is a real saving.

The honest cost of home tutoring is scheduling rigidity and travel. A tutor crossing Ghodbunder Road at six-thirty, or coming up the Western Express Highway from Bandra to Kandivali, is buying you a slot with their own evening, and that is reflected in what the slot costs and in how little room there is to move it. If your household needs to shift the time every other week, home classes will fray. Rain is the other factor nobody mentions in July: a monsoon evening in Mumbai can turn a thirty-minute drive into ninety, and an arrangement with no fallback simply loses that session.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai can teach History genuinely well, which is not something we would say about every subject, so we offer it rather than treating it as second best. An essay opened in a shared document and commented on live, with the tutor's remarks appearing next to the student's own sentences, is a genuinely good way to teach argument. It is also how we reach a family in Panvel or Kasarvadavali who wants a specialist in a regional option that three tutors in the city teach. The counterweight is that the examinations are handwritten and timed, so a student who only ever types will be slow on the day.

Hybrid is what most of our year two History families settle into, and it is not a compromise so much as the sensible shape. A home session every week or fortnight for timed handwritten work, marking face to face and the conversations that need a room; an online session in between for essay planning and source discussion, which costs nobody an hour in traffic. Through a mock period the ratio usually tips towards home. Through the long first term it tips the other way.

sections.heading: How are IB DP History tutors in Mumbai checked?
paragraphs: Every IB DP History tutor in Mumbai on the platform is checked on four things before a profile reaches you: identity, qualification, subject-specific teaching record, and references from families or schools they have worked with. We ask what they have taught, at which level, over how long, and we ask them to talk through how they would mark a weak essay. A general humanities graduate who has never worked with Diploma Programme criteria is not the same as somebody who has, and we do not list them as though they were. Whether you describe the arrangement as home tuition or as an IB private tutor Mumbai agencies would call one-to-one, the checks behind the profile are identical.

The subject-specific part matters more in History than in most subjects. Someone can hold an excellent History degree, know a period deeply, and still be unable to teach a sixteen-year-old how to structure a response to a command term, because university History and Diploma Programme History reward different things. So the screening conversation is practical. Show us how you would respond to this paragraph. What would you write in the margin. What would you ask this student to do differently next week.

Then there is what you should check yourself, which no platform can do for you. Ask the tutor directly which prescribed topics and which regional option they have taught, not which ones they could cover. Ask to see how they annotate an essay. Ask what the first four weeks would look like and whether anything is expected between sessions. Ask how they handle the boundary on the internal assessment, where a tutor may teach skills and discuss a draft the student wrote but must never write or rewrite any part of it. A tutor who is vague about that boundary is a risk to your child's diploma, not just to their grade.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, or who quotes a figure for how many points they typically add. Nobody can promise a specific grade in a subject marked by external examiners against published criteria, and the ones who do are usually selling confidence rather than teaching. A good tutor will tell you in the first session what they think is realistically achievable and what it would take, and will revise that view out loud as evidence comes in.

sections.heading: Argument, evidence and historiography: what the marks actually reward
paragraphs: Start with the thesis, because everything else hangs off it. A Diploma Programme History essay needs a claim in its opening paragraph that a reasonable person could disagree with, and then it needs that claim to survive to the end. Most student essays fail one half or the other. Either the opening says what the essay will discuss rather than what it will argue, which gives the examiner nothing to track, or a position is stated and then quietly abandoned by paragraph three as the student drifts into telling the story. We teach this as a mechanical check: read your last sentence, then read your first, and if the two do not speak to each other the essay has not sustained anything.

Command terms are the second thing, and they are not decoration. A question asking to what extent something was the case is demanding a judgement with a degree attached, so an answer that lists factors and stops has not answered it. Evaluate asks for weighing. Compare and contrast asks for a structure that genuinely runs both sides through the same categories, not two separate descriptions bolted together. Discuss asks for a considered range of views and then a position. Students who learn to read the verb before the content, and to write the first sentence of the conclusion before writing the essay, stop producing the particular kind of near-miss essay that reads well and scores four.

Third, evidence has to be deployed rather than listed. The test we give students is simple: for every piece of evidence in a paragraph, can you say in one clause what claim it supports. If the answer is that it is relevant, or that it happened then, the sentence is decoration. Specific, well-chosen detail attached to an explicit claim beats volume every time, and a student who learns this usually writes shorter essays and scores higher, which takes some convincing at home.

Historiography is the part most students handle worst because they are taught it as a shopping list of names. Engaging with how historians disagree does not mean quoting a historian and moving on. It means knowing that an interpretation came out of particular questions, particular available evidence and a particular time, and being able to say why one reading has been challenged. This matters most in exactly the topics where feelings run highest. On the history of India, on Partition, on anything with a religious or communal dimension, the honest position in a Diploma Programme essay is not a verdict delivered with confidence but an account of where serious historians differ, on what grounds, and what evidence each side rests on. A tutor's job there is to show a student how to attribute an interpretation to whoever holds it, to represent a position they disagree with fairly before questioning it, and to keep their own politics out of the room entirely. A student who can do that is doing history. A student who has been handed someone else's conclusions is doing something else, and examiners can tell.

The last piece is pace, and it is the one that catches out strong candidates. History is a writing subject under a clock, and a student who has never written a full essay at speed by hand will discover in the examination hall that knowledge does not convert into words fast enough. Thinking time has to be budgeted, planning has to shrink to a few lines, and the hand has to be conditioned. This is why our tutors set timed handwritten work from early on rather than saving it for mock season, and why a student who types everything needs a deliberate plan to get back onto paper.
bullets: A thesis must be arguable in paragraph one and still standing in the conclusion
Read the command term before the content: to what extent demands a judgement
Every piece of evidence should attach to one explicit claim, or it is decoration
Historiography means explaining why interpretations differ, not naming historians

sections.heading: What progress in History looks like at four weeks and one term
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see structural change and very little else. The opening paragraph starts containing a claim. Paragraphs begin with a point rather than a date. The student can tell you, unprompted, what the question is asking before they start writing. That is the whole of a realistic first month, and parents who were expecting a grade jump are often disappointed by it. They should not be: structure is the thing that moves grades later, and it is the only thing that can genuinely change in four sessions.

By the end of a term the changes are in selection and timing. The student drops examples that do not serve the argument. Essays get a little shorter and considerably denser. Source questions stop being retold. Timed writing begins to finish. Around here a teacher usually notices something before the mark does, and a comment on a returned essay saying the argument is clearer is a better signal than the number next to it.

Across a full examination cycle, movement of a band or two is common for a student who was losing marks to technique rather than to not knowing the course. It is much less common for a student who is genuinely behind on content and started in the final term, and we will say so at the outset rather than take the booking quietly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and neither does any tutor on the platform. External examiners mark against published criteria and we have no influence over that, which is exactly as it should be.

What we can be accountable for is the process: that the tutor turns up, that work is marked properly and returned, that you get a plain account of what is improving and what is not. If a month has gone by with none of that, the problem is the match and not your child. Tell us and we will replace the tutor, carrying over everything the first one recorded so your child does not sit through another diagnostic from scratch. Families also sometimes decide after a term that the sensible next step is fewer sessions rather than more, and we will tell you when we think that is the case.
bullets: Four weeks: structure changes, claims appear in opening paragraphs, grades may not move
One term: sharper selection of evidence, shorter denser essays, timed work finishing
One exam cycle: band movement is common for technique problems, less so for content gaps

sections.heading: Starting with a History home tutor in Mumbai: what to prepare
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful and all of them are already in the house. The most recent marked History essay with the teacher's comments on it. The list of prescribed topics and the regional option the school is teaching, which is usually on the course outline handed out at the start of year one. And a clear-eyed sentence from your child, not from you, about what they find hardest, because a student who says they cannot finish in time needs a different first session from one who says they never know what the question wants.

The session itself runs about the same way whoever the tutor is. Twenty minutes reading and discussing the marked essay, with the tutor asking the student to justify choices rather than correcting them. A short piece of timed writing. Then a conversation about what the two of them saw. It ends with the tutor writing down two priorities and what the next three sessions will do about them, which you should receive in writing. You are entitled to read that plan and to ask why those two and not others.

Practicalities are worth fixing in the same conversation rather than discovering later. Where the work will happen, and whether that room is actually quiet at seven in the evening. Which day holds for the whole term, including through mock season. What happens when a session is missed by either side. Whether a parent wants to be in the room, which for a sixteen-year-old is usually better answered no, and whether a short written note after each session is expected.

Then send us the request. Tell us the area, the year, Higher Level or Standard Level, and two or three times that genuinely work, and we will come back with names rather than a brochure. A home tutor for History Mumbai families can hold for a full year two is a scarce thing in some neighbourhoods, and we would rather tell you that on day one, with an online or hybrid alternative on the table, than keep you waiting politely for a fortnight.

Expect a timed piece of writing in session one, not a syllabus overview

Ask for the written two-priority plan if it has not arrived by the end of the week

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Bandra West for a weekday evening History slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, Bandra West is one of the easier parts of Mumbai to staff for an evening slot. The constraint is not whether somebody will come but where they are coming from. A tutor living in Khar West, Santacruz or Juhu reaches Bandra West comfortably at six-thirty; one coming from Malad on the Western Express Highway or across the Bandra Worli Sea Link from Worli is buying that slot with an hour of their own evening, and that shows up in both price and reliability. We match along the corridor wherever we can, and if the only strong regional-option specialist is further away we will suggest a hybrid pattern instead.

faqs.question: What should we have ready at home before the first home tuition session?
faqs.answer: A table, a quiet hour and the last marked essay. History home tuition needs less equipment than almost any other subject and more silence than most: the student will be writing under time, which is impossible with a television in the next room. Beyond that, have the course outline listing the prescribed topics and regional option, any returned mock papers, and a printer if you have one, since source papers are much easier to annotate on paper. No textbook purchase is needed before the first session, and a tutor who asks you to buy a set of books before meeting your child is worth questioning.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a society gate pass to come to our building every week?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is worth sorting out in the first week rather than at the gate on session two. Most Mumbai societies will issue a standing visitor entry for a regular tutor if a resident registers them, and some larger complexes in Powai, Kharghar or Hiranandani Estate want identity details filed in advance. Tutors on the platform are used to this and carry identification. The practical tip is to put the tutor's name and the fixed weekly time with your security desk at the start of the term, because a tutor held at the gate for fifteen minutes every week will eventually stop taking the slot.

faqs.question: My son has memorised the entire course and still gets a 4. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly he is writing chronology instead of argument. This is the most common pattern we see, and it feels deeply unfair to a hard-working student. Diploma Programme History rewards a claim that is stated early and then defended with selected evidence; a complete, accurate, well-ordered account of what happened does not do that, so it sits in the lower bands however much it contains. The fix is technique, not more content, and it usually shows up in four to six weeks as a structural change before it shows up as a grade. Ask the tutor to mark one essay for argument only, ignoring factual coverage entirely, and the gap becomes visible immediately.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Diploma Programme History usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week is the normal arrangement for an IB DP History tutor in Mumbai, and two is usually only sensible in the run-up to mocks or the final examination session. History improves through written work done between sessions rather than through contact hours, so a student taking two sessions a week and writing nothing in between will progress more slowly than one taking a single session and producing an essay for it. We would rather set up one well-prepared weekly hour with real homework attached than sell a second hour that fills the same time with talk. During mock season many families move temporarily to two, then drop back.

faqs.question: Is History at Standard Level easier than Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It is smaller rather than easier. Standard Level students cover the same source paper and the same kind of world history essay work; Higher Level adds a further externally assessed component drawn from a regional option, which means more content and more essay practice across the two years. The thinking demanded is the same at both levels, so a Standard Level student who writes chronology will struggle exactly as a Higher Level student does. Choose the level on interest and on what the rest of the subject combination looks like, and confirm the current structure with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator rather than with any website.

faqs.question: What does engaging with historiography actually mean for a sixteen-year-old?
faqs.answer: It means being able to explain why historians reached different conclusions, not reciting their names. A student engaging properly can say what questions an interpretation was answering, what evidence was available to the person who made it, and on what grounds other historians have challenged it. That is a manageable skill at sixteen when it is taught as a habit rather than as a list to memorise. On contested subjects, including much of the history of India and Partition, the expectation is that a student represents a disagreement accurately and attributes each position to whoever holds it, rather than delivering a verdict. A good tutor models that and keeps their own views out of it.

faqs.question: We live in Kharghar and my daughter studies in Bandra Kurla Complex. Who can you match?
faqs.answer: Someone in Navi Mumbai, almost certainly, because the match follows the home and not the school. Kharghar sits comfortably within the Navi Mumbai node network alongside Belapur, Nerul and Panvel, and a tutor from those nodes reaches you on Palm Beach Road or the Sion Panvel Highway in a sensible amount of time. A tutor based near the school in Bandra Kurla Complex would be crossing the Atal Setu or the creek at exactly the wrong hour, and that arrangement rarely survives a full term. Where a Navi Mumbai specialist in the right regional option is not available, online is the better answer than a heroic commute.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a subject like History?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not quote a number because any figure would be invented. Level is the first: Higher Level work and year two work cost more than Standard Level or year one. Subject scarcity is the second, and History sits on the scarce side of the Mumbai market compared with Maths or Economics. Travel is the third, which is why a tutor crossing Ghodbunder Road at six in the evening prices differently from one walking across Khar West. Session length and frequency are the fourth and fifth. Ask any tutor to state their rate, their travel expectation and their cancellation rule in writing before the second session.

faqs.question: The tutor is good but there is no improvement after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Say so, this week. A month is long enough to judge direction even though it is not long enough to judge outcome, and the honest question is whether anything structural has changed in the writing. If the opening paragraphs still have no claim in them and the student still cannot say what a command term is asking for, the teaching is not landing, whatever the sessions feel like. Sometimes the fix is a different approach from the same tutor, which we will ask for first. Sometimes it is a different person. A replacement inherits the diagnostic notes and the marked work, so your child does not start again from the beginning.

faqs.question: Will a tutor promise my child a 7?
faqs.answer: No, and you should treat it as a warning sign if one does. External examiners mark Diploma Programme History against published criteria, and no tutor and no platform has any influence over that process, so a promise of a specific grade is a promise about something the person making it does not control. What a serious tutor will give you instead is a realistic assessment after seeing the work, a statement of what would need to change, and a revised view as evidence comes in. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. We are accountable for the quality and consistency of the teaching, and that is the honest limit of it.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram match an IB DP home tutor in Mumbai for Theory of Knowledge?
paragraphs: IB Gram matches a Theory of Knowledge tutor from three inputs: the prescribed title your child has chosen, the exhibition prompt and objects they have drafted, and the two subjects they take at Higher Level. Those three decide the shortlist. A tutor who reads the title and immediately asks which knowledge question is buried inside it is the person you want in the room on a Tuesday evening.

Parents who ask for an IB DP home tutor in Mumbai usually describe a subject problem, because that is the language schools use on a report. TOK does not behave like a subject problem. A profile listing all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers, meaning the International General Certificate of Secondary Education as well as the IB, tells you nothing about whether that person can mark an essay against the published assessment instrument. So the request form asks for the title text, the submission month and whether the exhibition has been uploaded, and those three answers filter the pool before anybody is suggested.

The shortlist comes back describing the areas of knowledge each tutor has actually taught, not a list of boards. If your child's title points at history and the arts, a tutor whose TOK teaching has been built on the natural sciences will pull the essay towards examples they are comfortable with, which is precisely how a prescribed title gets answered sideways. Matching on area of knowledge rather than on seniority is the one decision that changes the result here.

You then speak to the shortlist yourself. Ask each person to read the title aloud and say what the second half of it is doing, and the conversation sorts itself out inside ten minutes. IB Gram does not sit in that call and nobody is booked until you have had it, which is also why the shortlist is deliberately short.

2. Say whether the TOK exhibition is drafted, uploaded or not yet started.
